e0OWlyS0Hr.method: In training, VGGT features of the reference views condition denoising and VGGT features of the ground-truth target view supervise intermediate representations; at inference, dual-condition guidance strengthens the contributions of the reference views and the target-view rendering. It refines renderings at arbitrary requested poses without predefined trajectories.
e0OWlyS0Hr.key_idea: Condition the denoiser on reference-view VGGT features and align intermediate features to target-view VGGT features, then apply dual-condition guidance at inference.
e0OWlyS0Hr.evidence: Comparisons with strong baselines on identical renderings from 2DGS and FSGS in 3-input-view settings; trained only on 2DGS renderings (the rest is cut off, and reviewers note 300 DL3DV-10K training scenes and transfer to 3DGS and FSGS).
e0OWlyS0Hr.claimed_gains: In 3-input-view settings it runs 6.9x faster end-to-end with comparable PSNR using 2DGS, and 3.7x faster with higher PSNR using FSGS, than cycle-based refinement.
e0OWlyS0Hr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it gives a practical quality-efficiency tradeoff by avoiding repeated reconstruction-generation cycles, with broad evaluation across datasets, reconstruction methods, and input-view counts and informative placement ablations.
e0OWlyS0Hr.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited novelty and weak control: feature injection, alignment, and classifier-free guidance are established techniques, and the comparisons to DIFIX and to GSFixer's standalone restorer do not isolate the source of the gain.

zaZbwEqMCo.one_liner: Online monocular Gaussian-splatting reconstruction for UAV streams with multi-view depth reassessment, balanced Gaussian expansion, and tangential-radial position updates.
zaZbwEqMCo.problem: Aerial 3D Gaussian Splatting methods are mostly offline, while online UAV reconstruction must work from incomplete observations over wide depth ranges and uneven multi-view evidence within a limited optimization budget.
zaZbwEqMCo.method: OUR-GS adapts Gaussian map construction and refinement to viewing distance and available multi-view evidence through multi-view depth reassessment (MDR), balanced Gaussian map expansion (BGME), and tangential-radial decomposed position updates (TRDU).
zaZbwEqMCo.key_idea: Adapt depth correction, Gaussian allocation, and position updates to viewing distance and multi-view evidence, with position updates decomposed into tangential and radial components.
zaZbwEqMCo.evidence: Experiments on five outdoor UAV datasets with ablation studies; the end of the abstract is cut off.
zaZbwEqMCo.claimed_gains: Consistently improves reconstruction quality over existing methods, especially on forward-facing large-scale sequences, with the lowest GPU memory requirement; the abstract gives no numbers (a reviewer cites 0.85-6.65 dB over MODP).
zaZbwEqMCo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method gives consistent rendering-quality gains across five UAV datasets with the lowest GPU memory, and that the three components are reasonably motivated.
zaZbwEqMCo.main_concern: Reviewers cite thin evidence for the geometric claims: no direct quantitative geometric-accuracy evaluation (only PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS), component ablations that are qualitative or limited to one dataset, and little analysis against prior online UAV Gaussian methods such as OUSA-GS.

KMZBYN8Dn8.one_liner: Represents each agent skill as aligned actor guidance and evaluator rubric, co-evolved alternately, with verifier rewards on responsible turns.
KMZBYN8Dn8.problem: Skill-based multimodal agent training relies on sparse outcome rewards with little supervision for intermediate decisions, and rubric-based rewards are hard to build at scale and often disconnected from the actor's procedure.
KMZBYN8Dn8.method: Each skill carries actor-facing guidance and an evaluator-facing rubric, and a multimodal verifier checks skill-defined goals from screenshots and tool outputs to assign completion and progress rewards to responsible turns. Guidance revisions are validated by paired rollouts under a frozen policy, and rubric revisions offline under fixed guidance, in alternation.
KMZBYN8Dn8.key_idea: One skill yields both how-to-act guidance and a what-success-looks-like rubric, updated in alternation so each revision is validated with the other held fixed.
KMZBYN8Dn8.evidence: Diverse multimodal agent benchmarks (eight per a reviewer) with two trained backbones, plus controlled paired rollouts comparing evolved skills with their predecessors.
KMZBYN8Dn8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using the same procedural knowledge for action guidance and process evaluation is a useful design, with consistent gains over the strongest skill-based baseline across benchmarks.
KMZBYN8Dn8.main_concern: Reviewers say the shared-source alignment claim and the reliability of intermediate process credit are not directly isolated, and that the advance is incremental relative to SkillRL, step-wise rubric rewards, and rubric-agent co-evolution work.

ANLRqccMSL.one_liner: Offline RL for flow-matching policies using soft-value gradients from fixed behavior-process continuations, avoiding trajectory backpropagation and actor-action critic queries.
ANLRqccMSL.problem: Improving flow-matching policies with a learned critic in offline RL is unstable when backpropagating through multi-step sampling, and critic queries on actor-generated actions expose the policy to out-of-distribution value errors.
ANLRqccMSL.method: SVFM samples stochastic continuations of a fixed behavior process from noised data actions, evaluates the critic at their endpoints, and uses a log-mean-exp of these values as a Monte Carlo target for a soft-value network whose gradient guides actor updates. An adaptive temperature scales with the spread of critic values across continuations.
ANLRqccMSL.key_idea: Train a soft-value network on log-mean-exp critic values at endpoints of behavior-process continuations and use its gradient to guide the actor for KL-regularized improvement.
ANLRqccMSL.evidence: OGBench, LIBERO, and LIBERO-Plus benchmarks, plus real-world manipulation with both task-specific flow policies and a pretrained VLA model.
ANLRqccMSL.claimed_gains: not stated (only qualitative: higher average success rates than the compared baselines on OGBench, LIBERO, and LIBERO-Plus)
ANLRqccMSL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem and approach are clearly defined, that fixed behavior continuations keep guidance queries independent of the current actor, and that results on OGBench, LIBERO, and real-world manipulation are promising.
ANLRqccMSL.main_concern: Reviewers cite computational cost: each soft-value update needs K=8 SDE-sampled continuations, and one reviewer reports about twice the training runtime and slower inference than Q-Flow and QAM, which undercuts the claimed savings over backpropagation through time.

ZqUD1PVF8Q.one_liner: Learns designer-style Bezier anchor placement through a sparse anchor field and decoder to guide boundary-constrained curve fitting from raster.
ZqUD1PVF8Q.problem: Raster appearance alone does not determine where to place anchors when dividing a contour into Bezier segments, and vectorizers that optimize only pixel error give control layouts that are not compact for editing.
ZqUD1PVF8Q.method: A sparse anchor field learned from designer-authored SVGs jointly encodes contour geometry and segment junctions, and an anchor decoder predicts explicit anchor proposals from features learned under field supervision. These proposals guide boundary-constrained fitting and local refinement to recover cubic Bezier paths.
ZqUD1PVF8Q.key_idea: Learn where designers put segment junctions, including on smooth contours, as a sparse anchor field, and use the predicted anchors to seed Bezier fitting.
ZqUD1PVF8Q.evidence: Clean single-path inputs, boundary perturbations, a component-based full-image pipeline, and a user study on local editing.
ZqUD1PVF8Q.claimed_gains: On clean single-path inputs, 99.52% mean IoU while using 56.6% fewer anchors on average than AdaVec, with lower boundary error and closer agreement with source-SVG anchor layouts.
ZqUD1PVF8Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well chosen and that matched-count and shared-backend ablations show learned anchor placement beats uniform and error-greedy placement, with compact anchors and a favorable fidelity-compactness balance.
ZqUD1PVF8Q.main_concern: Reviewers cite thin evidence for the field and decoder components and modest margins: clean-path fidelity is already saturated (AutoTrace reaches 98.073% IoU), field-peak readout matches the decoder in Table 3, the method is slower, and prior work is missing.

QKhTbRF4Wx.one_liner: Embodied MLLM agent whose skills are finite-state machines of task-progress states and transitions, co-evolved with state-conditioned GRPO.
QKhTbRF4Wx.problem: Embodied agents need reusable, transferable behavioral patterns as skills whose context stays compact and stage-relevant while adjusting dynamically as the task progresses.
QKhTbRF4Wx.method: StateSkill models interaction experience as a finite-state machine with task-progress states, transitions, and state-conditioned guidance; StateSkill-Evolve refines it from successful and failed state-guided trajectories, and StateGRPO alternates skill evolution with state-conditioned GRPO optimization so skills and model co-evolve.
QKhTbRF4Wx.key_idea: Organize a skill as a finite-state machine of task-progress states, transition gates, and per-state guidance, revised iteratively from trajectories and co-trained with GRPO.
QKhTbRF4Wx.evidence: Experiments across various embodied tasks (details cut off); reviewers cite LIBERO-PRO and RoboCasa with same-knowledge ablations.
QKhTbRF4Wx.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract (a reviewer cites LIBERO-PRO success rising from 25.8% to 68.4% with Qwen3.5-9B and no policy fine-tuning).
QKhTbRF4Wx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the state-structured execution gives substantial practical gains, with same-knowledge ablations isolating the benefits of state-conditioned guidance, transition gates, and action priors.
QKhTbRF4Wx.main_concern: Reviewers say generalization and co-evolution claims are not isolated: task splits across skill construction, evolution, and RL training are unclear, and there is no equal-budget comparison against refining skills once and then training with frozen skills.

5gCuH26SmE.one_liner: Combines YOCO decoder-decoder with parameter-shared recursion confined to the shallow efficient-attention self-decoder, keeping a constant global KV cache.
5gCuH26SmE.problem: Standard Transformers scale inference-time compute inefficiently, since conventional looping strategies carry high computational overhead and a KV cache that grows with model depth.
5gCuH26SmE.method: Universal YOCO (YOCO-U) uses a Universal Self-Decoder that performs multiple iterations through parameter sharing, confined to the shallow, efficient-attention layers of the YOCO architecture, which supplies a constant global KV cache and linear pre-filling.
5gCuH26SmE.key_idea: Loop only YOCO's shallow efficient-attention self-decoder with shared parameters, so effective depth grows without regenerating per-layer KV caches or rerunning global attention.
5gCuH26SmE.evidence: General and long-context benchmarks, with reviewers noting comparisons to YOCO and RINS, equal-FLOP results, and serving measurements from a vLLM-style engine.
5gCuH26SmE.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract (only qualitative: remains highly competitive on general and long-context benchmarks; a reviewer cites a 4.45-percentage-point average gain over YOCO at equal FLOPs).
5gCuH26SmE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the design is simple and well motivated, that confining recursion to the shallow self-decoder preserves YOCO's cache and linear pre-fill, and that the quality-efficiency tradeoff is useful with sound ablations.
5gCuH26SmE.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited novelty and thin evidence: it combines existing looped-transformer ideas (Universal Transformer, RINS, Mixture-of-Recursions), fixes the loop count rather than showing test-time scaling, overstates headline efficiency numbers, and rests on small gains with one seed.

xkSJKCAw1J.one_liner: Uses continuous-symmetry equivariant layers whose Goldstone-like modes carry signals across depth and recurrent iterations without residuals or normalization.
xkSJKCAw1J.problem: Deep and recurrent networks need stable information flow across depth and time, which is usually obtained from architectural stabilizers such as residual connections or normalization.
xkSJKCAw1J.method: The paper studies networks whose internal layers are equivariant under a continuous symmetry (U(1) and O(4) per the reviews), which can support Goldstone-like degrees of freedom, and analyzes signal propagation analytically and empirically in feedforward networks, RNNs, and GRUs.
xkSJKCAw1J.key_idea: Equivariance under a continuous symmetry protects a propagating degree of freedom (a Goldstone-like mode) that keeps signals and gradients coherent over depth and recurrent steps.
xkSJKCAw1J.evidence: Analytic derivations and experiments on trainability in deep feedforward networks and on long-sequence tasks for RNNs and GRUs; reviewers cite 100-layer Fashion-MNIST, delay-copy, and permuted-MNIST.
xkSJKCAw1J.claimed_gains: not stated (only qualitative: improved trainability, representational diversity, and long-sequence performance)
xkSJKCAw1J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using symmetry and physics-inspired propagation for information flow is interesting, with theory on gradient rank and non-vanishing properties and experiments, including controls, consistent with the analysis.
xkSJKCAw1J.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited practical relevance and rigor: the analysis centers on U(1)-equivariant networks that most architectures are not, controls are unstabilized baselines only, and the Goldstone-mode definition is not closed-form.

AlPtNEYCnw.one_liner: Distills a teacher-forced AR video model into a few-step student on-policy, with AR real and fake score models.
AlPtNEYCnw.problem: Recent autoregressive video generators depend on a separate bidirectional teacher for few-step distillation, which limits AR training as a native foundation for the whole generation pipeline.
AlPtNEYCnw.method: Teacher-forcing AR diffusion training yields a many-step AR generator, which On-Policy Forcing distills into a few-step student while preserving the causal factorization, using AR models for both real and fake score estimation so both are conditioned on clean student-generated history.
AlPtNEYCnw.key_idea: Use causal AR models for both real and fake scores during on-policy distribution-matching distillation, so both condition on clean student-generated history instead of a bidirectional teacher.
AlPtNEYCnw.evidence: VBench evaluation of a four-step student distilled with 1.3B AR score models against Self Forcing and Causal Forcing, plus 2x2 real/fake-score conditioning controls at equal training budget.
AlPtNEYCnw.claimed_gains: The four-step student reaches 84.08 Total on VBench, 0.86 and 0.79 points above Self Forcing and Causal Forcing distilled with 1.3B bidirectional score models, and improves Dynamic Degree by 28.33 points over the controlled bidirectional real/fake configuration at equal training budget.
AlPtNEYCnw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the 2x2 real/fake conditioning study cleanly shows that mismatched conditioning breaks DMD-style distillation, and that the clean-prefix, causally conditioned teacher design is clear and reproducible.
AlPtNEYCnw.main_concern: Reviewers say the gain is not cleanly attributed: it mixes clean-prefix conditioning with removal of future context and extra AR training data, and the recipe resembles existing work (CausalCine), so the contribution is mostly a controlled analysis.

WhjzanUYiV.one_liner: Self-supervised 3D scene learning on a Volume Transformer, with decoupled teacher-student views, leak-free masked prediction, and cluster-based 2D distillation.
WhjzanUYiV.problem: Self-supervised representation learning for 3D scenes has not matched 2D success, with limitations in current teacher-student designs such as inconsistent targets, leakage from masked geometry, and direct regression of 2D image features.
WhjzanUYiV.method: VINO swaps the hierarchical PTv3 backbone for a Volume Transformer (a ViT-like 3D architecture), gives the teacher clean targets and the student stronger perturbations, and hides masked geometry from the student so it infers missing representations from visible context. It distills 2D knowledge through view-consistent cluster assignments in frozen 2D feature space rather than regressing image features.
WhjzanUYiV.key_idea: Separate teacher and student roles, block student access to masked geometry, and distill from view-consistent cluster assignments of frozen 2D features instead of regressing them.
WhjzanUYiV.evidence: Dense linear probing across indoor and outdoor benchmarks and out-of-domain transfer, with step-by-step ablations on ScanNet200 against Sonata per the reviews.
WhjzanUYiV.claimed_gains: not stated (only qualitative: substantially improves dense linear probing across indoor and outdoor benchmarks and transfers strongly out of domain)
WhjzanUYiV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the redesign is well motivated, addresses concrete sources of information leakage and inconsistent supervision, and achieves strong results across settings, with systematic ablations of design choices.
WhjzanUYiV.main_concern: Reviewers cite attribution and positioning: gains are confounded with the stronger Volume Transformer backbone, ablations change several factors at once, and several design choices resemble prior work (Point-MAE, CrossMAE, AsymDSD).

zy85LVX0E8.one_liner: All-atom RNA structure tokenizer using strictly local autoencoders over nucleotides, dinucleotides, and base pairs, aware of chemical modifications.
zy85LVX0E8.problem: Existing RNA structure tokenizers overlook that base pairs and dinucleotides are central building blocks and that chemical modifications are prevalent.
zy85LVX0E8.method: RNAcoder tokenizes dinucleotides and base pairs alongside single nucleotides, each through a strictly local autoencoder, and handles chemical modifications; its tokens are placed in coarse-grained graphs that represent whole RNA structures for downstream prediction.
zy85LVX0E8.key_idea: Learn separate local all-atom autoencoder tokens for nucleotides, dinucleotides, and base pairs, using a 37-slot atom nomenclature (RNAtom37) that covers modified nucleotides.
zy85LVX0E8.evidence: Downstream small-molecule binding site prediction, RNA-protein interface prediction, and ligand chemical class prediction, plus a check that learned tokens align with Leontis-Westhof base pair families never used in training.
zy85LVX0E8.claimed_gains: not stated (only qualitative: improved performance on three downstream tasks)
zy85LVX0E8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that treating base pairs and dinucleotides as tokens is biologically well motivated and modification-aware, and that ablations show removing the pair tokens hurts all three downstream tasks.
zy85LVX0E8.main_concern: Reviewers cite overstated downstream claims: RNAcoder beats hand-crafted 2.5D graphs but loses to pretrained tokenizers (BiHiTo, RiboSphere) on RNA-Site and RNA-Ligand, and key controls and statistical tests are missing.

S89Rno3C6A.one_liner: Chooses sample weights from both loss and gradient information, since loss-only reweighting can slow convergence or oscillate.
S89Rno3C6A.problem: Loss-only dynamic sample reweighting ignores how emphasizing high-loss samples changes the geometry of the update, and can give an arbitrarily worse local convergence rate than uniform-weight gradient descent or a stable two-cycle at larger step sizes.
S89Rno3C6A.method: Geometry-Aware Reweighting (GAR) chooses weights from both loss and gradient information; for minibatch SGD it satisfies the uniform-weight SGD upper bound minus an explicit nonnegative term, and it is extended to momentum and AdamW.
S89Rno3C6A.key_idea: Select per-sample weights using loss and gradient geometry jointly, so the weighted update improves on uniform SGD's bound instead of distorting the step direction.
S89Rno3C6A.evidence: Counterexamples on simple strongly convex problems, convergence bounds for minibatch SGD, and experiments on 120M-300M language models against uniform-weight AdamW and loss-based LinUpper.
S89Rno3C6A.claimed_gains: Achieves lower evaluation log-perplexity than both uniform-weight AdamW and the loss-based LinUpper reweighting on 120M-300M language models; no numeric margins are stated.
S89Rno3C6A.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the counterexamples clearly show why loss-based reweighting can hurt optimization and that the method is theoretically motivated under its stated assumptions.
S89Rno3C6A.main_concern: Reviewers cite the gap between theory and practice: the guarantees rely on unobservable loss gaps, the implementation uses last-layer gradients and a few fixed-point iterations, and results lack multiple seeds and compute-cost measurements.

WR7MuVZTH0.one_liner: Sequential RL-routed EEG emotion recognition that picks region, channel, or relation experts, or stops, anchored by a low-order classifier.
WR7MuVZTH0.problem: Useful EEG emotion structure spans channels, regions, and inter-region relations with a scale that varies per recording, while existing static or sample-adaptive graphs build a broad relational representation in one pass before the value of its computations is known.
WR7MuVZTH0.method: A training-fitted low-order anchor supplies initial class logits, then a graph-constrained actor-critic selects a REGION, CHANNEL, RELATION, or STOP action, evaluating only the selected shared expert whose evidence conditions the next decision. A strictly forward accumulator incorporates preceding windows within each trial.
WR7MuVZTH0.key_idea: Treat recognition as sequential evidence acquisition in which an actor-critic picks which hierarchical expert to evaluate next, conditioned on evidence already acquired, and learns when to stop.
WR7MuVZTH0.evidence: Four datasets, a matched three-seed comparison with one-shot top-k and no-RL routing, ablations of the anchor and forward history, and evidence-nulling diagnostics.
WR7MuVZTH0.claimed_gains: 66.81% Accuracy against 65.87% for one-shot top-k and 65.64% for no-RL routing in a matched three-seed evaluation; removing the anchor reduces Accuracy by 7.42 points and forward history contributes 6.06 points.
WR7MuVZTH0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the statistical evaluation is rigorous (subject-level paired tests, bootstrap confidence intervals, Holm correction, released code) and that the appendix controls and interventions let readers check where the gains come from.
WR7MuVZTH0.main_concern: Reviewers say the core RL acquisition contributes little: with no expert called, accuracy already matches or nearly matches the full system, and the gains come mainly from the generic anchor and forward-history components.

uZLZCV3OA6.one_liner: Proves exact softmax attention needs arithmetic circuits of size N^(omega(1,a,1)+o(1)), matching rectangular matrix multiplication.
uZLZCV3OA6.problem: Standard softmax attention forms all query-key scores even when each query yields one scalar, leaving open whether exact attention can avoid the arithmetic complexity of rectangular matrix multiplication.
uZLZCV3OA6.method: The paper proves an exp-log span theorem: modulo additive constants, all within-row score differences lie in the Q-linear span of the circuit's exponential inputs and logarithm outputs. Combined with mixed-coefficient extraction, this recovers the rectangular matrix-multiplication tensor and gives the lower bound.
uZLZCV3OA6.key_idea: An exp-log span theorem places within-row score differences in the rational-linear span of the circuit's exp inputs and log outputs, letting mixed-coefficient extraction recover the matrix-multiplication tensor.
uZLZCV3OA6.evidence: A theoretical proof for N queries and keys of width d=ceil(N^a) with 0<a<=1 in the exact-real circuit model with +, -, x, /, exp, and ln gates; no experiments are mentioned.
uZLZCV3OA6.claimed_gains: The minimum exact-real circuit size is N^(omega(1,a,1)+o(1)), closing the previous single-head gap between omega(1,a,a) and omega(1,a,1), and dense independently parameterized attention needs n(m-1) exp/log gates.
uZLZCV3OA6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question about fundamental limits of exact attention is interesting, the lower bound closes open questions from prior work (Saha et al.), and the techniques are technically deep.
uZLZCV3OA6.main_concern: Reviewers cite presentation: the proof-driven paper is hard to follow, key terms (tensor rank, holomorphic germ) are undefined, and the need for the span theorem and the technical obstacles are not explained.

e5oZuoa5Vq.one_liner: Video diffusion guided by normal maps rendered from generative 3D meshes lifted from one reference image.
e5oZuoa5Vq.problem: Video diffusion models struggle with precise camera and motion control when large viewpoint shifts, changing occlusions, or complex dynamics reveal unseen regions, and warped guidance carries incomplete geometry and misleading view-dependent appearance cues.
e5oZuoa5Vq.method: Generative 3D lifting estimates complete object and human meshes from a single reference image, and normal maps rendered under specified camera trajectories and foreground motions guide the video model while the reference image supplies appearance conditioning. Soft spatial-aligned injection and minimally invasive fine-tuning add the guidance, trained on about 2,000 monocular clips with instance-masked normal sequences and instance-level spatial perturbations.
e5oZuoa5Vq.key_idea: Condition the video model on normals rendered from a coarse, topologically complete 3D cache and on appearance from the reference image, trained with perturbed normals to tolerate imperfect cached geometry.
e5oZuoa5Vq.evidence: Training on around 2,000 monocular clips without explicit 3D assets or paired multi-trajectory recordings; reviewers cite camera, human (PA-MPJPE), and object-control results with ablations, but the abstract is cut off before the results.
e5oZuoa5Vq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that an editable, complete 3D foreground cache with decoupled geometry and appearance conditioning gives practical camera, human, and object control, with substantial reported motion-control gains and useful ablations of the normal-perturbation strategy.
e5oZuoa5Vq.main_concern: Reviewers cite evaluation validity and attribution: RPE is computed between consecutive frames over outputs of 25 to 121 frames, so camera rankings are not comparable, and no controlled test isolates the benefit of complete geometry or separates the method from the closely related Shape-for-Motion.

wcANqDQO12.one_liner: GUI-agent defense: provenance-aware action screening blocks environment-induced harm, then recovery guidance resumes the user's task.
wcANqDQO12.problem: Detect-and-block defenses against untrusted environmental content can cause benign users' legitimate GUI-agent tasks to be abandoned instead of completed.
wcANqDQO12.method: IntentGuard's Blocking module screens actions by provenance to find environment-induced unsafe behavior and stop contaminated context from reaching harmful actions, and its Recovery module generates structured guidance that helps the underlying agent bypass malicious content and resume the intended task without retraining. The authors also introduce EnvGuard-Bench, a 2x2 benchmark over benign or malicious user intent and environmental content.
wcANqDQO12.key_idea: Pair provenance-aware action screening with structured recovery guidance so the agent bypasses malicious environment content and resumes the benign task without retraining.
wcANqDQO12.evidence: Evaluation on EnvGuard-Bench's four settings with emphasis on the benign-user, malicious-environment case, plus ablations of progress assistance and blocking; the abstract is cut off before the results.
wcANqDQO12.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract (a reviewer cites attacked-task SCR rising from 45% to 67% when Blocking is added).
wcANqDQO12.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benign-user, malicious-environment formulation is useful and EnvGuard-Bench's matched 2x2 design fills a real gap, with joint reporting of task completion and safety.
wcANqDQO12.main_concern: Reviewers say the gains are hard to separate from benchmark-provided task information and richer recovery prompts: Progress-only already lifts completion, and baselines lack comparable progress or recovery information.

jMC3j2D1QK.one_liner: Selects RLVR training prompts with non-stationary contextual Thompson Sampling and frontier probes, predicting prompt utility before rollouts.
jMC3j2D1QK.problem: As a model's competence changes during RLVR, the value of each training problem changes, and existing data selection relies on offline profiling, coarse curricula, or filtering after rollouts have already been generated.
jMC3j2D1QK.method: Each training problem is an arm in a non-stationary contextual bandit whose context encodes competence statistics, difficulty, and reasoning-pattern information; Thompson Sampling predicts utility before rollouts, periodically probes low-success problems without policy updates, and uses a composite reward of advantage magnitude, competence-edge membership, and question-space diversity with a sliding-window reward model.
jMC3j2D1QK.key_idea: Treat each prompt as a bandit arm whose utility, tied to its current pass rate through advantage magnitude, is predicted by Thompson Sampling before any rollouts are generated.
jMC3j2D1QK.evidence: Ablations and analyses across multiple model sizes and reasoning tasks per the reviews; the abstract is cut off before the results.
jMC3j2D1QK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it targets a practical RLVR bottleneck by selecting informative prompts before rollouts, and that the non-stationary contextual bandit framing is interesting and evaluated across model sizes with ablations.
jMC3j2D1QK.main_concern: Reviewers cite weak justification of the utility proxy and hand-designed reward: mean absolute advantage does not guarantee learning gains, the composite reward weights are empirical, and design details such as the history window are unclear.

n4tcebRHmB.one_liner: Combines function-preserving rotations with a quantization-noise-aware safe subspace to make W4A4 post-training quantization work for multimodal embedding models.
n4tcebRHmB.problem: Strong PTQ methods stay near full precision at W4A16, W8A16, W4A8 and W8A8 on universal multimodal embedding models but collapse at W4A4, a failure that layer-wise reconstruction error does not explain.
n4tcebRHmB.method: RONA applies function-preserving rotations and reparameterizes weights along a group-aligned, quantization-noise-aware safe subspace, with a per-layer absorption coefficient calibrated against grouped-GPTQ weight reconstructions and query-target embedding geometry while the backbone stays frozen.
n4tcebRHmB.key_idea: Weights are reparameterized along subspace directions that stay safe under activation-quantization noise, with a per-layer coefficient set by embedding-geometry calibration.
n4tcebRHmB.evidence: Evaluated on 78 MMEB-V2 tasks (image, video, visual-document) across three backbones against strong PTQ baselines, with ablations.
n4tcebRHmB.claimed_gains: 73.55 at W4A4, 3.65 points above the strongest PTQ baseline, retaining 94.4% of full precision.
n4tcebRHmB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the retrieval-geometry diagnosis of W4A4 failure and the broad evaluation over 78 MMEB-V2 tasks and three backbones.
n4tcebRHmB.main_concern: Latency, throughput and memory are not measured, and one reviewer finds noise-aware absorption adds only 0.89 points over a 72.66 variant with absorption disabled.

RDfFgjrwFz.one_liner: Benchmark generating videos and reference labels from game records to test event perception, state interpretation and tracking.
RDfFgjrwFz.problem: Existing video benchmarks give limited insight into whether models keep a coherent understanding of an evolving, partially observable world state, and such annotations are hard to obtain from real videos.
RDfFgjrwFz.method: Uses competitive games to generate videos and aligned reference labels at scale, with three task categories (perceiving critical events, interpreting state updates, tracking resulting states), and evaluates a golden set of 180 tasks across 9 games under native and tool-assisted agentic protocols.
RDfFgjrwFz.key_idea: Game records give deterministic ground-truth world state, so videos and verifiable labels can be generated automatically without manual annotation.
RDfFgjrwFz.evidence: A golden set of 180 tasks across 9 games evaluated under native visual understanding and tool-assisted agentic analysis.
RDfFgjrwFz.claimed_gains: The best-performing systems achieve F1 scores of 13.2 and 51.0 under the native and tool-assisted protocols.
RDfFgjrwFz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper clear and well motivated, with controlled game environments a valid route to verifiable video evaluation and a solid automated label pipeline.
RDfFgjrwFz.main_concern: Only 180 tasks across 9 games support the scalability claim, and the native and agentic protocols differ in visual coverage, tool access and budgets.

Xh8FY5LwDg.one_liner: Extracts spatially varying neural materials from images via inverse path tracing initialized and regularized by a feed-forward reconstruction model.
Xh8FY5LwDg.problem: Acquiring and authoring neural materials is hard because their nonlinear latent spaces make naive inverse-rendering optimization infeasible.
Xh8FY5LwDg.method: Trains a Large Material Reconstruction Model (LMRM) that predicts base color, neural material latents and aleatoric uncertainty from images, then runs test-time inverse path tracing from that initialization, anchoring high-confidence regions to the LMRM prediction.
Xh8FY5LwDg.key_idea: Predicted aleatoric uncertainty weights a regularizer that ties confident regions to the feed-forward material prior during test-time inverse path tracing.
Xh8FY5LwDg.evidence: Experiments on synthetic and real assets compared with PBR-based methods, with ablations on material parameterization, LMRM initialization and uncertainty-guided regularization.
Xh8FY5LwDg.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only claims better visual quality and material decomposition than PBR-based methods.
Xh8FY5LwDg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that neural materials capture far more complex appearance than PBR and that LMRM initialization with uncertainty-guided regularization gives strong, well-ablated results.
Xh8FY5LwDg.main_concern: Practicality: the method needs known geometry, camera poses and HDR environment lighting, quality drops with predicted geometry, and test-time optimization takes about 15 minutes per object on an A100.

qCPcEC71m6.one_liner: Graph-structured agentic framework coordinating a main agent and role-specific sub-agents for perception, verification and memory in robot manipulation.
qCPcEC71m6.problem: The paper argues that a single policy is insufficient for long-horizon robot tasks that need planning, perception, verification, failure recovery and memory.
qCPcEC71m6.method: A Main Agent keeps task-level state while Sub Agents handle perception, execution monitoring, verification and memory consolidation in isolated contexts, with Operational, Imagination and Evaluation Skills wrapping heterogeneous backends, plus criterion-grounded verification, textual failure diagnosis and Branch Stack recovery.
qCPcEC71m6.key_idea: Role-specific isolated contexts return only decision-relevant evidence to a main agent, while verification and a Branch Stack provide localized failure recovery.
qCPcEC71m6.evidence: Public benchmarks without additional fine-tuning and real-robot experiments, with ablations across mechanisms and backends.
qCPcEC71m6.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports 'outstanding performance' on several public benchmarks without numbers.
qCPcEC71m6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a practical, modular system-level architecture that integrates planning, perception, verification, recovery and memory, with broad validation across settings and backends.
qCPcEC71m6.main_concern: Limited methodological novelty, since the components (hierarchical planning, multi-agent orchestration, skills, memory, recovery) exist in prior agentic robotics frameworks and the source of the gains is hard to isolate.

FJeh7fEsBN.one_liner: Benchmark for heterogeneous 3D class-incremental learning plus PolyMem, an exemplar-free method storing higher-order feature statistics.
FJeh7fEsBN.problem: 3D class-incremental learning must handle same-class point clouds from heterogeneous domains (CAD, RGB-D scans, video reconstructions, corrupted data), which complicates intra-class feature distributions and memory.
FJeh7fEsBN.method: Defines the Domain3D-CIL protocol with mixed-domain point clouds and no domain labels at training, adapts mainstream CIL methods to 3D, and proposes PolyMem, which implicitly models higher-order feature statistics in an analytic statistical memory.
FJeh7fEsBN.key_idea: Frozen pretrained features pass through an RBF-derived polynomial feature map into accumulated statistics solved by closed-form ridge regression, capturing higher-order statistics without exemplars.
FJeh7fEsBN.evidence: Ten pretrained-model-based CIL methods run with the same backbone and protocol on four dataset combinations, with extra backbones, task splits and a polynomial-order ablation, over 3 runs.
FJeh7fEsBN.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports improved average performance across domains and notable gains on real-world domains without numbers.
FJeh7fEsBN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the heterogeneous 3D CIL setting is relevant and underexplored and that PolyMem consistently improves average accuracy across dataset pairs and backbones.
FJeh7fEsBN.main_concern: Nothing in PolyMem is shown to be specific to heterogeneity or 3D (it resembles RanPAC with a different feature map), so the gain may come from a better kernel approximation, and baselines such as KLDA and FeCAM are missing.

JlkIX1gcs0.one_liner: Self-play RL trains adversarial traffic that causes avoidable, foreseeable collisions with black-box driving planners, using a counterfactual braking reward.
JlkIX1gcs0.problem: Closed-loop driving benchmarks reveal little about planner weaknesses, and adversarial collisions are only informative if the planner could have avoided them.
JlkIX1gcs0.method: Trains traffic agents with self-play RL at scale against a black-box planner, using a non-differentiable reward that tests whether braking in time would have avoided the collision and whether the danger was foreseeable early enough to react.
JlkIX1gcs0.key_idea: The reward is a counterfactual check of whether timely braking would have avoided the collision and whether it was foreseeable, optimized with self-play RL.
JlkIX1gcs0.evidence: Five rule-based and learned planners compared against gradient-based adversaries, plus cross-evaluation, use as a traffic model in real-world scenes against log replay and rule-based traffic, and an at-fault criterion from nuPlan.
JlkIX1gcs0.claimed_gains: About three times more avoidable collisions than gradient-based adversaries, which collide about as often or less.
JlkIX1gcs0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that targeting avoidable and foreseeable failures is useful and clearly presented, with ablations showing why failure quality matters.
JlkIX1gcs0.main_concern: Baselines KING and ReGentS get 10 seconds while Planner-Breaker runs up to 256 seconds (median collision at 10.5 seconds), so the avoidable-failure advantage is confounded with attack duration.

Fj3LLUetVb.one_liner: Animates vector glyphs with their own finite-element vibration modes, with a frozen video diffusion model supervising amplitudes and phases.
Fj3LLUetVb.problem: Free-form point optimization under video score distillation moves points and frames independently along noisy gradients, tearing outlines and causing jitter, while skeleton or keypoint alternatives need category-specific priors.
Fj3LLUetVb.method: A finite-element eigenproblem on the vector outline yields the glyph's softest bending modes for the whole letter and each part, rigid translations and rotations are applied per part in closed form, and a frozen video diffusion model supervises only mode amplitudes and phases driven by whole-cycle harmonics.
Fj3LLUetVb.key_idea: Motion is restricted to a low-dimensional basis of glyph eigenmodes with whole-cycle harmonic drive, so SDS gradients produce smooth, seamlessly looping animation.
Fj3LLUetVb.evidence: Comparison with Dynamic Typography, ablations on temporal parameterization (median jerk 0.78 vs 2.86 over 20 paired cases) and spatial components, a user study and X-CLIP scores.
Fj3LLUetVb.claimed_gains: not stated; the visible abstract describes smoother, looping motion without numbers.
Fj3LLUetVb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the glyph-derived modal basis with harmonic temporal drive is well motivated and reduces jitter and boundary stretching, supported by the temporal ablation.
Fj3LLUetVb.main_concern: Experiments do not isolate the benefit of FEM eigenmodes over a simpler smooth deformation basis, and evidence that the motion matches the prompted action is limited.

kX23kRoFcf.one_liner: Distills a constitution into LoRAs and steering vectors, subtracting control-trained from constitution-trained ones, for tunable inference-time defenses.
kX23kRoFcf.problem: The generality and flexibility of constitution-based alignment are unclear, and models remain open to jailbreaks (especially long-context and multi-turn attacks) and misalignment.
kX23kRoFcf.method: Distills constitution-consistent behavior from synthetic corpora into low-rank adapters and steering vectors, then subtracts control-trained objects from constitution-trained ones to form constitutional adapters, which can be scaled at inference time and transferred zero-shot from a base model to its post-trained checkpoint.
kX23kRoFcf.key_idea: Subtracting an adapter trained on a matched control corpus from the constitution-trained adapter isolates the constitutional behavior, and inference-time scaling trades defense against benign compliance.
kX23kRoFcf.evidence: Multiple recent models evaluated on many safety benchmarks, attack methods (including Crescendo and Best-of-75) and defense baselines, with long-context and multi-turn settings.
kX23kRoFcf.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports higher jailbreak defense success and measured alignment without numbers.
kX23kRoFcf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation clear and a lightweight approach using only constitution data practically relevant, with the matched control-corpus difference and broad experiments as strengths.
kX23kRoFcf.main_concern: Baseline and improvement numbers appear to mix attack-success and defense-success metrics, no LoRA baseline matches the refusal-steering baseline, and the Claude-centered generation and judging pipeline limits the generality claims.

8pA5Tl0IWS.one_liner: Unified autoregressive few-step video generation and editing model distilled with velocity moment matching and autoregressive unrolling.
8pA5Tl0IWS.problem: Converting a strong multi-task bidirectional video model into a few-step causal student is costly and suffers from over-saturation, degraded motion and temporal instability.
8pA5Tl0IWS.method: One model covers Text-to-Video, Video-to-Video, Editing Propagation, Reference-guided Video Editing and Camera Pose Change, trained with two-stage distillation: Velocity Moment Matching (VMM) at student-reached intermediate states, then autoregressive unrolling on the student's own predictions.
8pA5Tl0IWS.key_idea: VMM matches conditional velocity moments at student-reached states, avoiding ODE-pair pregeneration and causal teachers, and unrolling exposes the student to its own autoregressive predictions.
8pA5Tl0IWS.evidence: Comparisons of distillation methods (including Self-Forcing) with control experiments from identical initializations, and demonstrations of the five tasks, several of them only qualitative.
8pA5Tl0IWS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a practical single model covering several generation and editing tasks with low-latency block-wise output, and VMM as a simpler distillation path.
8pA5Tl0IWS.main_concern: Gains cannot be attributed to VMM because the distillation comparisons change objective, rollout strategy, learning rates and compute together, and the dual-type conditioning interface is not ablated.

sHe1G2Bj2B.one_liner: Trains k LoRA adapters on a shared backbone so each contributes one sample, optimizing pass@k jointly.
sHe1G2Bj2B.problem: Inference-time scaling usually samples repeatedly from a single policy rather than spreading the sample budget across complementary policies.
sHe1G2Bj2B.method: Realizes a population of k policies as separate LoRA adapters on a shared language model backbone, where each adapter contributes one response to a k-sample objective optimized for pass@k.
sHe1G2Bj2B.key_idea: Each of k jointly trained adapters supplies exactly one of the k samples, so training for best-of-k pushes the adapters to specialize on complementary problems.
sHe1G2Bj2B.evidence: Linear-setting theory showing a LoRA population can reach zero best-of-k approximation error where single LoRAs cannot, and experiments on multiple reasoning tasks against single-policy and mixture baselines.
sHe1G2Bj2B.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports consistent pass@k improvement over a single-policy baseline without numbers.
sHe1G2Bj2B.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea intuitive and well controlled (mixture baseline, parameter-count and training-cost controls) with consistent gains across tasks and seeds.
sHe1G2Bj2B.main_concern: The surrogate gradient rewards extra successes beyond the first, unlike pass@k, so gains may reflect the estimator, and novelty over population RL and multiple choice learning is moderate.

hzhdHQ3mYZ.one_liner: Gaussian proxy for medical volume rendering with shared geometry and function-conditioned appearance, enabling transfer-function edits without refitting.
hzhdHQ3mYZ.problem: A Gaussian proxy fitted to one transfer function (TF) must be fitted again whenever the TF is edited.
hzhdHQ3mYZ.method: Each Gaussian stores local tissue and intensity samples to which a requested region-specific TF is applied by direct lookup, while a shared neural network and low-rank factors learn the remaining cinematic appearance change, with both offsets vanishing at the base TF.
hzhdHQ3mYZ.key_idea: Direct TF lookup on per-Gaussian tissue-intensity samples plus offsets that vanish at the base TF keeps geometry fixed while appearance follows the TF.
hzhdHQ3mYZ.evidence: Seven CT and MR scans compared with region-aware VEG on validation, interpolation, composition and out-of-distribution edits.
hzhdHQ3mYZ.claimed_gains: Mean PSNR gains of 1.10 to 1.52 dB over region-aware VEG, with cached rendering averaging 524 FPS at 1600 resolution and 1.17 ms TF updates.
hzhdHQ3mYZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that treating the TF as inference-time control over one Gaussian proxy with shared geometry is a promising, well-motivated design that improves on VEG-style methods.
hzhdHQ3mYZ.main_concern: The comparison relies on a custom VEG extension and omits Render-FM, and per-Gaussian tissue labels fixed at initialization can mismatch the optimized geometry.

wtioNroBNW.one_liner: Develops a vector Bellman theory for multichain robust average-reward MDPs and a Halpern-type planning algorithm with convergence guarantees.
wtioNroBNW.problem: Robust average-reward MDPs can have optimal long-run rewards that depend on the initial state, which requires a vector Bellman theory covering recurrent-class rewards and transition uncertainty.
wtioNroBNW.method: For finite models with compact post-action (s,a)-rectangular ambiguity, a gain-first, bias-second principle gives a coupled vector gain-bias system whose finite solutions identify the optimal robust gain and stationary saddle strategies, and a robust approximately shifted Halpern algorithm plans using the asymptotically affine behavior of the Bellman operator.
wtioNroBNW.key_idea: A coupled vector gain-bias Bellman system imposed on both controller and adversary certifies the optimal robust gain from all initial states and drives a shifted Halpern iteration.
wtioNroBNW.evidence: Theoretical results on solvability conditions, convergence of gain estimates and Bellman displacements, and finite-budget average-optimality of greedy controllers; no experiments are mentioned.
wtioNroBNW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it provides a comprehensive theory for multichain robust MDPs that was previously absent, with novel components such as the solvability characterizations.
wtioNroBNW.main_concern: At 71 pages with essential arguments in the appendices, reviewers say the paper is too long for a conference and hard to review properly.

6wzeuCEa6X.one_liner: Benchmark where two LLM agents attack and defend live services concurrently in isolated sandboxes, ranked on a unified reference scale.
6wzeuCEa6X.problem: Cybersecurity agent benchmarks evaluate attack or defense in isolation against static targets, which saturate and miss simultaneous attack and defense under live pressure.
6wzeuCEa6X.method: Two agents compete under identical rules in multi-round attack-and-defense matches over continuously changing services, supported by an automated agentic pipeline that reproduces, packages, verifies and reviews new challenges, a ranking algorithm mapping attack, defense and service-uptime ability onto a unified scale, and a resource-efficient game-selection algorithm.
6wzeuCEa6X.key_idea: Symmetric concurrent attack-and-defense matches turn static CTF targets into evolving contests, with pairwise outcomes mapped to a unified reference scale for ranking.
6wzeuCEa6X.evidence: Evaluation of 11 frontier LLM agents in isolated sandbox matches (the abstract is truncated before the results).
6wzeuCEa6X.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that live, symmetric attack-and-defense evaluation addresses an important limitation of static cybersecurity agent benchmarks.
6wzeuCEa6X.main_concern: Reviewers cite overstated novelty, uncontrolled CVE exposure across model knowledge cutoffs, and the exclusion of 169 (about 30%) of matches, along with unclear writing.

YgT9fcKfut.one_liner: Optimistic FTRL with an EMA cascade for high-order optimism achieves horizon-independent individual regret in finite N-player normal-form games.
YgT9fcKfut.problem: Standard Optimistic Hedge has worst-case individual regret at least exponential in either the number of players or the largest action-set size.
YgT9fcKfut.method: ECHO-OFTRL is a deterministic, fully uncoupled optimistic FTRL algorithm with an exponential-moving-average cascade for high-order optimism, and its regret bound is related to the order of the prediction-error filter's zero at one.
YgT9fcKfut.key_idea: An exponential-moving-average cascade supplies high-order optimistic predictions inside OFTRL, whose prediction-error filter has a high-order zero at one that controls regret.
YgT9fcKfut.evidence: Theory only: a lower bound for Optimistic Hedge, a self-play upper bound for every horizon and an adversarial-setting guarantee; no experiments are mentioned.
YgT9fcKfut.claimed_gains: Self-play regret O(N log m_max) for every horizon T >= 1, and adversarial regret at most the self-play bound plus O(sqrt(T log m_max)).
YgT9fcKfut.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the individual-regret lower bound for Optimistic Hedge and the horizon-independent O(N log m_max) upper bound are significant results on a well-motivated problem.
YgT9fcKfut.main_concern: Sections 4 and 5 give little intuition for why higher-order optimism yields the bound, and the comparison with concurrent work (for example Soleymani and Piliouras) is incomplete.

yOY1B2wtju.one_liner: Controlled ablation replacing image embeddings with padding tokens shows how visual content shapes scaling in native multimodal pre-training.
yOY1B2wtju.problem: How visual signals shape scaling behavior and support capabilities beyond visual understanding in native multimodal pre-training is unclear.
yOY1B2wtju.method: Trains matched models across sizes and compute budgets with either real image embeddings or content-free padding token embeddings, then compares text prediction loss, compute-optimal allocation, aggregate language scores and text-only spatial reasoning.
yOY1B2wtju.key_idea: Replacing image embeddings with content-free padding while keeping the text and sequence structure isolates the contribution of visual content across scale.
yOY1B2wtju.evidence: Controlled runs across multiple model sizes and training budgets (largest 3B activated non-embedding parameters per reviewers), evaluated on text loss, language benchmarks and text-only spatial reasoning tasks.
yOY1B2wtju.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports that the relative multimodal loss benefit grows approximately as a power law of compute.
yOY1B2wtju.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the matched image-versus-padding design across scales and compute budgets is careful and that the finding that vision helps text-only spatial reasoning is interesting.
yOY1B2wtju.main_concern: The padding control may introduce its own training effects for image-dependent text, and the largest model size and modest, selective spatial gains limit the scaling conclusions.

k4hW7kO4qJ.one_liner: Variational inference with diffusion priors using a Fisher-divergence-plus-terminal-KL objective, with particle and amortized variants for imaging inverse problems.
k4hW7kO4qJ.problem: Scalable variational inference with diffusion priors and an implicit, non-degenerate posterior is hard because the prior KL term depends on the score of the variational distribution.
k4hW7kO4qJ.method: Principled Posterior Matching uses the KL-dissipation relation to write the discrepancy of two diffusion-evolved distributions as an integrated Fisher divergence plus a terminal KL, derives a pathwise gradient via a score-projection identity, and supports particle optimization per observation or an amortized reconstruction network.
k4hW7kO4qJ.key_idea: The prior KL is rewritten through KL dissipation as an integrated Fisher divergence plus a terminal KL, giving a pathwise gradient that is unbiased when scores are exact.
k4hW7kO4qJ.evidence: Natural-image inpainting, super-resolution and deblurring, fluorescence-microscopy reconstruction and synthetic radio-interferometric imaging (abstract truncated), plus toy experiments.
k4hW7kO4qJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the objective is cleaner than the integral KL used by DAVI, serves both per-observation particles and an amortized network without likelihood-score approximation, and is clearly written.
k4hW7kO4qJ.main_concern: The unbiased or exact framing holds only for exact scores, and posterior quality is not measured well (uncalibrated diversity score, thin reporting, no error bars).

pkTV4050pC.one_liner: Global Bayesian optimization on partially observed graphs via a low-rank surrogate graph, Laplacian-spectrum GP kernel and decision-aware edge queries.
pkTV4050pC.problem: BO over graph nodes needs a globally defined kernel, which incomplete topology makes unavailable, limiting existing methods to local neighborhood-based exploration.
pkTV4050pC.method: Reconstructs a graph-valid low-rank surrogate from revealed edges, uses its Laplacian spectrum to define a Gaussian process kernel over all nodes (a linear model in d-dimensional node features), and derives acquisition rules that pick edge queries by their expected effect on the next function evaluation.
pkTV4050pC.key_idea: A kernel from the Laplacian spectrum of a low-rank graph surrogate lets function evaluations learn shared coefficients while edge queries learn node features.
pkTV4050pC.evidence: Proofs that a small number of structural observations identifies the surrogate and that geometry error affects regret only at the selected node and the optimum, plus experiments on protein interaction networks, a molecular similarity graph, a Wikipedia page graph and synthetic graphs.
pkTV4050pC.claimed_gains: Lower final regret than structure-free search and local graph BO on all ten objectives at matched budget (abstract truncated after 'at matched').
pkTV4050pC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the partially observed graph BO setting is new, the global surrogate with shared coefficients and learned features is sound, and results beat local methods, especially on large graphs.
pkTV4050pC.main_concern: The pair-query comparison does not isolate the benefit of decision-aware acquisition because it changes landmark queries, pinning and membership updates together, and the topology uncertainty model looks ad hoc.

tT2r5ALG1e.one_liner: Cascade of lightweight retrievers, a verifier and an on-demand MLLM responder keeps proactive assistants always on at lower energy.
tT2r5ALG1e.problem: Always-on proactive assistants cannot invoke a multimodal LLM at every timestep on device because it is prohibitively expensive.
tT2r5ALG1e.method: PRISM uses lightweight Visual and State Retrievers to flag instruction-relevant events with high recall, an on-demand Verifier that checks whether each candidate satisfies the requested condition using current context, recent history and semantic states, and an MLLM Responder invoked only after verification.
tT2r5ALG1e.key_idea: Continuous monitoring is cast as semantic retrieval, and a verifier gates actionability so the MLLM runs only on verified candidates.
tT2r5ALG1e.evidence: PhoStream benchmark evaluation of proactive tasks, premature responses and a performance-energy comparison against direct MLLM invocation, with component and threshold ablations; energy is estimated from prefill cost using proxy models.
tT2r5ALG1e.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract; reviewers quote the Forward metric rising from 7.7 to 22.7 and premature triggering falling from 81.3% to 9.4% on PhoStream.
tT2r5ALG1e.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the retrieve-verify-respond decomposition addresses a real on-device deployment problem and that the Verifier cuts premature triggering and improves the Forward metric on PhoStream.
tT2r5ALG1e.main_concern: The energy savings rest on an incomplete estimated cost model (prefill only, fixed power draw, proxy models, no decoding or ASR), so the Pareto claim is not measured.

ohU5InsZEd.one_liner: Grows spiking neural networks by adding identical neuron pairs whose outputs cancel exactly, preserving temporal function while keeping gradients nonzero.
ohU5InsZEd.problem: Fixed-width SNNs either limit representation or waste computation, and growing them is hard because structural changes disrupt temporal dynamics and zero readout blocks the immediate gradient to new neurons.
ohU5InsZEd.method: Adds neurons as identical pairs whose forward contributions cancel exactly while their backward signals stay nonzero and opposing, implemented as an atomic transaction that expands the model, migrates Adam state, verifies invariants and resumes surrogate-gradient training.
ohU5InsZEd.key_idea: Identical neuron pairs with opposite outgoing weights cancel in the forward pass yet receive opposing nonzero gradients, so growth preserves logits and still trains.
ohU5InsZEd.evidence: Theoretical guarantees (temporal function preservation, conditional immediate trainability, optimizer-state preservation, layer-wise composition) and experiments on fully connected LIF SNNs including DVS Gesture, with exact preservation verified at every growth event.
ohU5InsZEd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paired-birth construction gives exact, verifiable preservation of temporal logits and optimizer state while keeping new neurons immediately trainable.
ohU5InsZEd.main_concern: Empirical scope is narrow (fully connected LIF SNNs, no CIFAR10-DVS, convolutional or recurrent models), and one reviewer argues the construction adds little beyond known antisymmetric zero-output initializations.

sUleXx9qfl.one_liner: LiDAR 3D single-object tracker fusing a history-only motion prior with point observations by covariance intersection for cross-sensor transfer.
sUleXx9qfl.problem: Trackers trained on one LiDAR configuration bind appearance, motion scale and confidence to it, so historical archives are hard to reuse on new sensor setups, and localization errors accumulate through the search region.
sUleXx9qfl.method: Separates a continuous-time transition prior from acquisition-sensitive point observations: builds masked point tokens, compares the current crop with an initialization anchor and recent memories to predict an appearance innovation with uncertainty, trains on range-density-degraded paired views, and fuses motion and appearance estimates by covariance intersection.
sUleXx9qfl.key_idea: Factorizing tracking into a history-only motion transition and a sensor-sensitive observation, fused by covariance intersection, with paired degraded views to discourage sensor-specific shortcuts.
sUleXx9qfl.evidence: A frozen all-direction protocol covering six transfer directions across three public driving datasets and two object categories, with ablations of the key components.
sUleXx9qfl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree cross-sensor source-only transfer is a significant setting, the six-direction evaluation is rigorous, and ReLiTrack achieves the best average Success and Precision across transfer tasks.
sUleXx9qfl.main_concern: Algorithmic novelty is limited because motion prediction, memory and covariance intersection are established techniques, uncertainty accuracy is not directly validated, and the degradation only simulates point-support changes.

3mZxgwZqti.one_liner: Illumination Intensity Ranking loss supervises regional brightness order and position in a latent bridge matching model for illumination editing.
3mZxgwZqti.problem: Pixel-wise alignment measures reconstruction error but does not organize illumination variation with regional brightness, so relighting outputs stay close to the source lighting.
3mZxgwZqti.method: Introduces the IIR loss, which builds luminance rankings over image patches to supervise how bright each region should be and where regions of corresponding brightness should occur, integrated with latent bridge matching (IC-LBM) and condition-confirmed initialization for illumination injection.
3mZxgwZqti.key_idea: Rank patch luminance and supervise both rank values and positions, coupling regional brightness with spatial layout without intrinsic decomposition or 3D reconstruction.
3mZxgwZqti.evidence: Indoor scene relighting experiments with ablations on luminance and positional consistency and on the conditioning mechanism.
3mZxgwZqti.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract claims the best performance on indoor scene relighting without numbers.
3mZxgwZqti.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the IIR loss targets a real failure of pixel-wise relighting objectives and that quantitative results and ablations show the luminance and position terms help.
3mZxgwZqti.main_concern: Related work does not critically discuss prior patch-based illumination-aware methods such as intrinsic image harmonization, leaving the positioning of the contribution unclear.

T8LCiayxWk.one_liner: Filters VLA post-training demonstrations by scoring each sample's gradient compatibility with matched clean validation samples during a one-epoch warm-up.
T8LCiayxWk.problem: Post-training VLA models on collected robot data is sensitive to errors such as execution mistakes, sensor drift and timestamp misalignment, manual inspection is costly, and existing cleaners target specific corruption types.
T8LCiayxWk.method: During a one-epoch warm-up, scores each candidate sample online by comparing its gradient with those of task-semantic and visually matched validation samples, aggregates scores per episode, and applies a simple automatic rule to turn them into filtering decisions.
T8LCiayxWk.key_idea: Local gradient compatibility with semantically and visually matched clean reference samples, measured along the training trajectory, proxies each sample's effect on post-training.
T8LCiayxWk.evidence: Synthetic corruptions, naturally suboptimal demonstrations and real-world robot tasks across multiple VLA backbones, with baselines and ablations.
T8LCiayxWk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree local gradient compatibility against matched references is an intuitive, model-aware idea backed by comprehensive evaluation across corruption types, backbones and real robots.
T8LCiayxWk.main_concern: The method needs a clean reference set of good demonstrations, which may be as hard to collect as a clean dataset, and reference matching may wrongly drop valid but different demonstrations.

Br0eBRM5mb.one_liner: Benchmark of 918 screen-recorded web-editing requests with speech and cursor references, testing intent recovery and editing.
Br0eBRM5mb.problem: Screen-recorded edit requests use deictic words such as 'this' and 'there' whose referents depend on speech, cursor trajectories, page state and edit history, which benchmarks assuming explicit specifications do not test.
Br0eBRM5mb.method: A bilingual benchmark of 918 instances spanning 13,907 edit steps with three tracks: Direct Editing from recordings, Instruction Recovery of explicit intent, and Instruction Utility, where recovered instructions drive a fixed code executor.
Br0eBRM5mb.key_idea: Separating direct editing, instruction recovery and executor-based instruction utility shows whether failures come from grounding weak references or from executing edits.
Br0eBRM5mb.evidence: 17 open- and closed-source models evaluated, with step-level analyses, controlled ablations on temporally aligned audiovisual evidence and alternative judges.
Br0eBRM5mb.claimed_gains: The best models reach 51.17 EFS for Direct Editing and 49.14 IRS, and the strongest recovered instructions reach 51.08 EFS under a fixed executor versus 89.69 EFS with oracle instructions.
Br0eBRM5mb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written, addresses a practical speech-plus-cursor editing setting, and evaluates 17 models with extensive robustness analyses.
Br0eBRM5mb.main_concern: The EFS weighting is weakly justified and some rankings shift under alternative weights, and the scripted requests limit ecological validity.

DCKtUYfPsp.one_liner: Gaussian image codec using closed-form single-Gaussian error to decide where to fit more Gaussians, with calibrated global budget allocation.
DCKtUYfPsp.problem: Existing per-image Gaussian codecs need costly image-specific optimization to decide how limited Gaussian capacity is distributed across heterogeneous regions.
DCKtUYfPsp.method: Uses the closed-form reconstruction error of the single-Gaussian case as a cheap measure of local difficulty to fit higher-capacity candidates only where useful, calibrates short-horizon distortion estimates with a few longer-horizon fits, then globally selects under a Gaussian budget and compresses the result.
DCKtUYfPsp.key_idea: Closed-form single-Gaussian error flags difficult regions cheaply, and a few long fits calibrate short-fit distortion estimates for global budget-aware selection.
DCKtUYfPsp.evidence: Rate-distortion and fitting-time comparisons with representative Gaussian codecs on standard and large image datasets, plus decoding throughput.
DCKtUYfPsp.claimed_gains: Competitive or superior rate-distortion performance while cutting per-image fitting time by 3.0x to 15.7x, with decoding at 175.9 to 478.2 MP/s.
DCKtUYfPsp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper targets the practical cost of per-image Gaussian fitting and reports competitive rate-distortion with substantial fitting-time gains.
DCKtUYfPsp.main_concern: Teacher calibration is not validated by a calibrated-versus-uncalibrated ablation, and it is calibrated to 160-step fits while the final codec keeps 40-step parameters.

XblId7XPeb.one_liner: Sequential recommender combining frozen language semantic state, horizon-aligned successor dynamics and a behavioral prior via minimum-information closure.
XblId7XPeb.problem: Language-enhanced sequential recommenders capture what a sequence means but not where it is going, and repeating a one-step operator assumes horizon-invariant dynamics.
XblId7XPeb.method: Frozen language representations give a recency-weighted semantic state, training interactions give sparse popularity-relative successor dynamics queried at each source event's exact distance to the target, and a pretrained recommender gives a behavioral reference, combined by a minimum-information closure that deviates minimally from the behavioral prior.
XblId7XPeb.key_idea: Each history event queries a successor operator at its exact distance to the target, and the evidence is merged with the behavioral prior by a minimum-deviation closure.
XblId7XPeb.evidence: Three same-setting Amazon benchmarks against prior methods, with component, horizon, state, popularity, encoder-transfer and efficiency ablations and theory on horizon mismatch and a robust ranking condition.
XblId7XPeb.claimed_gains: Best in 11 of 12 comparisons with prior methods, and improves all 21 full-catalog metrics over its anchor, with relative gains up to 18.64%.
XblId7XPeb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation (semantic similarity versus directional transition dynamics) is clear, the framework is interpretable, and it consistently improves over the matched backbone.
XblId7XPeb.main_concern: The independent value of horizon alignment is not isolated (gains over the one-step history control are small, for example 0.0008 NDCG@10), and novelty beyond combining existing mechanisms is limited.

oRou0GnNA8.one_liner: Replaces long tool outputs with the agent's expectation plus a small-model residual stating what the result confirms, corrects or reveals.
oRou0GnNA8.problem: Long tool outputs accumulate in LLM agent context and raise inference cost, and compression that keeps facts does not convey how results confirm or revise the agent's expectations.
oRou0GnNA8.method: Before each tool call the main agent writes a compact expected observation; after execution a smaller model compares the actual output with it and writes a semantic residual (confirms, corrects, newly reveals, unresolved), and for long outputs the expectation-residual pair replaces the raw output in later context.
oRou0GnNA8.key_idea: Compress tool feedback relative to an explicit pre-execution expectation so the context records evidence updates rather than only fact coverage.
oRou0GnNA8.evidence: Six software-engineering and terminal-agent benchmarks including ProgramBench, with a matched summary baseline and offline diagnostics, run with Qwen models.
oRou0GnNA8.claimed_gains: 98.97% of Raw's macro-averaged task score with on average 59.06% of its main-agent tokens and 60.79% of its estimated cost, and 4.10 percentage points above a matched summary on ProgramBench.
oRou0GnNA8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating fact coverage from evidence updating is a simple, training-free and practical idea, with a well-designed matched-summary comparison.
oRou0GnNA8.main_concern: Evidence that the residual itself matters is weak: the matched control is the weakest summary on ProgramBench, differences from simpler alternatives are within noise, and only Qwen models are tested.

RBUjKdb9eV.one_liner: Pretrained camera-space inverse-dynamics model scores executability of imagined futures, and a VITA loss trains world models on recovered-action discrepancy.
RBUjKdb9eV.problem: World action models generalize poorly across tasks even when their predicted futures depict plausible manipulation, and it is unclear whether the failure lies in future generation or action recovery.
RBUjKdb9eV.method: Decouples a world action model into a world model and an inverse-dynamics model, holds the IDM fixed (AoE, pretrained on large-scale robot data) while swapping the source of future images, then adds the VITA loss that passes generated futures through the frozen AoE and penalizes discrepancies in recovered actions.
RBUjKdb9eV.key_idea: Generated futures pass through a frozen camera-space inverse-dynamics model, and the loss penalizes differences in recovered actions, redirecting generation toward gripper and interaction regions.
RBUjKdb9eV.evidence: Two world models and three manipulation benchmarks (LIBERO and RoboTwin2.0 per reviewers), with diagnostics comparing recorded and predicted futures.
RBUjKdb9eV.claimed_gains: Raises the execution success of generated futures from near zero to 47.0%.
RBUjKdb9eV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the diagnosis that failures concentrate on gripper and interaction geometry and the VITA loss clearly improve execution success across world models, with thorough ablations.
RBUjKdb9eV.main_concern: Evaluation is simulation-only with no real-robot results, lacks baselines with large-scale pretraining such as DreamZero or Cosmos3-DROID, and reports no generated-video quality metrics.

V1bWbnDP2H.one_liner: Jenga-based bimanual manipulation benchmark with six task families, a Real2Sim pipeline and paired real-sim policy evaluation.
V1bWbnDP2H.problem: Evaluating manipulation under interaction-induced scene changes needs long-horizon tasks where earlier actions alter contacts and structural support for later ones.
V1bWbnDP2H.method: Six configurable Jenga task families involve bimanual coordination and tool use, a Real2Sim pipeline builds matching simulated environments, and four policy architectures are evaluated over twelve configurations with separately trained real and simulated policies and progress metrics beyond binary success.
V1bWbnDP2H.key_idea: Jenga gives repeatable structures where each manipulation changes support for later actions, and Real2Sim twins allow comparing real and simulated policy evaluation.
V1bWbnDP2H.evidence: Four policy architectures across twelve configurations, with 12,000 demonstrations and 960 evaluation episodes per reviewers, and a real-sim progress correlation analysis.
V1bWbnDP2H.claimed_gains: Real-sim progress correlation of Pearson r = 0.880 and a normalized MMRV of 0.1217.
V1bWbnDP2H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating contact-rich, structure-changing manipulation is a meaningful problem and that the benchmark with paired real and sim environments represents substantial engineering effort.
V1bWbnDP2H.main_concern: Task diversity is narrow (same wooden blocks, structured sequences), cross-domain agreement is weaker than the pooled correlation suggests with large ranking reversals, and no sim-to-real transfer or new insight is offered.

B0gCltBp7d.one_liner: Hyperbolic upper-half-space positional encoding that jointly represents spatial position and magnification hierarchy for multi-resolution whole-slide MIL.
B0gCltBp7d.problem: Existing positional encodings model each resolution independently or treat cross-resolution spatial relationships uniformly, ignoring that the area covered by a patch grows quadratically with magnification in multi-resolution WSIs.
B0gCltBp7d.method: Hyperbolic Hierarchical Positional Encoding (H2PE) embeds spatial topology and resolution hierarchy in hyperbolic upper half-space, uses physical scale (MPP) to place patches from different magnifications, and provides injection schemes for different MIL aggregators.
B0gCltBp7d.key_idea: Patches from different magnifications are placed in hyperbolic upper half-space, whose exponential capacity encodes the resolution hierarchy and scale-dependent spatial distance.
B0gCltBp7d.evidence: Three public datasets and three multi-resolution MIL architectures (ZoomMIL, H2MIL and DSMIL per reviewers) with AUC and ACC tables, ROI explanations, efficiency analysis and ablations.
B0gCltBp7d.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract; a reviewer reports it is best on all but 3 of 12 cases.
B0gCltBp7d.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the geometric formulation is well motivated for an underexplored problem, is model-independent with small runtime overhead, and performs competitively across aggregators.
B0gCltBp7d.main_concern: The case for hyperbolic geometry is thin: only three magnification levels limit the distortion advantage, normalizing Euclidean distances by patch size may do as well, h differs across backbones, and no significance tests or recent backbones are included.

J5LbOg4v7d.one_liner: Propagates TD(lambda) credit backward through a provenance DAG of memory creation so ancestor memories receive Q-value updates.
J5LbOg4v7d.problem: Episodic memory methods score each memory independently, ignoring the dependency chains through which retrieved memories enable the creation of later memories.
J5LbOg4v7d.method: Records which memories were retrieved when each new memory was created in a provenance DAG, applies TD(lambda) eligibility traces to memory Q-values with credit decaying as (gamma*lambda)^d with DAG depth d, and values a retrieval set as the mean of per-memory values plus an explicit approximation residual within an Exogenous-Context MDP formulation.
J5LbOg4v7d.key_idea: Eligibility-trace credit decays with structural DAG depth rather than temporal distance, so memories that enabled later useful memories are rewarded.
J5LbOg4v7d.evidence: Five interaction, code-generation and agentic benchmarks, with ablations on LiveCodeBench, BFCL and DSBench and analyses of Q-values and runtime learning.
J5LbOg4v7d.claimed_gains: Improves average held-out, final runtime and cumulative success rates over the strongest baseline by 2.53, 4.23 and 2.13 percentage points.
J5LbOg4v7d.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that transferring eligibility traces to a provenance DAG is a principled, intuitive credit-assignment mechanism with consistent gains across extensive benchmarks and baselines.
J5LbOg4v7d.main_concern: The method depends on the quality of the extracted DAG, with no analysis of memory footprint or latency as the graph grows, an additive set-value assumption that ignores synergies, and a hard-to-follow Exogenous-Context MDP formulation.

fHbDsua46v.one_liner: Brings outcome-reward RL to latent reasoners via a Gaussian surrogate policy over latent transitions and a learned stopping head.
fHbDsua46v.problem: Latent reasoners remain imitation-bound because latent trajectories lack a tractable per-step likelihood and an adaptive stopping interface, so outcome rewards cannot elicit latent test-time scaling.
fHbDsua46v.method: SLPO adds a differentiable surrogate policy over latent transitions (an isotropic Gaussian surrogate likelihood) for trajectory-level credit assignment, and a correctness-supervised stopping head that outcome-reward optimization refines into a variable-horizon policy.
fHbDsua46v.key_idea: An isotropic Gaussian surrogate gives latent transitions a tractable likelihood for policy-gradient RL, while a stopping head learns the number of latent steps from outcome reward.
fHbDsua46v.evidence: Two continuous latent reasoners (COCONUT and CODI per reviewers), two backbones and three held-out benchmarks, with transfer to soft-token inference.
