fHbDsua46v.claimed_gains: Improves Pass@8 and Pass@16 in all 12 backbone-dataset settings, with gains of up to 12.07 percentage points.
fHbDsua46v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated and the Gaussian surrogate plus stopping gate gives a practical interface, with Pass@8 and Pass@16 gains across all tested settings.
fHbDsua46v.main_concern: Reviewers ask for ablations that remove the surrogate and the stopping head separately, note that the theory rests on unchecked closeness conditions, and point to small gains on CODI.

hlY5KNCRw8.one_liner: Multi-view 3D referring segmentation framework adding semantic category enhancement, text-conditioned spatial position guidance and cross-view aggregation.
hlY5KNCRw8.problem: Sparse multi-view observations give incomplete, fragmented object representations that make it hard to capture category-specific semantics and to distinguish instances by spatial location.
hlY5KNCRw8.method: Semantic Category Enhancement (SCE) strengthens target category representations through text-guided semantic alignment, Spatial Position Guidance (SPG) estimates text-conditioned confidence scores over scene locations to find target-relevant regions, and a multi-view aggregation strategy improves cross-view consistency of predictions.
hlY5KNCRw8.key_idea: Two ambiguity-specific modules, text-guided category anchors and text-conditioned location confidence, are paired with shared-query cross-view aggregation for sparse-view referring segmentation.
hlY5KNCRw8.evidence: Experiments on the MVRefer benchmark against MVGGT, with ablations of the SCE, SPG and cross-view aggregation components.
hlY5KNCRw8.claimed_gains: Outperforms MVGGT by 7.3 points in Acc@0.50 on the Multiple subset of MVRefer.
hlY5KNCRw8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that splitting the problem into semantic and spatial ambiguity is well motivated and that each module is ablated and helps, with clear presentation and comprehensive experiments.
hlY5KNCRw8.main_concern: Novelty relative to MVGGT is incremental, since the task and benchmark are inherited and the modules resemble category prototypes, Mask2Former-style masked attention and standard shared-query aggregation.

p1kyxdof0f.one_liner: Adds token-wise adaptive recursion inside the LoRA latent space with a shared transformation and threshold-based router.
p1kyxdof0f.problem: LoRA uses a fixed low-rank architecture whose expressiveness is usually raised by enlarging or adding modules at proportional parameter cost.
p1kyxdof0f.method: MoLR recursively refines each input's down-projected latent representation with a shared transformation, while a lightweight threshold-based router decides per token whether to refine further and dynamically adjusted thresholds encourage balanced use of recursion depths.
p1kyxdof0f.key_idea: Reapplying one shared transformation in LoRA's bottleneck, with a per-token threshold router choosing the recursion depth, adds depth without adding per-step parameters.
p1kyxdof0f.evidence: Language and vision tasks (21 datasets on six backbones per reviewers) compared with LoRA variants such as TopLoRA and MoSLoRA, with seed variance reported and analyses of recursion-depth allocation.
p1kyxdof0f.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract; reviewers cite average gains of 0.77 to 1.97 points over the strongest competing variant.
p1kyxdof0f.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the shared recursion inside LoRA's compact latent space is a reasonable, parameter-efficient design with consistent gains across backbones and tasks.
p1kyxdof0f.main_concern: Novelty beyond existing conditional recurrence and LoRA variants is limited, and the ablation lacks a depth-matched fixed baseline while accuracy falls at large recursion depth.

SRFXeYxg2B.one_liner: Benchmark for camera loss mid-task in VLA models, plus MINT, which trains policies on missing views and substitutes predicted images.
SRFXeYxg2B.problem: VLA models are developed and evaluated with all camera streams available, and how a camera dropping out during closed-loop manipulation affects them is poorly understood.
SRFXeYxg2B.method: MAIL-Bench interrupts different cameras at multiple stages of each policy's successful reference trajectory; MINT trains VLA policies to handle missing inputs and supplies predicted images, using optical-flow extrapolation for missing wrist views or total vision loss and an action-conditioned world model for missing third-person views, and withdraws predictions when they become unreliable.
SRFXeYxg2B.key_idea: Missing views are replaced by optical-flow or world-model predicted images, gated by reliability checks that withdraw the predictions once they become unreliable.
SRFXeYxg2B.evidence: Experiments on pi0.5 and GR00T N1.5 plus real-robot closed-loop experiments on the AgiBot G2.
SRFXeYxg2B.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says MINT improves task success under camera loss over the original models without numbers.
SRFXeYxg2B.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that mid-episode camera loss is a deployment-relevant, underexplored failure mode and that MAIL-Bench is a clean, useful test bed.
SRFXeYxg2B.main_concern: Evaluation uses only already-successful trajectories with fixed 30/45/60% onsets that match MINT's training curriculum, and ablations suggest the gains come mainly from missing-view fine-tuning rather than world modeling.

qZzF1akjXA.one_liner: Coarse-to-fine audio-driven listener facial motion model with delay-centered gated fusion and stochastic expression-subspace refinement.
qZzF1akjXA.problem: Responsive listener facial motion must account for speaker-cue timing and continuity with the listener's ongoing motion while capturing locally variable events such as brief expressions and blinks that are hard to predict deterministically.
qZzF1akjXA.method: A Reactive Gated Speaker-Listener Fusion module combines listener motion history with speaker audio through a delay-centered attention prior and adaptive gating, a coarse decoder predicts a base motion trajectory, and audio-conditioned stochastic residuals in the expression subspace refine it while keeping the coarse pose parameters.
qZzF1akjXA.key_idea: Delay-centered attention with adaptive gating handles timing, and stochastic residuals restricted to the expression subspace add facial variation without disturbing head pose.
qZzF1akjXA.evidence: ViCo and L2L evaluations on motion-quality metrics, delay, gate and blink analyses, deployment on an Ameca humanoid robot and a perceptual user study.
qZzF1akjXA.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports improvements over the evaluated baselines across multiple motion-quality metrics without numbers.
qZzF1akjXA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the coarse-to-fine separation of stable pose from stochastic expression refinement is well motivated and improves expression dynamics and blink realism on ViCo and L2L.
qZzF1akjXA.main_concern: Components mostly build on established techniques, and the delay analysis and stochastic refinement are not shown to capture true speaker-to-listener delays or diverse, contextually appropriate reactions.

0Knrw0HVz2.one_liner: Training-free method that moves attention from the latest tool-output visual tokens back to earlier visual evidence in think-with-images models.
0Knrw0HVz2.problem: More tool invocations (cropping, zooming) in think-with-images models fail to consistently reduce hallucinations because the model over-relies on the most recent visual observation and neglects evidence from earlier tool calls.
0Knrw0HVz2.method: RAVE recycles excess attention from visual tokens in the latest tool output and reallocates it to historical visual contexts, with no training.
0Knrw0HVz2.key_idea: Rebalancing attention away from the latest tool output toward earlier tool outputs counters the visual recency bias along the reasoning chain.
0Knrw0HVz2.evidence: Six models and fifteen benchmarks, with analyses showing the under-use of earlier visual evidence.
0Knrw0HVz2.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports reduced hallucinations and improved perception and reasoning without numbers.
0Knrw0HVz2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the analysis of under-used historical tool outputs is informative and that RAVE is effective across models and benchmarks.
0Knrw0HVz2.main_concern: The visual recency bias may be confounded with ordinary positional attention bias in transformers, and related training-free baselines such as Active-Look and RTWI are not compared.

mAcu7TsIqB.one_liner: Probabilistic forecaster adding a Fourier-phase Gaussian clock to a history-conditioned Gaussian state in an additive latent prior.
mAcu7TsIqB.problem: Normalized histories can look alike at different cycle positions while their future distributions differ, so latent uncertainty models conditioned only on normalized history are 'phase blind'.
mAcu7TsIqB.method: Combines a history-conditioned Gaussian state with a Fourier-phase-conditioned Gaussian clock into an additive latent prior with closed-form mean and variance, decodes non-iteratively with a push-forward decoder mixing lead-time-specific and phase-conditioned mappings, and trains with empirical CRPS or a phase-balanced P-CRPS variant.
mAcu7TsIqB.key_idea: Temporal phase enters the latent prior and decoder additively through a Fourier-phase clock Gaussian, so predictive uncertainty can differ by cycle position.
mAcu7TsIqB.evidence: Seven real-world benchmarks compared with baselines such as PPM, with component ablations, phase-representation comparisons and sensitivity analyses.
mAcu7TsIqB.claimed_gains: not stated; the visible abstract reports improved probabilistic and point forecasting without numbers.
mAcu7TsIqB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the phase-ambiguity motivation is clear, CRPS improves across all seven datasets with non-iterative inference, and the controls and ablations are informative.
mAcu7TsIqB.main_concern: The benefit of the additive state-clock architecture is not isolated from the objective change and phase features, and methodological novelty is limited.

NH3RSAVUZU.one_liner: Learns activation steering maps by matching joint distributions of activations across contiguous layer groups, justified by Kolmogorov's extension theorem.
NH3RSAVUZU.problem: Distinct activation path laws can share identical per-layer marginals, so marginal alignment alone cannot identify the intended path law.
NH3RSAVUZU.method: Builds a Kolmogorov loss that matches joint activation distributions over contiguous groups of layers, and fits steering maps from cached activations without extra forward or backward passes through the pretrained model.
NH3RSAVUZU.key_idea: Matching consistent finite-dimensional joint distributions across layer groups, rather than per-layer marginals, identifies the reference path law.
NH3RSAVUZU.evidence: Theory (weak convergence under kernel conditions, output agreement beyond marginal matching, optimality of the difference-in-means vector among additive maps) and jailbreak and truthfulness experiments on language models from 7B to 31B parameters across several steering map families.
NH3RSAVUZU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation that marginal matching misses cross-layer dependencies is clear, the theory is principled, and fitting on cached activations is computationally attractive.
NH3RSAVUZU.main_concern: The guarantees concern actual intervened trajectories while the practical method fits cached activations, the contribution of cross-layer matching is only partly isolated, and baselines such as LoRA, full fine-tuning and ReFT are missing.

Eru67oe4t0.one_liner: Multi-view reflection separation diffusion framework that routes cross-view information using corrupted geometry, plus the MVRefSep dataset.
Eru67oe4t0.problem: Single-image reflection separation is fundamentally ambiguous, and in multi-view settings the reflections themselves corrupt the geometric correspondences needed to relate views.
Eru67oe4t0.method: GeoRCA establishes cross-view associations from corrupted multi-view geometry, MGR-Diff drives differential generation using the distinct cross-view variations of the consistent transmission and view-dependent reflection layers, and MVRefSep is a new multi-view reflection separation dataset and benchmark.
Eru67oe4t0.key_idea: Geometry-constrained candidate routing with content-dependent attention exploits that transmission is consistent across views while reflection varies, even when geometry is corrupted.
Eru67oe4t0.evidence: Experiments on the new MVRefSep benchmark with component ablations, modulation-direction comparisons and geometric correspondence analyses.
Eru67oe4t0.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract claims the best performance without numbers.
Eru67oe4t0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the multi-view diffusion approach to transmission-reflection separation is well motivated, the experiments are fairly comprehensive, and the MVRefSep dataset is a valuable contribution.
Eru67oe4t0.main_concern: All ablations run on MVRefSep-Test and are used to select default configurations, with no separate validation set, so the reported test results may be optimistic.

GksRP6onZd.one_liner: Generative video codec transmitting per-denoising-step residual segments, compressed by a diffusion-transformer entropy model, to steer denoising toward the source.
GksRP6onZd.problem: Decoder-side diffusion in generative video compression relies on generative priors alone and usually works in latent space, which loses information irreversibly and lacks explicit source constraints.
GksRP6onZd.method: Encodes source pictures with a learned video codec, splits the distortion between reconstruction and source into residual segments, one per denoising step, and compresses them with a residual codec that uses a diffusion transformer as the entropy model, working directly in pixel space.
GksRP6onZd.key_idea: Residuals of the codec reconstruction are acquired and coded at each denoising step, so the decoder is constrained by the source throughout denoising.
GksRP6onZd.evidence: Experiments against previous generative video codecs on benchmarks including MCL-JCV, with component ablations.
GksRP6onZd.claimed_gains: 63.7% and 83.8% BD-rate reductions in LPIPS and PSNR, respectively, compared with the previous best method.
GksRP6onZd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that transmitting residuals to constrain denoising is a meaningful, clean paradigm that outperforms the compared generative codecs, with informative ablations.
GksRP6onZd.main_concern: Missing baselines (the DCVC-UF base codec, GVC-RT, GVC1D, S2VC, VTM-RA) and unreported complexity make the superiority claim hard to confirm, and the 8-frame latency differs from the single-frame-latency baselines.

o9QQ5aTWFw.one_liner: Self-speculative decoding with a weight-quantized sparse-attention drafter, a BF16 LM-head candidate reranker and a margin-aware reducer.
o9QQ5aTWFw.problem: In long-context self-speculative decoding, a sparse-attention drafter still reads target-sized weights, and naive low-bit weight quantization of the drafter degrades acceptance length.
o9QQ5aTWFw.method: Combines a weight-quantized sparse drafter with a Reranker that recomputes candidate logits using BF16 LM-head weights and a margin-aware Reducer that keeps alternatives under a bounded candidate budget, with final verification by the original full-attention BF16 model.
o9QQ5aTWFw.key_idea: Token flips from quantization concentrate at low-margin positions and the BF16 target token stays among the top draft candidates, so reranking a few candidates with a BF16 head recovers acceptance.
o9QQ5aTWFw.evidence: End-to-end speedups under a fixed KV-cache budget against Vegas and vLLM, mainly Qwen3-8B on RULER with batch size times length fixed at 128K, plus error analysis and ablations.
o9QQ5aTWFw.claimed_gains: 1.49x average and 1.53x maximum end-to-end speedups over Vegas, and up to 2.21x over vLLM.
o9QQ5aTWFw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it targets a real weight-side serving bottleneck with clear motivation, preserves the target's greedy outputs, and recovers acceptance at low overhead with the reranker and reducer.
o9QQ5aTWFw.main_concern: Evidence is narrow (mainly Qwen3-8B on RULER at fixed 128K, no mixed-length serving trace) and baselines such as DFlash, EAGLE-3 and a quantized-body-plus-BF16-head ablation are missing.

2iq2rcBQWc.one_liner: Predicts by maximum-entropy expectation over all parameter configurations of a power-law network, with training samples as constraints, in closed form.
2iq2rcBQWc.problem: Conventional training seeks a single parameter configuration, which is underdetermined when the number of parameters exceeds the number of training samples.
2iq2rcBQWc.method: SML computes predictions as expectation values integrating over all parameter configurations, with training samples as constraints in an entropy-maximization process, realized in closed form on a power-law network so that the number of unknowns scales with data size rather than network size.
2iq2rcBQWc.key_idea: Replace one fitted parameter set with the maximum-entropy ensemble average over parameters constrained by the training samples, which is analytically tractable for a power-law network.
2iq2rcBQWc.evidence: Standardized function benchmarks against 19 reference model variants and 848 real-world datasets, with robustness tests to input noise, irrelevant features and contamination.
2iq2rcBQWc.claimed_gains: Ranks first on standardized function benchmarks against 19 reference model variants and outperforms most of them on 848 real-world datasets.
2iq2rcBQWc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, cheap and needs no per-dataset tuning, performs well in the small-sample, high-dimensional regime and is robust to noise.
2iq2rcBQWc.main_concern: The closed form exists only for a power-law network that is linear in its parameters, so claims about general neural networks are untested, and tree models can do better when feature importance differs greatly.

V4YIqL8Vfu.one_liner: Training-free module that resamples action chunks at a requested rate and rescales by directional inconsistency between adjacent actions.
V4YIqL8Vfu.problem: Imitation-learned policies inherit the execution speed of their demonstrations, and test-time speed changes can create unrecoverable out-of-distribution observations that reduce task success.
V4YIqL8Vfu.method: Post-processes action chunks from a frozen pretrained policy by resampling each chunk at the requested rate, then uses directional inconsistency between adjacent actions to adaptively set how closely execution can approach the requested speed.
V4YIqL8Vfu.key_idea: Cosine inconsistency between adjacent actions in a chunk serves as a learning-free signal that limits how far the rescaled speed may approach the requested speed.
V4YIqL8Vfu.evidence: Three policy families and 50 simulated tasks, plus four real-world manipulation tasks.
V4YIqL8Vfu.claimed_gains: Realized execution rates spanning 0.22x to 2.53x while preserving per-task success in simulation, and 94% average real-world success versus the frozen policy's 93.8% at rates from 0.38x to 1.97x.
V4YIqL8Vfu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a simple, retraining-free method with a clear mechanism that keeps success rates higher than baselines at similar speeds across policy families and benchmarks.
V4YIqL8Vfu.main_concern: It is unclear how much the inconsistency gate adds (a fixed factor of 1.2 matches its 95.3% success at slightly lower speed), and realized speed falls short of requested speed and is measured in control steps rather than wall-clock time.

aF08o11NMm.one_liner: Probes residual-stream directions encoding verified task progress in tool-using LLM agents and steers execution when progress deviates.
aF08o11NMm.problem: It is unclear whether long-horizon LLM agents keep an internal task-progress representation that evolves during execution, since prior work examined only explicit outputs or observable behavior.
aF08o11NMm.method: Uses externally verifiable task constraints and matched comparisons to find residual directions reflecting verified progress at an entry point (first token after the latest observation) and a decision point (first answer token after reasoning), traces how they evolve with tool observations, and applies Evidence Assimilation Steering and Evidence Review Steering when progress deviates.
aF08o11NMm.key_idea: Directions that track externally verified progress reveal when evidence is poorly assimilated, and selective steering at those deviations corrects the behavior.
aF08o11NMm.evidence: Held-out tasks with matching by task and turn, same-action and shuffled-label controls and bootstrap uncertainty, plus steering experiments across several models and settings, evaluated on travel planning per reviewers.
aF08o11NMm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is meaningful, the externally grounded progress definition with matched and shuffled-label controls reduces alternative explanations, and steering improves behavior across several models.
aF08o11NMm.main_concern: The progress reference is under-specified and not fully controlled for confounds such as context length, and evaluation is limited to travel planning with near-saturated or near-zero metrics.

b6bSlY0FCC.one_liner: Collaborative 3D detection that converts box-level messages from unseen agents into pseudo-BEV maps and ego-compatible latent features without adaptation.
b6bSlY0FCC.problem: Collaborative perception methods assume fixed or known collaborator encoder configurations, so agents with unseen LiDAR beam counts or encoder architectures that appear after deployment cannot join without adaptation.
b6bSlY0FCC.method: ALF converts auxiliary box-level messages into pseudo-BEV maps and synthesizes ego-compatible latent features by combining object-centric cues with scene context from the ego feature.
b6bSlY0FCC.key_idea: A configuration-independent box message is lifted into the ego feature space using object cues and ego scene context, so no per-configuration adapter is trained.
b6bSlY0FCC.evidence: V2X-Real zero-shot evaluation across 64 case studies, three protocols and four fusion backbones, with same-box controlled comparisons against late fusion.
b6bSlY0FCC.claimed_gains: Outperforms the strongest prior baseline by 35.91% in relative mAP@0.7 across 64 zero-shot case studies while requiring only 120 bytes per agent per frame.
b6bSlY0FCC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the box-message interface is well motivated and communication-efficient and that the systematic zero-shot evaluation with same-box late-fusion controls supports feature-level lifting.
b6bSlY0FCC.main_concern: The net gain over no collaboration appears modest and is not reported for the zero-shot cases, and feature-based baselines may be handicapped by an untrained channel projection.

F3UDkyRPXW.one_liner: Single-stage flow matching DiT generates triangle soups with Laplacian positional encoding injected through RoPE as a connectivity prior.
F3UDkyRPXW.problem: Triangle mesh generators are either slow autoregressive models or multi-stage diffusion pipelines, and naive unordered triangle-soup generation yields duplicated or missing triangles and poor connectivity.
F3UDkyRPXW.method: DeltaFlow trains a Diffusion Transformer with flow matching on unordered triangle soups. It maps each mesh's dual-graph Laplacian coordinates onto a shared template used for rotary position embeddings.
F3UDkyRPXW.key_idea: Dual-graph Laplacian coordinates are mapped onto a shared template and used as RoPE positions, giving the denoiser a connectivity prior without needing the target topology.
F3UDkyRPXW.evidence: Compared against other mesh generative and flow-based methods on 1-NNA, a tightness score, and duplicate-face rate, with mesh inpainting and point-cloud-conditioned generation demos; a reviewer notes training on four ShapeNet categories.
F3UDkyRPXW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the Laplacian positional encoding a simple, well-motivated connectivity prior that targets duplicate and disconnected faces, with strong results over baselines.
F3UDkyRPXW.main_concern: The evaluation is incomplete: no face-orientation or normal-consistency metrics, no Chamfer distance for conditional settings, training on four ShapeNet categories with simple shapes, and the Laplacian template's specific contribution is not isolated.

DBtNko6b1g.one_liner: Training-free rolling forecasting that shifts the previous forecast into a draft, refines it in parallel, and ensembles overlapping forecasts.
DBtNko6b1g.problem: Time-series foundation models decode autoregressively, and rolling forecasting shifts the input window at each step so the previous KV cache cannot be reused.
DBtNko6b1g.method: TempoDraft rebuilds the current context state and computes the first forecast token exactly as in autoregressive decoding, then shifts the previous forecast to form an aligned draft and refines the remaining forecast tokens in parallel. A rolling forecast ensemble combines current and earlier forecasts of the same timestamps.
DBtNko6b1g.key_idea: The previous forecast, shifted to the new window, serves as a self-draft refined in parallel instead of decoding each token sequentially.
DBtNko6b1g.evidence: Evaluation on nine datasets with four transformer TSFM backbones including Timer, comparing accuracy against STRIDE and shift-and-paste and speed against full autoregressive decoding, according to reviews.
DBtNko6b1g.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, training-free, usable with pretrained TSFMs without changing weights, and addresses a practical source of repeated computation, with evaluation across nine datasets and several backbones.
DBtNko6b1g.main_concern: The accuracy-latency comparison with other acceleration methods is incomplete, standard TSFM benchmarks (GiftEval, fev-bench) are missing, and the rolling ensemble and Jacobi-style refinement are questioned as not new.

vxDVTfb1IH.one_liner: Flow-matching co-folding model built only from standard transformers and pretrained protein language model embeddings, without triangle updates.
vxDVTfb1IH.problem: Co-folding models in the AlphaFold lineage depend on bespoke components (pair representations, triangle updates, deep MSA encodings), and it is unclear whether these are required.
vxDVTfb1IH.method: SimpleFold2 embeds sequences with pretrained protein language models and generates structures with a flow-matching generator made only of attention and MLP layers, without triangle updates, template stacks, recycling, or equivariant modules. It is scaled to 3B parameters.
vxDVTfb1IH.key_idea: Frame co-folding as general-purpose flow-matching generation with plain transformer layers over pLM embeddings, dropping pair representations and triangle updates.
vxDVTfb1IH.evidence: Protein-ligand co-folding (Runs N' Poses, OpenBind), monomers, and FoldBench categories, with test-time scaling and runtime and memory comparisons.
vxDVTfb1IH.claimed_gains: The sampler uses approximately 0.3x the memory of AlphaFold-style models and runs 10x faster (abstract cut off), with strong protein-ligand and competitive monomer performance at 3B parameters.
vxDVTfb1IH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the model gives large speed and memory savings and competitive protein-ligand accuracy (68.1% ranked success on Runs N' Poses versus AlphaFold3's 69.7%) without pair or triangle machinery.
vxDVTfb1IH.main_concern: The training cutoff and test separation are undocumented, so low-similarity benchmark claims cannot be trusted, and the ranked results rely on a confidence module that uses triangle updates.

IOTQOHGMiB.one_liner: ECG-EGR represents ECGs as sparse waveform-grounded Events, composed relationally and read by an LLM, with finding-to-Event provenance.
IOTQOHGMiB.problem: Existing ECG models encode signals into latent representations optimized for prediction, leaving the link between representations, localized waveform evidence and clinical findings implicit.
IOTQOHGMiB.method: A sparse, variable-size set of Events is discovered, each with lead-time support, an immutable semantic address and a mutable reasoning state; their semantics are aligned with weak clinical supervision via unbalanced optimal transport, and Event states are composed relationally across time and leads. A language model sees ECG information only through composed Events, and a finding-conditioned retriever links generated findings to source Events and waveform regions.
IOTQOHGMiB.key_idea: Separate an immutable semantic address (evidence localization) from a mutable reasoning state per waveform Event, so grounding persists while relational composition updates context.
IOTQOHGMiB.evidence: Report generation experiments plus Event-level intervention tests (EG-Nec, EG-Suf) and visualizations of provenance.
IOTQOHGMiB.claimed_gains: A BLEU-1 score of 0.876 on report generation (the remaining reported numbers are cut off in the abstract).
IOTQOHGMiB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the clean separation of an immutable semantic address from a mutable reasoning state and the inspectable Event design that makes provenance tracing structurally possible.
IOTQOHGMiB.main_concern: The central provenance claim is not validated against clinician-annotated evidence regions, and the Event-level interventions do not show that retrieved regions actually influenced the generated findings.

FARvuE3ais.one_liner: Characterizes the exposure disparity hidden by checking fairness under finitely many attention curves and designs a robust ranking linear program.
FARvuE3ais.problem: Exposure fairness depends on an attention curve over positions, but the curve used for evaluation may differ from the one users follow, so a score under one or a few curves may not guarantee fairness.
FARvuE3ais.method: The paper defines the blind spot of a finite set of checked curves (the largest exposure disparity that can stay hidden while all checks pass), derives an exact formula for arbitrary targets and multiple overlapping groups, and bounds the number of curves needed for exact checks. It then formulates a robust ranking linear program that maximizes utility while controlling exposure disparity under an unknown attention curve.
FARvuE3ais.key_idea: Compute the worst-case undetected exposure disparity over all attention curves consistent with a finite set of passed checks, and constrain a ranking LP against it.
FARvuE3ais.evidence: An exact formula and bounds, plus experiments on Amazon ESCI, TREC Fair Ranking 2022 and German Credit.
FARvuE3ais.claimed_gains: Policies that are fair under a single logarithmic attention curve are still off target on average by 36%-44% of total attention under some monotone attention curve.
FARvuE3ais.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper poses a meaningful problem and gives a sound, well-structured theoretical characterization of what finite attention-curve checks guarantee.
FARvuE3ais.main_concern: The practical need for the minimum-audit-size result is unclear because all prefix curves can be checked cheaply (k=10-20), and the robust LP is seen as an incremental extension of existing fair-ranking formulations.

MSf236jCJZ.one_liner: Gaussian Splatting for nested transparent scenes: freeze shell Gaussians while refining the interior, then fuse multi-range depth meshes.
MSf236jCJZ.problem: In nested transparent scenes the dominant shell suppresses interior learning, and reducing each ray to a single depth discards weak surfaces or places geometry between interfaces.
MSf236jCJZ.method: Nested refinement fixes shell and background Gaussians and caps the shell's rendering contribution while optimizing the interior; Range-Aware Depth Extraction keeps depths from multiple search ranges for independent TSDF integration, and FUSE keeps all fine triangles and clips the coarse mesh to fragments beyond that coverage.
MSf236jCJZ.key_idea: Cap and freeze the shell so interior Gaussians receive gradient, and extract depth per search range into separate TSDF meshes merged by coverage-based exclusion.
MSf236jCJZ.evidence: Existing transparent-scene benchmarks (alphaSurf, TransLab, ClearPose, DTU per reviews) and the new TransNest, eight synthetic multi-view scenes with separate ground-truth geometry for shell and interior.
MSf236jCJZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the shell-dominance failure mode real and well analyzed, the two-stage strategy and separate shell/interior evaluation on TransNest useful, and results strongest on complex transparent scenes.
MSf236jCJZ.main_concern: Ablations are marginal or entangled (RADE/FUSE differences are small), nested refinement resembles NU-NeRF's outer-then-inner idea, and no real nested transparent captures are evaluated.

lDEbqJFnnw.one_liner: Maps human first-person gaze into the robot view to condition a VLA policy through prompting and action conditioning.
lDEbqJFnnw.problem: Language instructions alone leave the object, interaction location, and mid-execution target changes of interactive manipulation underspecified.
lDEbqJFnnw.method: Gaze2Act maps first-person gaze into the robot's view by cross-view semantic matching, producing an object mask and a gaze point for coarse-to-fine target specification. It feeds these cues into the VLA policy through perception-level prompting and action-level conditioning.
lDEbqJFnnw.key_idea: Ground human gaze in the robot camera via cross-view matching and inject the resulting mask and point into a VLA through visual prompting and action-level conditioning.
lDEbqJFnnw.evidence: 16 real-robot tasks across seven task categories on a Unitree G1 humanoid, with reviews citing a grounding evaluation of 750+ trials and ablations of both conditioning paths.
lDEbqJFnnw.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says Gaze2Act beats the evaluated baselines in intent accuracy and task success rate, without numbers)
lDEbqJFnnw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree gaze is a practical, working interface for specifying object identity and contact location, supported by extensive real-robot trials and ablations.
lDEbqJFnnw.main_concern: Gains are not isolated from the interface (gaze-grounded masks versus language-generated baseline masks) and the policy design, and tests use one robot platform and one VLA backbone.

RTW7caAjTy.one_liner: A single model as generator and reviser; on-policy self-distillation turns binary rewards into dense token-level supervision.
RTW7caAjTy.problem: RLVR gives only sparse binary rewards, while distillation needs external teachers or high-quality demonstrations that are costly or unavailable.
RTW7caAjTy.method: One model plays a Generator that produces an initial response and a Reviser that conditions on that response and its binary reward to produce an improved one. The reviser's token distributions are distilled into the generator through on-policy self-distillation, after a self-revision training warm-up.
RTW7caAjTy.key_idea: Use the model's own revision, conditioned on its attempt and binary reward, as a token-level teacher distribution for its first-attempt generation.
RTW7caAjTy.evidence: Math and code reasoning benchmarks with Qwen3-4B-Instruct and Olmo-3-7B-Instruct, compared with RFT, GRPO, and OPSD under matched budgets.
RTW7caAjTy.claimed_gains: SD-Zero improves performance by at least 10% over the base models and outperforms RFT, GRPO, and OPSD (the rest of the comparison is cut off in the abstract).
RTW7caAjTy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the self-revision idea is interesting and practical, with the highest aggregate accuracy among compared methods, useful controlled comparisons, and clear writing.
RTW7caAjTy.main_concern: The comparison is confounded because SD-Zero gets a rejection-filtered revision warm-up while GRPO is cold-started, and token-level self-localization of errors is not directly shown.

u3SohYBZGH.one_liner: LoreMem indexes streaming video with ranked concepts from a predefined lexicon using frozen encoders, avoiding caption generation.
u3SohYBZGH.problem: Online memory construction for long-form video assistants must keep pace with the stream under a fixed compute budget; when it falls behind, unfinished work accumulates and recent evidence is delayed.
u3SohYBZGH.method: LoreMem is a caption-free multimodal memory: frozen encoders select concepts from a predefined lexicon to index visual observations and dialogue, storing sparse concept identities and ranks, while the original observations are kept for answering.
u3SohYBZGH.key_idea: Index observations by selecting and rank-storing concepts from a predefined lexicon with frozen encoders instead of generating captions, so indexing cost stays bounded.
u3SohYBZGH.evidence: QA on completed indexes across four video QA benchmarks against caption memory, plus a workload evaluation using construction times measured on a Galaxy S26 Ultra over six hours of 30-second arrivals.
u3SohYBZGH.claimed_gains: 52.0% average accuracy, 7.9 percentage points above Qwen3-VL-4B caption memory, and no backlog accumulation over six hours of 30-second arrivals on a Galaxy S26 Ultra.
u3SohYBZGH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem relevant and the method simple, training-free, and effective, with consistent gains across benchmarks and mobile-device measurements showing no construction backlog.
u3SohYBZGH.main_concern: QA is evaluated only on fully built indexes with construction latency measured separately, and baselines omit streaming and memory methods such as Flash-VStream and Dispider.

z1CFFUEfzF.one_liner: Early-fusion multimodal autoregressive text-to-image models trained from scratch on 100M image-text pairs, without language pretraining.
z1CFFUEfzF.problem: Modern text-to-image systems rely on internet-scale language pretraining, and it is unclear whether such pretraining is necessary for strong generation.
z1CFFUEfzF.method: Xanthus is a family of early-fusion multimodal autoregressive models pretrained entirely from scratch on GPIC, a dataset of 100M image-text pairs. Controlled data composition and scheduling experiments test whether external text-only pretraining helps, and the same models also learn image captioning from the paired data.
z1CFFUEfzF.key_idea: Train a single early-fusion autoregressive model jointly on image-text pairs from scratch, replacing a separately pretrained language encoder.
z1CFFUEfzF.evidence: Comparisons with LlamaGen-XL/8 and JiT-T2I-XXL/8++ on gFD using GPIC, with data composition and scheduling ablations across five model sizes.
z1CFFUEfzF.claimed_gains: Xanthus-0.52B scores 48.0 vs 63.5 gFD for LlamaGen-XL/8 with 18.2x less pretraining compute, and Xanthus-1.6B scores 35.3 vs 43.2 gFD for JiT-T2I-XXL/8++ with 275x less pretraining compute.
z1CFFUEfzF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the substantial controlled experiments (five model sizes, data composition and scheduling ablations) and the strengthened, compute-transparent baselines.
z1CFFUEfzF.main_concern: Evaluation is mostly in-distribution gFD on GPIC without standard benchmarks such as GenEval or DPG-Bench or prompt-adherence tests, so the broad claim that language pretraining is unnecessary is not established.

BmXzqYwtwC.one_liner: Models honey bee colony dynamics with an interpretable ODE system derived from first principles with entomologists, plus stability analysis.
BmXzqYwtwC.problem: Colony behavior must be modeled, forecast, and understood from sparse, noisy measurements by methods that domain experts accept as explainable, fast, and accurate.
BmXzqYwtwC.method: A dynamical system of differential equations with few interpretable parameters (foraging rate, mortality rate, and others), fitted to hive data, with stability analysis.
BmXzqYwtwC.key_idea: Write colony dynamics as first-principles differential equations whose few parameters have direct biological meaning, so fitting yields interpretable forecasts.
BmXzqYwtwC.evidence: Experiments on the largest available real-hive dataset, with fitted parameters transferred to new colonies; reviews note comparisons against black-box deep-learning methods.
BmXzqYwtwC.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract claims good accuracy on the largest available hive dataset, linear scaling in input size, and good forecasts for new colonies from fitted parameters.
BmXzqYwtwC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the biologically motivated, interpretable model whose parameters support equilibrium analysis and intervention simulation, applied to a real sparse and noisy forecasting problem.
BmXzqYwtwC.main_concern: Methodological clarity and validation are insufficient: unexplained confidence intervals, sparse data-collection detail, mostly graphical comparisons, and a questioned omission of larval loss in the population flows.

ZMZN292Xwv.one_liner: SGF adds margin regularization and hierarchical boosting to generative feedback for fine-grained CLIP perception with far fewer training samples.
ZMZN292Xwv.problem: Generative feedback for CLIP needs heavy data and compute because projected representations can collapse toward a constant and single-level supervision wastes hierarchical information, while naive multi-level supervision causes conflicting gradients.
ZMZN292Xwv.method: Margin regularization requires matched conditions to give lower reconstruction loss than mismatched ones by a positive margin. Hierarchical boosting adds coarse-to-fine supervision progressively while retaining earlier objectives so they stabilize before finer levels are introduced.
ZMZN292Xwv.key_idea: Require matched conditions to beat mismatched ones in reconstruction loss by a margin, and phase in coarse-to-fine supervision levels progressively.
ZMZN292Xwv.evidence: Experiments across six CLIP backbones; reviews cite MMVP-VLM and multimodal QA results plus component ablations.
ZMZN292Xwv.claimed_gains: Reports top fine-grained perception using only 84K training samples, at least 82% fewer than prior methods, with a 5.8-9.1x training speedup over the fastest competitor.
ZMZN292Xwv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the low training cost (about 4 GPU hours with 84K samples) is practically useful and that the two components address concrete, empirically supported issues such as projector collapse.
ZMZN292Xwv.main_concern: Controls are incomplete: baselines are not compared under the same 84K-sample budget (their GPU hours are extrapolated), the hierarchical-boosting ablation lacks all-level joint training and schedule variants, and preservation of original classification and retrieval ability is not reported.

uM8g3d6hvG.one_liner: Event-conditioned residual adapters repair internal visual tokens in frozen vision-language encoders for low-light understanding.
uM8g3d6hvG.problem: Pixel-space low-light restoration does not directly recover the visual representations needed for correct language-model answers.
uM8g3d6hvG.method: ECLAR uses synchronized events to repair RGB patch states through four residual adapters aligned with paired clean representations. It retains pretrained readout modules and the visual token count, requiring only low-light RGB and events at inference.
uM8g3d6hvG.key_idea: Align event-conditioned residual repairs of intermediate RGB patch states with clean-image representations inside a frozen visual encoder.
uM8g3d6hvG.evidence: Training uses SEE-600K, and SDE-VQA-Bench evaluates 8,357 reviewed questions on 1,838 frames from 91 sequences with Qwen3-VL-2B and InternVL2.5-2B.
uM8g3d6hvG.claimed_gains: ECLAR reaches 0.7817 clean-token cosine similarity, improves Qwen3-VL-2B Macro by 11.91 points, exceeds the strongest cascade by 4.19 points, recovers 57.2% of the degradation gap, adds 2.58 points over RGB-only control, and improves InternVL2.5-2B by 4.41 points.
uM8g3d6hvG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value parameter-efficient repair of internal visual representations while preserving the frozen model's native interface.
uM8g3d6hvG.main_concern: Reviewers repeatedly request controlled ablations to isolate the contributions of repair locations, supervision objectives, and architectural choices.

sDFSMIesla.one_liner: Finite-sample and Pass@k bounds explain how on-policy distillation can improve single-sample accuracy while reducing multi-sample success.
sDFSMIesla.problem: On-policy distillation lacks a clear account of generalization under prefix-distribution shift and performance at larger sampling budgets.
sDFSMIesla.method: The paper derives generalization upper and lower bounds involving empirical loss, sample size, student description length, and prefix shift. It bounds student-teacher Pass@k gaps and constructs a KL proximal update that improves Pass@1 while suppressing correct responses on harder prompts.
sDFSMIesla.key_idea: Analyze how prefix-distribution shift and teacher preferences redistribute correct-response probability across easy and hard prompts.
sDFSMIesla.evidence: Finite-sample bounds, matching-order small-KL Pass@k bounds, synthetic experiments, and language-model experiments support the analysis.
sDFSMIesla.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the lower-bound treatment of unseen prefixes and the formal explanation of improving Pass@1 alongside declining Pass@k.
sDFSMIesla.main_concern: Reviewers question the theory's practical applicability because its assumptions can yield loose bounds and the LLM experiments weakly validate the predicted mechanism.

yKeV07wo27.one_liner: Student-only participation-ratio constraints regularize intermediate visual-token dimensionality during vision-language embedding distillation.
yKeV07wo27.problem: Compact vision-language embedding students can lose intermediate token dimensionality during distillation despite output-level alignment.
yKeV07wo27.method: CRED constrains selected student layers' participation ratios to remain at least as high as the initial hidden state's ratio. It combines this scalar spectral regularizer with output-level distillation and approximates participation ratios through random projections.
yKeV07wo27.key_idea: Penalize intermediate student participation ratios below the initial-state ratio without matching teacher activations.
yKeV07wo27.evidence: MMEB evaluations include two student architectures, out-of-distribution results, and ablations of the regularizer and its estimation.
yKeV07wo27.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the student-only scalar regularizer simple and practical because it avoids intermediate teacher features and layer matching.
yKeV07wo27.main_concern: Reviewers question whether preserving participation ratio justifies claims about preserving effective rank or useful semantic information.

DNh5I1QPKw.one_liner: Neutral-relative shared expression codes let rig-specific predictors reuse learned control mappings across heterogeneous facial rigs.
DNh5I1QPKw.problem: Direct facial-control regression requires a separate mapping for each source-target rig direction.
DNh5I1QPKw.method: RetargetingFace compares expressive renders with matched neutral renders and aligns expression codes across rigs by action and strength. Each target predictor trains once on its own rig's codes and controls, then decodes codes from other rigs.
DNh5I1QPKw.key_idea: Align neutral-relative expression codes across rigs so independently trained target-control decoders accept multiple source rigs.
DNh5I1QPKw.evidence: A GNM-generated dataset contains 532 FLAME and ARKit expression states, with human evaluations on held-out transfers, externally captured expressions, and GNM or MHR transfers.
DNh5I1QPKw.claimed_gains: Predictors exceed Direct MLP by 0.16 mean human-rating points in each FLAME↔ARKit direction on a 1–3 scale, with gains over the strongest evaluated prior methods averaging 18.7% on these transfers and 9.9% on externally captured expressions.
DNh5I1QPKw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find shared expression representations and reusable target predictors sensible, with human evaluations supporting cross-rig transfer.
DNh5I1QPKw.main_concern: Multiple reviewers warn that evaluating with the method's own embedding space can favor its predictions and weaken comparison independence.

zW1rC1dm94.one_liner: Encoding analyses map backpropagated gradients onto fMRI and MEG to compare model learning signals with brain hierarchies.
zW1rC1dm94.problem: It remains unclear whether backpropagated gradients follow the spatial and temporal brain correspondence observed for forward activations.
zW1rC1dm94.method: The paper extends neural encoding analyses to use backpropagated gradients as predictors of brain responses to natural images. It compares gradient computation order and spatial organization with human cortical and temporal hierarchies.
zW1rC1dm94.key_idea: Fit brain-response encoding models to backpropagated gradients and compare their spatial and temporal alignment across network depth.
zW1rC1dm94.evidence: Analyses use human fMRI and MEG recordings, focus on DINOv3, and reproduce findings across eight vision models.
zW1rC1dm94.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value testing correspondence between model learning signals and brain activity beyond conventional forward-representation comparisons.
zW1rC1dm94.main_concern: Reviewers question interpreting gradient-brain correspondence as evidence about biological backpropagation because model objectives, neural measurements, and biological timing differ.

13xkLFO9wB.one_liner: Information-geometry analysis and estimate-and-track acquisition optimize fine versus coarse supervision when aggregation weights are unknown.
13xkLFO9wB.problem: Unknown aggregation changes which response directions coarse labels identify, complicating annotation-cost tradeoffs for recovering full responses.
13xkLFO9wB.method: The paper characterizes the information geometry of expensive vector labels and cheaper scalar aggregates with unknown weights. An estimate-and-track policy learns the aggregation rule and follows the optimal resolution mix, with a closed-form break-even condition.
13xkLFO9wB.key_idea: Estimate unknown aggregation weights and track the fine-coarse label allocation determined by identifiable information and annotation cost.
13xkLFO9wB.evidence: Theory establishes optimal leading cumulative risk with a matching local asymptotic minimax lower bound, while synthetic experiments test acquisition transitions and oracle-share convergence.
13xkLFO9wB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the interpretable characterization of information lost through unknown aggregation and when coarse supervision becomes worthwhile.
13xkLFO9wB.main_concern: Reviewers question practical generalization because the theory relies on idealized linear assumptions and validation uses only synthetic settings.

ERJvJesEvQ.one_liner: Marginal-preserving rollout coupling uses lattice sampling for inference coverage and stratified sampling for reinforcement-learning efficiency.
ERJvJesEvQ.problem: Independent language-model rollouts ignore a large design space of dependent samplers with different coverage and learning properties.
ERJvJesEvQ.method: The paper characterizes how different joint rollout distributions preserve model marginals while changing test-time coverage and reinforcement-learning behavior. It compares lattice, stratified, and token-level Sobol sampling with independent sampling.
ERJvJesEvQ.key_idea: Couple parallel rollouts through structured sampling schemes while preserving each rollout's marginal language-model distribution.
ERJvJesEvQ.evidence: Theoretical analysis accompanies experiments across four controlled reasoning benchmarks and reinforcement-learning evaluations.
ERJvJesEvQ.claimed_gains: Lattice sampling matches i.i.d. pass@k with 25–47% fewer rollouts, while stratified sampling matches i.i.d. reinforcement-learning performance with 34.5%–59.2% fewer training steps.
ERJvJesEvQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the systematic theoretical and empirical comparison of rollout-coupling strategies.
ERJvJesEvQ.main_concern: Reviewers regard the methodological contribution as limited because the samplers and several analytical tools build on established prior constructions.

4ZknweRfcV.one_liner: Object-mask grounding evaluates vision SAE features, while pairwise visual separation probes whether feature splits reflect visual specialization.
4ZknweRfcV.problem: Concept prediction and peak localization do not establish whether sparse-autoencoder features activate across the objects they represent.
4ZknweRfcV.method: PACO-SAE treats concept grounding as semantic segmentation using exhaustive PACO-LVIS annotations and separate feature-selection and test splits. Pairwise Visual Separation compares between-group and within-group visual variation to examine feature splitting without subclass labels.
4ZknweRfcV.key_idea: Evaluate entire feature activation regions against object masks and compare visual variation between objects assigned to different features.
4ZknweRfcV.evidence: Experiments cover 63 object concepts, four SAE families, four sparsity levels, and a human study of 200 feature pairs.
4ZknweRfcV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the carefully constructed object-level benchmark for exposing gaps between concept prediction, localization, and spatial grounding.
4ZknweRfcV.main_concern: Reviewers repeatedly note that evaluation on one DINOv3 backbone and layer limits generalization to other visual representations.

tWQgUn6nze.one_liner: Ablations and operator theory show Transolver's slice self-attention is dispensable while streaming FlashSlice accelerates essential slice-deslice global mixing.
tWQgUn6nze.problem: The mechanisms driving Transolver's PDE accuracy—token self-attention among physics slices versus global slice/deslice point mixing—are poorly isolated, while materializing slice-weight tensors limits memory efficiency.
tWQgUn6nze.method: Through ablations across nine 3D CFD benchmarks and averaging neural operator theory, the authors show that replacing slice-token self-attention with a constant linear map preserves accuracy because slice/deslice mixing plus pointwise MLPs suffices for universal approximation. They also build FlashSlice, a FlashAttention-style streaming kernel that computes slice and deslice over mesh points without materializing the slice-weight tensor.
tWQgUn6nze.key_idea: Replace Transolver's slice-token self-attention with a constant linear map while retaining repeated slice/deslice global mixing computed via a streaming FlashSlice GPU kernel.
tWQgUn6nze.evidence: Supported by universal approximation proofs via averaging neural operators and controlled ablations across nine 3D fluid dynamics benchmarks with up to 1.3e8 points per sample.
tWQgUn6nze.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers unanimously praise the large-scale, carefully controlled ablations across nine 3D fluid dynamics benchmarks isolating global slice/deslice coupling as the primary driver of accuracy.
tWQgUn6nze.main_concern: Reviewers note that the headline empirical finding—that token self-attention in Transolver can be removed without losing accuracy—was already reported by Hu et al. (2026).

yM2G5gPY6k.one_liner: Background and 940-nm near-infrared priors disentangle illumination disturbances before gated RGB-NIR cross-attention for remote photoplethysmography.
yM2G5gPY6k.problem: Illumination variations overwhelm subtle facial pulse signals in rPPG, and direct fusion of raw RGB and near-infrared features still propagates illumination disturbances into heart-rate predictions.
yM2G5gPY6k.method: NIRP-Net performs prior-guided feature disentanglement using 940-nm low-irradiance and physiology-irrelevant background priors to suppress illumination disturbances in RGB and NIR representations, then applies gated cross-attention to aggregate complementary NIR cues. The authors also introduce FaceIVL, an RGB-NIR facial rPPG dataset recorded under controlled illumination variations.
yM2G5gPY6k.key_idea: Suppress illumination interference in RGB and NIR facial features using background and 940-nm low-irradiance priors before fusing complementary NIR cues via gated cross-attention.
yM2G5gPY6k.evidence: Evaluated on public RGB-NIR rPPG datasets and the newly collected FaceIVL dataset under controlled illumination variations.
yM2G5gPY6k.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating background-estimated lighting disturbances prior to adaptive gated RGB-NIR fusion is well motivated and improves heart-rate accuracy under lighting variations.
yM2G5gPY6k.main_concern: Reviewers cite missing experimental details (including validation splits, baseline input modalities, and FaceIVL lighting and release specifications) and lack of direct proof that subtracted features isolate illumination.

7vCv12dD04.one_liner: MiraBench tests robotic world models for physical consistency, action following, and predicted failure under perturbed actions.
7vCv12dD04.problem: Visual fidelity benchmarks do not establish whether robotic world models follow actions or predict failures when actions should fail.
7vCv12dD04.method: MiraBench separates action-conditioned reliability into Physics Adherence, Action-Following Fidelity, and Optimism Bias Detection. A human-annotated corpus supports evaluation of physical consistency, task-relevant action conditioning, and responses to failure-inducing actions.
7vCv12dD04.key_idea: Evaluate action-conditioned predictions through separate physical, action-following, and failure-sensitive judgments instead of visual fidelity alone.
7vCv12dD04.evidence: The benchmark evaluates 12 model configurations across conditioning types and model scales using over 16,000 human judgments.
7vCv12dD04.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value failure-sensitive world-model evaluation and the structured human annotations spanning multiple model configurations.
7vCv12dD04.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the proposed action perturbations actually cause failure, since execution-based validation is missing.

OglkXtVrvd.one_liner: GRIFDIR represents graph convolution kernels as finite element functions for diffusion over irregular meshes and arbitrary domains.
OglkXtVrvd.problem: Function-space diffusion backbones often favor regular grids and fail to preserve their theoretical advantages on complex domain topologies.
OglkXtVrvd.method: GRIFDIR expresses generalized graph convolution kernels as finite element functions. Its score network operates directly on unstructured meshes to model function-valued data across domain shapes and resolutions.
OglkXtVrvd.key_idea: Parameterize graph convolution kernels with finite element functions so the diffusion score operator acts directly on unstructured meshes.
OglkXtVrvd.evidence: Unconditional and conditional sampling experiments cover non-convex and multiply-connected geometries, with operator formalization and component, kernel, and radius ablations noted in reviews.
OglkXtVrvd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the mathematical grounding and resolution-transfer capability of the mesh-based diffusion architecture.
OglkXtVrvd.main_concern: Reviewers find the contribution over existing spline convolutions, quadrature-weighted operators, and related function-space diffusion architectures insufficiently distinguished.

tVwgDa3iMp.one_liner: Masked Flood complexes encode protein dynamics through persistent homology, supporting kinetic embeddings and generative ensemble modeling.
tVwgDa3iMp.problem: Static protein representations struggle to capture the conformational dynamics that determine protein function.
tVwgDa3iMp.method: A protein-specific masked Flood complex emphasizes inter-residue structure before persistent-homology diagrams are vectorized into shared coordinates. Time-lagged embeddings support Markov state models that guide training of the MarS-FM generative framework.
tVwgDa3iMp.key_idea: Apply residue-informed masking to a Flood complex, then vectorize persistent homology across conformations to learn shared structural and kinetic representations.
tVwgDa3iMp.evidence: Molecular-dynamics studies probe structural variability, kinetic information through Markov state models, and downstream MarS-FM ensemble statistics.
tVwgDa3iMp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the use of protein-informed persistent homology for structure and dynamics well motivated.
tVwgDa3iMp.main_concern: Reviewers find masking's incremental benefit unclear because it does not consistently outperform the original Flood complex or alternative persistent-homology constructions.

FT6beCc5Ju.one_liner: Gated Recurrent Transformers modulate shared transformer layers with elementwise gates conditioned on hidden states, prelude outputs, and noise.
FT6beCc5Ju.problem: Distinct transformer layers consume memory, while uniform depth sharing can reduce representational diversity and modeling quality.
FT6beCc5Ju.method: GRT repeatedly applies a shared transformer core with a lightweight projection and elementwise update gate. The gate conditions on the hidden state, a fixed prelude output, and freshly sampled noise to specialize each recurrence.
FT6beCc5Ju.key_idea: Condition elementwise recurrent updates on hidden states, fixed prelude features, and resampled noise so shared layers perform different transformations across depth.
FT6beCc5Ju.evidence: Comparisons span three GPT-2 scales and nine scale-by-budget cells, with isoFLOPS and isoPARAMS settings and component ablations.
FT6beCc5Ju.claimed_gains: Under the stated isoFLOPS constraint, a 3-layer GRT matches a 12-layer GPT-2 Small, while the isoPARAMS setting reports 2.76 validation loss versus 2.84 for a non-recurrent counterpart.
FT6beCc5Ju.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple gating design and ablations showing improvements over conventional recurrent weight sharing.
FT6beCc5Ju.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the isoFLOPS comparisons actually match training compute, given variable recurrence depth and additional forward FLOPs.

uBUEHestUS.one_liner: D4R separates local outlier correction from global low-rank regression using a distributed surrogate loss.
uBUEHestUS.problem: Outliers and distribution across machines complicate efficient estimation of shared low-rank structure in multivariate data.
uBUEHestUS.method: D4R constructs a refined separable surrogate loss that decouples local outlier correction from global reduced-rank coefficient estimation. Its distributed updates reduce computation and communication while supporting non-asymptotic coefficient-error analysis.
uBUEHestUS.key_idea: Use a separable surrogate to perform outlier correction locally and aggregate information for global low-rank coefficient updates.
uBUEHestUS.evidence: Non-asymptotic bounds establish the target statistical rate after finite communication rounds, supported by simulations and real-data studies.
uBUEHestUS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clean estimator decomposition and coefficient-error guarantees within their assumptions.
uBUEHestUS.main_concern: Reviewers find communication and computational efficiency claims insufficiently supported by quantified comparisons with competing or efficiently implemented centralized methods.

BiEg8snWxe.one_liner: SOLO shares a delayed, read-only terminal readout across locally trained modules without propagating gradients between modules.
BiEg8snWxe.problem: Backpropagation locks layer updates and retains activations, while private local-learning readouts lose coordination with deeper modules.
BiEg8snWxe.method: SOLO replaces module-specific readouts with a shared, read-only copy of the final module's readout from the previous step. Each module trains locally using this common output map without inter-module gradients or update locking.
BiEg8snWxe.key_idea: Copy the previous terminal readout into every local module to transmit downstream information while keeping backward passes independent.
BiEg8snWxe.evidence: Quality experiments pretrain 340M–2B Transformers on 15B tokens and include readout ablations; reviews identify a separate 96-layer synthetic-token throughput experiment.
BiEg8snWxe.claimed_gains: SOLO stays within one point of backpropagation in average zero-shot accuracy, reduces per-stage activation storage from O(p) to O(1) micro-batches, and reports up to 1.44× the best measured pipeline throughput.
BiEg8snWxe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find sharing the terminal readout a simple, well-motivated way to improve coordination and quality in local learning.
BiEg8snWxe.main_concern: Reviewers agree that separate quality and throughput settings do not establish an end-to-end efficiency advantage at matched model quality or training compute.

Cqe6TPvEWi.one_liner: GazeME learns prompt marker embeddings that emphasize target objects and suppress others using relative visual saliency.
Cqe6TPvEWi.problem: Text-to-image controls specify object appearance and location but offer limited control over relative visual attention among objects.
Cqe6TPvEWi.method: GazeME surrounds object descriptions with learnable saliency markers while keeping the generative model frozen. A saliency-semantics dataset and Saliency Prior Marker Activation train markers through stochastic activation based on relative object saliency, with automatic insertion at inference.
Cqe6TPvEWi.key_idea: Learn focus and suppression marker embeddings through stochastic activation informed by relative saliency across objects.
Cqe6TPvEWi.evidence: Experiments assess target saliency, semantic alignment, and image quality, with reviews describing AAM-based evaluation and a TranSalNet cross-check.
Cqe6TPvEWi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate control of object prominence and the lightweight optimization of marker embeddings with a frozen generator.
Cqe6TPvEWi.main_concern: Reviewers question evaluation independence because AAM supplies both training labels and the main saliency metric, while gains under an alternative evaluator are smaller.

fLQTnYHLzK.one_liner: ForceStereo calibrates disparity hypotheses and uses reliability-conditioned Neural ODE evolution to regulate observation influence on depth states.
fLQTnYHLzK.problem: Aggregate stereo accuracy can hide large errors in regions with unreliable observations, contaminating downstream 3D geometry.
fLQTnYHLzK.method: ForceStereo first calibrates ambiguous disparity hypotheses using scene-level context before forming a depth state. It then uses residuals, hypothesis ambiguity, and structural information to condition a Neural ODE that controls observation influence during disparity evolution.
fLQTnYHLzK.key_idea: Use reliability conditions to regulate how observations drive disparity-state evolution instead of directly converting residuals into disparity corrections.
fLQTnYHLzK.evidence: Experiments include ETH3D, KITTI 2012 and KITTI 2015, zero-shot settings, and component ablations.
fLQTnYHLzK.claimed_gains: ForceStereo reports up to 16.0% error reduction on ETH3D leaderboards and up to 25.3% zero-shot error reduction over prior best results.
fLQTnYHLzK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find reliability-aware stereo inference well motivated and recognize strong benchmark performance with supporting ablations.
fLQTnYHLzK.main_concern: Reviewers flag missing comparisons with strong recent stereo methods, particularly WAFT-Stereo.

pM6Z8yK7du.one_liner: NeST-KD forms shared teacher-neighborhood subgraphs and matches teacher-student conditional similarity distributions over them.
pM6Z8yK7du.problem: Random batches miss close teacher neighbors, while grouping neighbors alone fails to convey their graded teacher-defined similarities.
pM6Z8yK7du.method: NeST-KD retrieves teacher-space neighbors of seed texts to form a shared mini-batch subgraph, then matches teacher and student conditional similarity distributions. An auxiliary objective matches seed-to-pool similarity distributions and reuses eligible non-seed texts for supervision.
pM6Z8yK7du.key_idea: Transfer graded teacher similarities over shared neighborhood subgraphs instead of treating neighbor co-occurrence as sufficient supervision.
pM6Z8yK7du.evidence: Nine sentence-embedding datasets evaluate 66M and 22M MiniLM students, with controlled studies and same-pool ablations testing similarity supervision.
pM6Z8yK7du.claimed_gains: NeST-KD improves over the strongest baseline by 1.18 and 2.64 absolute points for the 66M and 22M MiniLM students, respectively.
pM6Z8yK7du.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clear motivation and central idea, with empirical comparisons and controlled ablations supporting the proposed similarity supervision.
pM6Z8yK7du.main_concern: Reviewers question cost comparability because expanded neighbor pools increase student computation and teacher embedding and neighbor-mining preprocessing costs are incompletely reported.

MOenIuYptM.one_liner: SWE Refactor Bench combines migration audits, fixed behavioral tests, and agent-generated counterexamples to evaluate whole-repository stack migration.
MOenIuYptM.problem: Behavior-only coding benchmarks can accept unchanged or copied implementations without verifying that a requested migration occurred.
MOenIuYptM.method: The benchmark covers whole-repository migrations and evaluates them through migration audits, fixed behavioral tests, and targeted tests generated by six independent coding agents. These stages assess both migration completeness and preservation of behavior.
MOenIuYptM.key_idea: Verify stack replacement separately from behavior, then search for hidden behavioral differences using independent coding agents.
MOenIuYptM.evidence: Evaluation includes 20 migrations across 4 kinds of technical debt and 520 runs from 8 models under 26 model-effort configurations.
MOenIuYptM.claimed_gains: Only 28 of 520 runs (5.4%) pass all stages, 13 of the 20 tasks have no accepted solution, and the best model, claude-opus-5, scores 47.0/100.
MOenIuYptM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the substantial migration tasks and the three-stage protocol's explicit distinction between completed migration and behavior preservation.
MOenIuYptM.main_concern: Reviewers question leaderboard reliability because acceptance depends strongly on the verifier panel and may also reflect single-run randomness.

EHWcKSfn8r.one_liner: FreeCHROMA conditions video diffusion on unaligned background references and trains joint compositing and harmonization with pseudo-paired monocular videos.
EHWcKSfn8r.problem: Existing compositing workflows constrain background choice and camera motion through aligned backgrounds, edited first frames, or separate harmonization.
EHWcKSfn8r.method: FreeCHROMA adapts a pretrained video diffusion model using one to three unaligned background references and optional text instructions. Pseudo-paired supervision from separated and augmented monocular videos trains foreground integration and harmonization within one generation process.
EHWcKSfn8r.key_idea: Train reference-conditioned video diffusion on pseudo-paired foreground-background data to jointly generate the environment and harmonize the foreground.
EHWcKSfn8r.evidence: Reviewers cite ablations showing that foreground illumination perturbation and background viewpoint augmentation improve harmonization and camera-trajectory consistency.
EHWcKSfn8r.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the practical compositing setting and the value of scalable pseudo-paired supervision for joint composition and harmonization.
EHWcKSfn8r.main_concern: Reviewers question evidence of background-reference control given unclear reference construction and same-video training that may permit residual-lighting shortcuts.

U49pujdOST.one_liner: Retrieving futures after similar histories, LAMP combines memory evidence with parametric predictions for time-series anomaly prediction.
U49pujdOST.problem: Forecasting favors normal trajectories and can smooth away rare abnormal dynamics needed for point-level anomaly prediction.
U49pujdOST.method: LAMP retrieves previously observed futures associated with similar historical windows from a multi-scale memory. It adaptively combines these futures with parametric predictions.
U49pujdOST.key_idea: Retrieve futures linked to similar historical patterns and adaptively fuse them with parametric predictions.
U49pujdOST.evidence: Experiments compare LAMP with 16 baselines on five multivariate time-series benchmarks, with reviews noting horizon comparisons, ablations, and efficiency analysis.
U49pujdOST.claimed_gains: The abstract reports average gains of 6.71% in V-PR and 9.37% in V-ROC, training up to 8.2× faster with 14.0× lower GPU memory usage.
U49pujdOST.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the practical motivation and reported prediction gains with a lightweight architecture.
U49pujdOST.main_concern: Reviewers find insufficient direct evidence or explanation that the proposed mechanisms preserve abnormal dynamics and produce early warnings.

32j2BsJSc9.one_liner: MLLM object tokens prompt few-shot segmentation on VastFSS, a benchmark spanning 2,400 categories.
32j2BsJSc9.problem: Existing few-shot segmentation benchmarks cover too few categories or domains to assess broad generalization.
32j2BsJSc9.method: VastFSS collects 104K images across 2,400 classes in natural and specialized domains. MA-FSS extracts support-target representations through learnable MLLM object tokens, using mask-guided attention and an adaptive token gate to prompt query segmentation.
32j2BsJSc9.key_idea: Learnable object tokens extract foreground representations from support images through mask-guided MLLM attention and serve as segmentation prompts.
32j2BsJSc9.evidence: Reviewers report comparisons with prior few-shot segmentation methods on VastFSS and improved performance for MA-FSS.
32j2BsJSc9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the benchmark's broad category and domain coverage for evaluating generalizable few-shot segmentation.
32j2BsJSc9.main_concern: Benchmark validation remains insufficient, with reviewers questioning semantic independence of evaluation splits and quantitative annotation quality.

vTPKOmuzFp.one_liner: Teacher debate supplies confidence-weighted token supervision on student trajectories for agentic and code distillation.
vTPKOmuzFp.problem: A single teacher can reinforce mistakes shared with its student, especially across long agentic trajectories.
vTPKOmuzFp.method: MAD-OPD uses teacher debate transcripts and confidence scores to weight token-level supervision at student-visited states. OPAD applies this stepwise to sampled tool actions, with Jensen–Shannon divergence for agentic tasks and reverse KL for code.
vTPKOmuzFp.key_idea: Teachers debate at student-visited states, then weight token-level distillation losses by confidence in their transcript-conditioned evaluations.
vTPKOmuzFp.evidence: Experiments cover six Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 teacher–student configurations on five agentic and code benchmarks, with divergence ablations and supervision controls.
vTPKOmuzFp.claimed_gains: For Qwen3 14B+8B→4B, the abstract reports gains of 4.39 points in agentic average and 4.24 points in code average, with the comparator truncated.
vTPKOmuzFp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the motivation for addressing shared teacher–student errors and the breadth of experimental evaluation.
vTPKOmuzFp.main_concern: Reviewers question whether gains hold against stronger alternatives under matched teacher-side computational budgets.

OVv0pXajLf.one_liner: Distribution-derived motion masks restrict Gaussian updates to suppress flicker in streaming 3D reconstruction.
OVv0pXajLf.problem: Per-frame optimization can mistake static-background noise for motion, causing unnecessary Gaussian updates and temporal flicker.
OVv0pXajLf.method: FS-GStream estimates frame-specific motion thresholds from distributions of log-transformed Gaussian translation magnitudes. Mask-guided optimization refines dynamic geometry and appearance while preserving static geometry and selectively updating static appearance.
OVv0pXajLf.key_idea: Threshold Gaussian translations using their frame-wise distribution, then apply different geometry and appearance updates to static and dynamic Gaussians.
OVv0pXajLf.evidence: Reviews describe evaluation on 3DGStream, HiCoM, and ReCon-GS across twelve backbone–dataset pairs, with reconstruction, temporal-consistency, and ablation results.
OVv0pXajLf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit consistent reconstruction and temporal-stability gains across backbones and the module's ease of integration.
OVv0pXajLf.main_concern: The evaluation omits closely related selective-update and flicker-suppression methods, leaving comparative advantages unclear.

AKiLxLXCPi.one_liner: Preview diagnosis and edits to cached generation trajectories correct video failures before completing the selected candidate.
AKiLxLXCPi.problem: Iterative text-to-video correction repeats full generation and can disrupt content that was already correct.
AKiLxLXCPi.method: PreCoG uses PreQA to diagnose semantic failures from inexpensive previews and construct corrective conditions. PreEdit edits cached trajectories while attenuating orthogonal changes, and only the selected candidate proceeds to full generation.
AKiLxLXCPi.key_idea: Diagnose preview failures, edit cached trajectories under corrective conditions, and finish generation only for the selected candidate.
AKiLxLXCPi.evidence: Experiments on Wan2.2 compare quality and alignment with VSR and GENMAC, while reviews discuss preview-to-final agreement measurements.
AKiLxLXCPi.claimed_gains: The abstract reports the highest compared VBench score, near-VSR prompt alignment at 0.56× its inference time, and better performance than GENMAC on all three quality and alignment metrics at 0.86× its inference time.
AKiLxLXCPi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation for preview-based correction and cached-trajectory reuse reasonable.
AKiLxLXCPi.main_concern: Reviewers question whether edited previews reliably predict final-video correctness, especially under the deployed evaluation configuration.

ykf6rUHIcg.one_liner: Adaptive kernel matching and spatial-feature propagation localize defects in industrial point clouds.
ykf6rUHIcg.problem: Fixed feature matching and independent anomaly scores miss sample-dependent defect responses and spatial continuity.
ykf6rUHIcg.method: AMProp3D estimates channel relevance from discrepancies between local test and normal-reference distributions, then measures deviations with adaptive-kernel maximum mean discrepancy. It propagates anomaly evidence among spatially close, feature-consistent regions.
ykf6rUHIcg.key_idea: Weight feature channels through local distribution discrepancies and propagate anomaly scores over spatially proximal, feature-consistent neighborhoods.
ykf6rUHIcg.evidence: Experiments cover four 3D anomaly benchmarks, including MiniShiftAD, Anomaly-ShapeNet, and Real3D-AD, with separate and combined module ablations.
ykf6rUHIcg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit detection and localization improvements across four datasets and ablations supporting both modules.
ykf6rUHIcg.main_concern: Reviewers see limited methodological originality beyond established adaptive kernel weighting and graph-based score propagation.

QOBHkcybyF.one_liner: CommandBench combines obfuscation, cross-language implementation, and unmet-specification tests to evaluate repository generation without rewarding source replay.
QOBHkcybyF.problem: Repository benchmarks can reward memorized training code, while manually authored tasks face scale and diversity limits.
