aSdJoe4JB5.main_concern: Reviewers question whether selecting camera views by higher video-text alignment scores improves success-versus-failure discrimination and raise protocol comparability concerns over Hard-5-only matched runs and initial-scene reuse.

yV9rJ7yJ0W.one_liner: Selects and times pairwise preference and absolute acceptability queries via information gain to learn personalized LLM serving and abstention.
yV9rJ7yJ0W.problem: Pairwise preference feedback alone cannot tell an online personalized LLM whether the preferred candidate is good enough to serve rather than abstain under a finite query budget.
yV9rJ7yJ0W.method: DUAL fits a Bayesian logistic user model of preference weights and an acceptance threshold to choose between serving a candidate response or abstaining, using information-gain scoring to select pairwise versus acceptability queries and calibrated cutoffs with quotas to time questions.
yV9rJ7yJ0W.key_idea: Use information-gain scoring with calibrated cutoffs and answer quotas to actively query pairwise preferences and acceptability thresholds for serving-or-abstention decisions.
yV9rJ7yJ0W.evidence: Supported by almost-sure convergence and finite-sample estimation bounds plus controlled question-selection simulations, a 200-profile 9,338-interaction policy study, and human-data evaluations on PRISM and PersonalLLM.
yV9rJ7yJ0W.claimed_gains: Information selection achieves 15.85% serving-mistake AUC versus 16.45% for fixed allocation at 940 answers, and in a 200-profile study at 930 answers over 9,338 interactions, DUAL reaches 14.71% AUC versus 15.94% for adaptive acceptability-only and 15.33% for serving-action EPIG.
yV9rJ7yJ0W.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the practical formulation combining pairwise preferences, acceptability thresholds, and abstention alongside transparent statistical reporting and convergence guarantees.
yV9rJ7yJ0W.main_concern: Dual-channel querying yields statistically unresolved gains over acceptability-only feedback on human PRISM ratings and underperforms when pairwise questions are charged for displaying two responses.

kODZPTXW7U.one_liner: Recombining skills learned on basic embodied tasks tests continual learning on unseen compositional tasks.
kODZPTXW7U.problem: Existing evaluations of self-evolving agents focus on non-embodied settings rather than continual learning in embodied simulation.
kODZPTXW7U.method: EmbodiedCLBench uses compositional generalization to test whether agents learn basic tasks and recombine acquired skills for complex unseen tasks. It compares agent harnesses and learning methods in an embodied simulator.
kODZPTXW7U.key_idea: Evaluate skill recombination by training on basic embodied tasks before testing complex unseen compositions.
kODZPTXW7U.evidence: Experiments cover four harnesses, two backbone models, and two learning methods, with analyses of complexity, sample scaling, action errors, and step budgets.
kODZPTXW7U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the deterministic offline graph evaluation and the broad comparisons of harnesses and learning methods.
kODZPTXW7U.main_concern: The benchmark measures narrow compositional transfer rather than broader continual learning, with little assessment of retention or forgetting.

TrdQSc0ow5.one_liner: Event-dependent semantic control drives Koopman dynamics while bounded decision closure preserves recommendation candidates.
TrdQSc0ow5.problem: Sequential recommenders entangle behavioral history, latest-event redirects, and ranking while leaving pretrained semantics as static item features.
TrdQSc0ow5.method: SEMKOOPREC combines a frozen behavioral anchor, persistent-transient Koopman dynamics, multi-horizon representation closure, and candidate-preserving decision closure. Its analysis bounds score errors and candidate changes caused by semantic events.
TrdQSc0ow5.key_idea: Treat semantic events as controls on persistent and transient Koopman states, then bound their effect on candidate ranking.
TrdQSc0ow5.evidence: Experiments cover three Amazon benchmarks, five datasets under strict history masking, alternative semantic representations, and matched ablations.
TrdQSc0ow5.claimed_gains: SEMKOOPREC achieves the best result on all 12 HR/NDCG metrics across three Amazon benchmarks, with HR@10 gains up to 36.50%, using fewer than 73K additional trainable parameters.
TrdQSc0ow5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the explicit dynamics-to-ranking analysis, clear mathematical presentation, and extensive evaluation under multiple protocols.
TrdQSc0ow5.main_concern: Experiments do not sufficiently show how semantic control and bounded candidate intervention change recommendations in practice.

eHZTS0CUu4.one_liner: Counterfactual claim overlays expose video-model deference, while decoupled arbitration separates evidence selection from reading.
eHZTS0CUu4.problem: Video benchmarks test reading on-screen text without measuring whether models improperly trust claims that conflict with visual evidence.
eHZTS0CUu4.method: VisualTrust pairs each question with claim-free, accurate-claim, and misleading-claim versions of one video. DEAR uses an independent conflict check, evidence selection without fixed modality priority, and a reader operating in a fresh context.
eHZTS0CUu4.key_idea: Isolate claim deference through single-fact counterfactual overlays, then arbitrate conflicting evidence before a fresh reader answers.
eHZTS0CUu4.evidence: The benchmark contains 5,063 cases across 14 claim-fact classes and evaluates seven open-weight and five proprietary models.
eHZTS0CUu4.claimed_gains: Mean accuracy falls from 90.3% without a claim to 53.9% with a misleading claim; among initially correct responses, 40.9% flip to the trap answer and only 0.6% become other errors.
eHZTS0CUu4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the controlled counterfactual design isolates an important failure mode and that DEAR offers a practical training-free mitigation.
eHZTS0CUu4.main_concern: The contribution beyond VisualTextTrap and its mitigation remains unclear without direct benchmark and method comparisons.

T0W6zdpGcc.one_liner: Sparse autoencoder factors recover class-agnostic objectness from frozen open-vocabulary detector embeddings.
T0W6zdpGcc.problem: Open-vocabulary detectors can miss unknown objects when class-name prompts are absent despite retaining useful region-level object cues.
T0W6zdpGcc.method: SAE-OVOW decomposes known-aligned region embeddings into sparse factors, selects reliable factors with similar distributions and diverse decoder directions, and aggregates their activations into objectness. It combines this score with known-class uncertainty for unknown detection.
T0W6zdpGcc.key_idea: Select transferable sparse latent factors from frozen region embeddings and aggregate their activations as class-agnostic objectness.
T0W6zdpGcc.evidence: Experiments on M-OWODB and S-OWODB include latent removal-and-recovery tests and post-hoc audits of coherent visual patterns.
T0W6zdpGcc.claimed_gains: On S-OWODB Task 2, SAE-OVOW improves U-Recall by 12.7 points and overall mAP by 5.3 points over the best competing results.
T0W6zdpGcc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value extracting objectness from frozen representations without unknown-class annotations or predefined attributes while preserving known-class performance.
T0W6zdpGcc.main_concern: Controlled comparisons with OW-OVD and simpler objectness or attribute baselines are missing, leaving the sparse-factor contribution unclear.

nr3Qtb3R2J.one_liner: Mask-aware caching reuses background states and stable-token velocities for efficient inpainting search.
nr3Qtb3R2J.problem: Standard inference-time scaling repeatedly processes unchanged unmasked context and applies uniform computation to masked tokens with different refinement needs.
nr3Qtb3R2J.method: The training-free framework aligns candidate background trajectories with mask-aware initial noise and caches anchor background KV states. Token-Aware Temporal Velocity Cache reuses predictions for stabilized masked tokens while focusing computation on uncertain ones.
nr3Qtb3R2J.key_idea: Share aligned background computation across candidates and adapt masked-token updates according to temporal prediction stability.
nr3Qtb3R2J.evidence: Experiments on EditBench and BrushBench compare quality and cost with standard multi-candidate scaling.
nr3Qtb3R2J.claimed_gains: The method reduces cost by up to 4.4× on EditBench and 4.6× on BrushBench over standard scaling while preserving scaling gains.
nr3Qtb3R2J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the training-free method is simple and practical, with substantial speedups, little quality loss, and useful ablations.
nr3Qtb3R2J.main_concern: Reviewers most often question the novelty of background KV caching and its differentiation from close prior work.

erYE1VciKv.one_liner: Flow-matching velocity responses and cross-frame differences provide forensic features for generated-video detection.
erYE1VciKv.problem: Appearance, semantic, and temporal artifacts used by synthetic-video detectors can be generator-specific and generalize poorly to unseen models.
erYE1VciKv.method: TRACE probes a pretrained video DiT at multiple flow timesteps and computes adjacent-frame velocity differences under shared noise. It adds Real-Centered Trajectory Optimization to model generation-aware trajectory representations and consistency.
erYE1VciKv.key_idea: Use shared-noise velocity-field responses from a frozen generative video model as transferable forensic representations.
erYE1VciKv.evidence: The abstract reports distinct real-versus-generated velocity responses across different pretrained video-generation backbones used as probes.
erYE1VciKv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the generation-process-aware motivation, transferable velocity-response features, minimal shared-noise design, and reported benchmark performance.
erYE1VciKv.main_concern: The method's difference-feature definition is inconsistent across sections, while reviewers also request stronger justification of timestep choices and computational overhead.

ehya7GFRpl.one_liner: A unified benchmark suite supports joint optimization of agent embodiment and control policy.
ehya7GFRpl.problem: Most policy-learning benchmarks fix agent design, despite embodiment and policy being coupled choices whose separate optimization can be suboptimal.
ehya7GFRpl.method: Co-Design Gym provides environments and a common interface for explicit design spaces and joint embodiment-policy optimization. It spans robotics, games, infrastructure, networks, multi-agent systems, and control with systematic algorithm comparisons.
ehya7GFRpl.key_idea: Expose embodiment design and policy learning as coupled optimization variables through a shared benchmark interface.
ehya7GFRpl.evidence: The suite contains 20 environment families and over 85 co-design presets, with a systematic evaluation of representative co-design algorithms.
ehya7GFRpl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the benchmark addresses a meaningful gap through broad environments, explicit design spaces, and a useful common interface.
ehya7GFRpl.main_concern: Reviewers most often question evaluation fairness and coverage, citing the four-hour wall-clock budget, unequal implementation overheads, and limited preset comparisons.

BPPIfaAp5k.one_liner: A permissively licensed image-text corpus provides fixed splits and tooling for reproducible visual generation.
BPPIfaAp5k.problem: Visual generative research lacks large, accessible, stable datasets with permissive licensing and a common training regime.
BPPIfaAp5k.method: GPIC provides safety-filtered, deduplicated internet images captioned by a vision-language model and centrally hosted with fixed splits. It includes a generative benchmarking protocol and a pixel-space flow-matching reference baseline.
BPPIfaAp5k.key_idea: Pair permissively licensed image-text data and fixed splits with a shared evaluation protocol for controlled generative comparisons.
BPPIfaAp5k.evidence: GPIC contains approximately 28 trillion pixels across 100M training, 200K validation, and 1M test examples, with a reference pixel-space flow-matching baseline.
BPPIfaAp5k.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that a large accessible permissively licensed corpus with fixed splits and evaluation tools is valuable for reproducibility and fair comparison.
BPPIfaAp5k.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about dataset reliability, including licensing assurance at scale, residual duplicates, limited quality filtering, and automatically generated captions.

xbljmN056N.one_liner: Contextual answerability feedback guides iterative corpus reformulation for stronger parametric factual learning.
xbljmN056N.problem: Document reformulation relies on human heuristics and expensive train-and-evaluate searches to identify useful training data.
xbljmN056N.method: Contextual Answerability measures how readily a model recovers a target fact from a reformulated document. Carve uses this feedback to iteratively explore and refine corpus-level reformulation strategies before training.
xbljmN056N.key_idea: Use low contextual answerability as a proxy for stronger parametric knowledge acquisition when selecting document reformulations.
xbljmN056N.evidence: Correlations across 20 strategies, an equal-item control, gradient analysis, and training-from-scratch and continued-pretraining experiments support the answerability-learnability relationship.
xbljmN056N.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the inverse answerability-learnability relationship interesting and well supported by correlations, controls, and training experiments.
xbljmN056N.main_concern: Reviewers most often cite limited baselines and narrow evidence, making it difficult to isolate CA-guided evolution or establish generality beyond one model family and Wikipedia.

bD70jJGngk.one_liner: Biological evidence episodes benchmark calibrated hypothesis forecasting and sequential experimental design.
bD70jJGngk.problem: It is unclear whether language models can weigh scientific evidence of varying reliability and relevance to make calibrated probabilistic judgments.
bD70jJGngk.method: EDB-Bio presents sequences of real experimental results and asks models for hypothesis probabilities, with Bayes-factor analyses of evidence weights and belief updates. Proper-scoring-rule post-training is evaluated alongside sequential experiment selection.
bD70jJGngk.key_idea: Evaluate scientific deliberation as probabilistic hypothesis forecasting from ordered experimental evidence with proper scoring rules.
bD70jJGngk.evidence: The benchmark contains 96k episodes across drug-perturbation transcriptomics, CRISPR screens, and GWAS, evaluating open-weight and frontier models on calibration, discrimination, belief revision, and experiment selection.
bD70jJGngk.claimed_gains: In sequential experiment selection, Ibis0 is 2.5× more efficient than the best frontier model.
bD70jJGngk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the probabilistic scientific-reasoning formulation, broad diagnostics, real biological data, and downstream experiment-selection evaluation.
bD70jJGngk.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the benchmark demonstrates generalizable evidence assessment, citing limited transfer, train-test overlap, and weaknesses in belief-revision metrics.

1HzFxSiV9v.one_liner: Proposes RA-TPT, replacing entropy minimization with bounded-margin and uncertainty-routed logit regularization for calibrated test-time prompt tuning.
1HzFxSiV9v.problem: Entropy minimization in test-time prompt tuning inflates predictive confidence on incorrect or ambiguous target-domain samples under distribution shift.
1HzFxSiV9v.method: RA-TPT combines an uncertainty-aware bounded-margin objective with a pseudo-label anchor, uncertainty-routed centered-logit dispersion and mean-logit regularizers, and soft conflict-aware gradient projection.
1HzFxSiV9v.key_idea: Limits logit inflation via uncertainty-routed dispersion regularization, bounded-margin separation, and conflict-aware gradient projection.
1HzFxSiV9v.evidence: Evaluated across 31 classification, ImageNet shift, biomedical, and remote sensing benchmarks with multiple VLM and standard classifier backbones.
1HzFxSiV9v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that addressing TTA miscalibration in logit space with uncertainty-aware regularization is practical and reduces ECE across diverse domains.
1HzFxSiV9v.main_concern: Reviewers view the methodological contribution as incremental over prior logit-control and gradient-projection methods, noting small unverified gains from individual components.

vXk0HWByZT.one_liner: Introduces tree-grams, autoregressive hierarchical tensor-factorized n-gram language approximators with separate horizon and capacity knobs.
vXk0HWByZT.problem: Hierarchical language models are studied synthetically, but their relevance and controllability as approximators of realistic language corpora remain underexplored.
vXk0HWByZT.method: Tree-grams factorize conditional probability tensors via hierarchical compositions of order-2 and order-3 tensors parameterized by context horizon n and rank d.
vXk0HWByZT.key_idea: Composes order-2 and order-3 tensors in a tree topology to control language context horizon n and capacity d independently.
vXk0HWByZT.evidence: Evaluated on TinyStories against count-based n-gram, SMM, and parameter-matched transformer baselines, plus muP hyperparameter transfer and topology pruning studies.
vXk0HWByZT.claimed_gains: Concentrated topology routing permits pruning up to 95% of candidate topologies without significant change in performance.
vXk0HWByZT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the interpretable hierarchical n-gram construction with separate horizon and capacity knobs and strong empirical comparisons against baselines.
vXk0HWByZT.main_concern: All experiments use only TinyStories and mostly hand-selected nearly balanced trees, leaving generalizability and the specific benefit of tree structure unclear.

MUCcGzornM.one_liner: Unifies exponent value and temporal locality via fixed-length Rice residual coding and fused GPU kernels for lossless LLM compression.
MUCcGzornM.problem: Existing lossless LLM compression methods fail to unify floating-point value locality and temporal KV-cache locality, leaving bandwidth bottlenecks untapped.
MUCcGzornM.method: Loce encodes floating-point exponent redundancy using a fixed-length Rice-based residual scheme that captures both value concentration and temporal locality relative to page-start tokens. At the system level, it introduces a GPU-friendly memory layout, fused decoding kernel, and inference pipeline.
MUCcGzornM.key_idea: Fixed-length Rice residual coding over unified value and temporal exponent locality pairs with GPU-optimized layouts and decoding kernels for lossless LLM inference.
MUCcGzornM.evidence: Evaluations test multiple LLMs and floating-point precisions (including FP8 and NVFP4) for compression ratios, kernel speedups, and decoding throughput.
MUCcGzornM.claimed_gains: Delivers an average 2.3x kernel-level acceleration and 1.5x decoding speedup over previous lossless compression methods.
MUCcGzornM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the paper targets a practical LLM memory-bandwidth bottleneck and achieves promising compression even on low-precision FP8/NVFP4 weights.
MUCcGzornM.main_concern: Reviewers note incremental novelty over FOR/PFOR and ZipServ, unclear isolation of temporal KV prediction vs. value locality, and missing clarity on attention-kernel speedups.

jsshaE1NNK.one_liner: Factorizes process reward modeling into separate plan reliability and step correctness predictions supervised via automated multiple executions.
jsshaE1NNK.problem: Existing process reward models conflate unreliable high-level plans with faulty step-level execution into a single scalar score.
jsshaE1NNK.method: Duet-PRM automatically generates factorized plan-reliability and step-correctness labels from multiple independent policy executions without human or auxiliary-LLM annotation, training a generative PRM to predict both signals.
jsshaE1NNK.key_idea: Supervises separate plan-reliability and step-correctness heads using execution-consistency statistics across multiple automated rollouts.
jsshaE1NNK.evidence: Evaluated on chain discrimination and Best-of-N selection across four mathematical reasoning benchmarks.
jsshaE1NNK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating plan reliability from step correctness is intuitive and that the automated supervision pipeline avoids human annotation.
jsshaE1NNK.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty relative to ReasonFlux-PRM, whether 4-rollout plan labels conflate plan quality with policy execution skill, and whether baseline input formats were matched.

imjZibyHqx.one_liner: Projects noisy audio tokens onto a target category's clean PCA subspace and interpolates them training-free inside frozen ALLMs.
imjZibyHqx.problem: Audio large language models degrade sharply when background noise and competing sound sources mask a target sound.
imjZibyHqx.method: LTM-AE extracts hidden-state representations from clean reference recordings to form a per-category long-term memory PCA subspace without updating ALLM parameters. At inference, it reconstructs incoming audio tokens in the selected category subspace and interpolates them with original tokens (adding a learned token-level gate for speech ASR).
imjZibyHqx.key_idea: Reconstructs noisy audio tokens inside a clean reference PCA subspace per target category and interpolates them before frozen ALLM decoding.
imjZibyHqx.evidence: Evaluated across 20 sound categories, three open-source ALLMs (including Qwen2-Audio), constrained/free-form classification, and speech ASR on MultiPerception mixtures.
imjZibyHqx.claimed_gains: Achieves 29.53 to 46.15 percentage-point accuracy gains over raw mixtures across models, and reduces transcription WER by 40% with a learned gate.
imjZibyHqx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the training-free subspace projection is simple, efficient, and evaluated cleanly across three distinct ALLMs.
imjZibyHqx.main_concern: Reviewers note that conditioning on the ground-truth target category confounds acoustic enhancement with category-prior steering, and synthetic -10 dB mixtures omit enhancement baselines.

lUmaFasRHR.one_liner: Refines world-action models post-deployment using successful and failed visual futures at turning points with value-gated classifier-free guidance.
lUmaFasRHR.problem: Post-deployment training for world-action models improves actions without refining world predictions, causing compounding errors in high-dimensional dexterous manipulation.
lUmaFasRHR.method: DEWO identifies interaction turning points from deployment experience and supervises world predictions on both successful and failed visual continuations to enable outcome-conditioned classifier-free guidance. A value head estimates task progress from video features and activates guidance during inference when progress stalls.
lUmaFasRHR.key_idea: Trains world-action models on divergent successful and failed visual futures around turning points and triggers classifier-free guidance via a progress value head.
lUmaFasRHR.evidence: Evaluated across three WAM formulations on five simulated DexJoCo tasks and four real-world tasks on Wuji and Sharpa dexterous hands.
lUmaFasRHR.claimed_gains: Increases real-world 3x3 grid success from 51.0% to 71.7% after two rounds of deployment learning across Wuji and Sharpa tasks.
lUmaFasRHR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree learning from failed visual outcomes without imitating failed actions is practical and validated across multiple WAMs and real dexterous hands.
lUmaFasRHR.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over Decision Diffuser/RECAP, unclear evidence that failed futures or world representation gains (without guidance) drive improvements, and real-world collection overhead.

QzwrGtWD1B.one_liner: Modulates multi-scale VQVAE content features with a contrastively learned modal-degradation embedding to jointly control medical deep unfolding.
QzwrGtWD1B.problem: Existing deep unfolding networks entangle modality-dependent tissue contrast with heterogeneous degradations in all-in-one medical image restoration.
QzwrGtWD1B.method: MoDeFold extracts content priors via a multi-scale VQVAE supervised by clean-code references and a joint prior via a contrastively trained Modal-Degradation Embedder, using the embedding to modulate content features before fusing both to control unfolding.
QzwrGtWD1B.key_idea: Uses a contrastively trained modal-degradation embedding to modulate multi-scale VQVAE content features and jointly steer a shared unfolding pipeline.
QzwrGtWD1B.evidence: Evaluated on all-in-one medical image restoration benchmarks (including AMIR) across MRI, CT, and PET with ablation studies on conditioning order.
QzwrGtWD1B.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using a joint modal-degradation embedding to modulate content features before unfolding is well-motivated and achieves the highest average PSNR and SSIM.
QzwrGtWD1B.main_concern: Reviewers note that each dataset pairs one modality with one fixed degradation and that MoDeFold uses extra eight-dataset pretraining and more parameters (49M vs. 42M for TAT) with very small AMIR margins (0.01-0.10 dB).

8aZviqJTBE.one_liner: Trains diverse VLA expert policies with parameter and view diversity, curates successful rollouts, and distills one student.
8aZviqJTBE.problem: Few-shot supervised fine-tuning of Vision-Language-Action models overfits to narrow demonstrations, while single-policy rollout reuse reinforces execution errors.
8aZviqJTBE.method: CoAct maintains a diverse expert pool via WeightCoAct (action-head discrepancy) and DataCoAct (expert-specific visual views), filters novel successful rollouts with Collective Trajectory Curation, and distills them into a single student policy.
8aZviqJTBE.key_idea: Diversifies a VLA expert pool via action-head discrepancy and persistent visual views, curates successful rollouts, and distills into one student.
8aZviqJTBE.evidence: Experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin, and five real-world tasks across multiple VLA backbones, plus matched-budget single-policy controls.
8aZviqJTBE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize strong multi-benchmark and real-robot gains and appreciate the matched-budget control showing multi-expert curation beats single-policy self-training.
8aZviqJTBE.main_concern: The few-shot framing understates the 100 extra labeled rollouts and multi-expert training cost, and an independent-experts baseline without WeightCoAct/DataCoAct is missing.

DWxCJ9CV5U.one_liner: Constructs an off-policy actor-critic algorithm for dynamic expectile and CVaR using elicitability and a perturbation-free surrogate.
DWxCJ9CV5U.problem: Optimizing dynamic risk measures with stochastic policies typically requires transition perturbation for policy updates and model-based approaches for value learning.
DWxCJ9CV5U.method: They derive a perturbation-free surrogate policy gradient under softmax parameterization, develop model-free value learning for dynamic expectile and CVaR via elicitability, and combine them into an off-policy actor-critic algorithm.
DWxCJ9CV5U.key_idea: Combines elicitability-based model-free value learning with a transition-perturbation-free softmax surrogate policy gradient for dynamic risk.
DWxCJ9CV5U.evidence: Tabular monotonic-improvement and value-convergence proofs, stochastic-approximation convergence results, and empirical comparisons against baselines like Exp-PPO.
DWxCJ9CV5U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value solving dynamic risk optimization with stochastic off-policy actor-critic and the tabular theoretical and empirical results.
DWxCJ9CV5U.main_concern: Theory is restricted to tabular settings with exact evaluation and does not prove global convergence or unique policy convergence, with a questioned proof and missing continuous baselines.

D8ewD7A7dL.one_liner: Trains a flow-matching refiner on data-centered perturbations to correct off-trajectory errors from molecular conformer generators.
D8ewD7A7dL.problem: Sequential diffusion and flow-matching conformer generators accumulate off-trajectory errors during low-SNR denoising steps due to train-inference distribution mismatch.
D8ewD7A7dL.method: The proposed mismatch-aware refiner is trained on perturbations centered around reference conformers and maps noisy upstream conformers back toward valid structures without estimating their residual error. It plugs into existing denoising-based generators to refine outputs in fewer total sampling steps.
D8ewD7A7dL.key_idea: Trains a flow-matching vector field on data-centered perturbations around reference conformers to refine off-trajectory outputs from pretrained generators.
D8ewD7A7dL.evidence: Evaluated on GEOM-QM9 and GEOM-Drugs across multiple denoising-based conformer generators, including step-matched controls and bond/angle/torsion ablations.
D8ewD7A7dL.claimed_gains: Uses 20 generation plus 20 refinement steps compared with 50 steps for generator-only baselines (from review) while improving conformer quality.
D8ewD7A7dL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the data-centered refiner is intuitive, reusable across generators, and improves conformer metrics even at matched or fewer sampling steps.
D8ewD7A7dL.main_concern: Reviewers question the theoretical justification of matching initial error scales to flow time t*, missing training-cost details, and lack of energy-based benchmarks.

p3A0n5sDNs.one_liner: Replaces PPO's linear likelihood-ratio surrogate with an n-th root power-law surrogate to damp large-ratio gradient spikes.
p3A0n5sDNs.problem: PPO and TRPO optimize linear importance-ratio surrogates that suffer high-variance gradient growth under large likelihood-ratio displacements.
p3A0n5sDNs.method: Symphony replaces the importance ratio r with its n-th root r^(1/n) in clipped and KL-constrained RL objectives, preserving the Fisher Information Metric direction at r=1 while damping gradient growth away from the behavior policy.
p3A0n5sDNs.key_idea: Applies an n-th root power-law transformation to likelihood ratios in policy optimization surrogates to preserve origin gradients while damping large-ratio variance.
p3A0n5sDNs.evidence: Evaluated on MJX continuous control (including 2B-step and tuned 10M-step Humanoid) and JAXAtari against PPO and SPO.
p3A0n5sDNs.claimed_gains: Achieves higher final returns than PPO and SPO in tuned 10M-step Humanoid and positive gains over PPO over 2 billion Humanoid transitions (exact numbers not stated in abstract).
p3A0n5sDNs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the simple, drop-in mathematical formulation and strong long-horizon stability on continuous control tasks.
p3A0n5sDNs.main_concern: Reviewers note gains rely on constant-learning-rate setups where standard PPO collapses, and point out missing comparisons against Dual-Clip PPO and recent ratio-bounding methods.

rvF3ZqTBhF.one_liner: Analyzes when predictive-improvement intrinsic rewards cause agents to seek redundant confirmation rather than new information.
rvF3ZqTBhF.problem: Finite-budget agents trained with predictive-improvement rewards can earn credit by confirming prior discoveries instead of exploring new information.
rvF3ZqTBhF.method: Analyzes current-answer rescoring, fixed-horizon prediction, complete observation deletion, and independent tests in noiseless bit models, noisy spatial fields, and Mastermind records.
rvF3ZqTBhF.key_idea: Compares prediction targets and retained-evidence rules to characterize the reward-information frontier and show when deletion/horizon rewards induce confirmation seeking.
rvF3ZqTBhF.evidence: Exact theoretical propositions on an independent bit model plus experiments on spatial field reconstruction, Mastermind, and sensor data.
rvF3ZqTBhF.claimed_gains: Complete observation deletion can make every reward-optimal policy spend half its budget on confirmation, and switching a field policy to deletion reward leaves 45% more reconstruction error than continued task training.
rvF3ZqTBhF.reviewer_consensus: Two reviewers value the sharp theoretical characterization of reward-optimal policies and the interventional vs. observational predictor distinction.
rvF3ZqTBhF.main_concern: Reviewers question how widely the analyzed deletion/Eq. (1) rewards are used in practice and note difficulty parsing the experimental setups.

pecCZ4r0qx.one_liner: Constructs a compositional certificate bounding return loss and safety under evolution for tool-augmented LLM skill libraries.
pecCZ4r0qx.problem: Skill-library LLM agents lack formal bounds on how per-skill errors compound across plans or how long safety guarantees hold as libraries are edited.
pecCZ4r0qx.method: The paper defines a two-layer model separating within-invocation decisions from cross-invocation artifact updates, measuring gaps against the frozen model's realizable optimum on a fixed plan. It decomposes return loss and derives a propagation bound allowing discontinuous skill ruptures and checkpointing over an editing horizon.
pecCZ4r0qx.key_idea: Decomposes plan-relative return loss in a two-layer artifact-passing model and bounds discontinuous skill-rupture propagation across an explicit editing horizon.
pecCZ4r0qx.evidence: Theoretical decomposition, propagation, and safety-under-evolution theorems supported by empirical error measurements and checkpointing experiments.
pecCZ4r0qx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper addresses an important, under-formalized problem and provides a useful vocabulary separating skill authoring from execution and artifact effects.
pecCZ4r0qx.main_concern: Reviewers find flaws in the supplementary safety proofs (e.g., per-action vs. per-skill capability budgets and pairwise conditional bounds) and note unclear theoretical novelty and experimental justification.

Fpevb9ga4I.one_liner: Analyzes factorwise polar flow as a continuous-time idealization of per-head Muon in self-attention.
Fpevb9ga4I.problem: In self-attention, per-head Muon updates key and query matrices separately even though logits depend on their product, making implicit bias dependent on factorization.
Fpevb9ga4I.method: The authors study momentum-free factorwise polar flow for a single attention head, analyzing singular-direction convergence for fixed gradients, Ky Fan max-margin convergence, and local product/weight convergence under exact softmax attention.
Fpevb9ga4I.key_idea: Models per-head Muon as factorwise polar flow on K and Q, characterizing when the normalized product converges to the width-h Ky Fan max-margin solution.
Fpevb9ga4I.evidence: Theoretical convergence proofs for fixed gradients and exact softmax attention, illustrated by numerical experiments.
Fpevb9ga4I.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper provides a technically sound theoretical characterization of factorwise spectral optimization bias in single-head self-attention.
Fpevb9ga4I.main_concern: Reviewers question the practical significance of the idealized single-head, momentum-free, fixed-representation setting and note presentation issues with undefined terms and strong assumptions.

HGaKxkVL3p.one_liner: Formulates influence functions in a sample-space dual representation whose complexity scales with dataset size rather than parameter count.
HGaKxkVL3p.problem: Computing classical parameter-space influence functions is infeasible when model parameter count is large relative to dataset size.
HGaKxkVL3p.method: For linearizable models, the authors express parameter updates in the span of training gradients to obtain a dual kernel-space linear system (and a reduced system excluding deleted samples) to estimate parameter, output, and loss changes.
HGaKxkVL3p.key_idea: Replaces the parameter-space Hessian inverse with a sample-space kernel linear system whose dimension scales with dataset size times output dimension.
HGaKxkVL3p.evidence: Analytical derivations and experiments on an MNIST fully connected neural network.
HGaKxkVL3p.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the dual formulation is mathematically clean and clearly presented, making cost independent of model parameter count.
HGaKxkVL3p.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited novelty over existing representer-theorem/kernel influence results, missing kernel-precomputation timing and baselines, and validation restricted to a small MNIST FCNN.

1yS6n7sHZW.one_liner: Evaluates active multi-scale geospatial reasoning by requiring MLLM agents to fuse map, satellite, and street-view tools.
1yS6n7sHZW.problem: Existing geographic localization benchmarks use static inputs and final-coordinate accuracy without testing active multi-scale evidence gathering.
1yS6n7sHZW.method: IDOL comprises 1,018 human-reviewed queries across 8 cities and 7 translated languages in two task families (unique pinpoint and open-ended predicate), requiring agents to call POI search, satellite, and street-view tools while evaluating intermediate reasoning.
1yS6n7sHZW.key_idea: Tests MLLM agents on active tool-based evidence fusion across POI maps, satellite imagery, and street views with process-level reasoning metrics.
1yS6n7sHZW.evidence: Evaluates MLLMs including GPT-5.6-Sol and Gemini-3.1-Pro on 1,018 queries with 600 human labels for judge reliability.
1yS6n7sHZW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree IDOL defines a practical, realistic active geolocalization task with broad city/language coverage and thorough judge-reliability checks.
1yS6n7sHZW.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about reproducibility due to live Google Maps dependencies, missing SearchPlaces-only baselines to prove multi-scale necessity, and lack of agent image memory across turns.

LrqoPCa0mY.one_liner: Co-optimizes an embodied VLA policy and a contact-grounded latent token using training-only 2D contact mask supervision.
LrqoPCa0mY.problem: Scalar RL rewards do not explicitly localize physical contact regions needed for precise robotic manipulation in Vision-Language-Action models.
LrqoPCa0mY.method: CPO-RL conditions action prediction on an input-dependent embodied CoT contact token and uses an auxiliary training-only decoder to predict 2D contact masks from RGB features and the latent token. After Contact-SFT initialization, online PPO updates the policy on all trajectories while supervising the auxiliary contact branch on successful simulated rollouts.
LrqoPCa0mY.key_idea: Conditions VLA actions on a latent contact token jointly supervised during online PPO by a training-only 2D contact-mask decoder.
LrqoPCa0mY.evidence: Experiments on four ManiSkill manipulation tasks, component ablations, and sim-to-real robot transfer.
LrqoPCa0mY.claimed_gains: Achieves 94.2% average success on four ManiSkill tasks, improving over RLinf by 19.3 percentage points and cutting mean episode length from 68.5 to 52.7 steps.
LrqoPCa0mY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that asymmetric contact-mask supervision during training is practical, adds no inference overhead, and clearly improves simulation and real-robot performance over the baseline.
LrqoPCa0mY.main_concern: Reviewers raise limited novelty, reliance on privileged simulator contact heuristics, and missing controls against non-contact dense spatial auxiliary tasks or stronger VLA baselines.

OmQHSMNyY5.one_liner: Geometry-matched target distributions guarantee linear recovery for JEPAs on non-Euclidean latent manifolds.
OmQHSMNyY5.problem: Existing JEPA identifiability analysis assumes Euclidean latent variables, leaving recovery guarantees for non-Euclidean latent geometry unresolved.
OmQHSMNyY5.method: The analysis extends distribution-matched JEPAs to embedded Riemannian manifolds and derives exact and approximate recovery conditions from latent geometry and positive-pair dynamics. Spherical, Gaussian, and toroidal experiments test geometrically matched and mismatched targets.
OmQHSMNyY5.key_idea: Match the target distribution to the latent manifold geometry so alignment and distribution matching identify latent states up to linear transformations.
OmQHSMNyY5.evidence: Theory covers exact spherical recovery and approximate-recovery bounds, while experiments compare linear recovery on Gaussian, spherical, and toroidal latent spaces.
OmQHSMNyY5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the paper offers a clear, meaningful theoretical extension of JEPA identifiability to non-Euclidean latent geometry.
OmQHSMNyY5.main_concern: Reviewers question the empirical support, citing output-dimension confounding, limited synthetic experiments, and missing comparisons with existing SSL methods.

GveQlZo18U.one_liner: A scientific agent proposes expression trees while an interface fits spatial fields and scores predictions.
GveQlZo18U.problem: Open-form PDE discovery must recover operator structure and nonparametric spatial coefficient fields without flexible fields masking structural errors.
GveQlZo18U.method: HER-PDE couples a scientific Agent with the Hypothesis Evaluation Interface. The Agent composes operator and field nodes into expression trees, while HEI fits time-invariant spatial fields and scores short-horizon predictions across two excitations, preserving operator scope and shared-field identity.
GveQlZo18U.key_idea: Separate agent-based structural search from continuous spatial-field fitting while evaluating complete expression trees across excitations.
GveQlZo18U.evidence: Evaluation spans seven two-dimensional heterogeneous PDE families with 5% state noise, 35 environments, 105 runs, field recovery, sealed prediction, and noise, solver, and morphology controls.
GveQlZo18U.claimed_gains: With 5% state noise across seven two-dimensional heterogeneous PDE families, HER-PDE recovers 70/105 exact structures and achieves 94.3% Pass@3 versus 39/105 exact recoveries for recursive typed evolution.
GveQlZo18U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly recovering open-form structure and nonparametric spatial coefficient fields is important, and they value the explicit preservation of operator scope and shared-field identity.
GveQlZo18U.main_concern: Reviewers question the breadth of the claims because HEI constrains discovery and the analysis does not establish identifiability of structures and coefficient fields.

VTlQbdIDXE.one_liner: Replaces fixed scATAC-seq peak lookup tables with coordinate- and chromosome-aware rotary/gated region embeddings trained via subset contrastive learning.
VTlQbdIDXE.problem: Extreme sparsity, high dimensionality, and inconsistent peak definitions across datasets hinder fixed-vocabulary lookup embeddings for single-cell chromatin accessibility (scATAC-seq) models.
VTlQbdIDXE.method: scChromHEARTs computes adaptive embeddings for arbitrary genomic intervals from chromosome identity and genomic coordinates using rotary transformations, biases, and gates, paired with subset-based contrastive self-supervised learning.
VTlQbdIDXE.key_idea: Generating interval embeddings dynamically from chromosome identity and coordinates via rotary transformations, biases, and gates eliminates fixed peak lookup tables and shares structure across nearby regions.
VTlQbdIDXE.evidence: Evaluated on cell-type annotation, perturbed cell generation, batch correction, cross-dataset transfer, and embedder-versus-lookup ablations.
VTlQbdIDXE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that computing region embeddings from chromosome identity and genomic coordinates cleanly avoids fixed-vocabulary lookup tables and is well supported by controlled embedding ablations.
VTlQbdIDXE.main_concern: Reviewers raise methodological and evaluation flaws, including inflated perturbation reconstruction metrics from passing real references through the trained decoder, unclear ChromFound/held-out-cell comparison protocols, and unconvincing superiority over simpler coordinate encoders.

62Q0vpzvta.one_liner: Supervises early-layer object depth formation and intervention-consistent late-layer answers in MLLMs using existing QA data.
62Q0vpzvta.problem: Multimodal LLMs can encode readable depth features internally without effectively using them to guide final spatial reasoning answers.
62Q0vpzvta.method: Motivated by a layerwise separation between depth readability and answer influence, the method supervises object depth in early layers and trains later layers to respond consistently to controlled depth-representation edits using only existing QA annotations and no inference changes.
62Q0vpzvta.key_idea: Jointly supervising early-layer depth readouts and late-layer consistency under controlled internal depth-relation edits couples depth representation formation with downstream answer use.
62Q0vpzvta.evidence: Mechanistic analyses and QA evaluations on VSI-Bench, CV-Bench, BLINK spatial tasks, MMSI-Bench, and ViewSpatial-Bench across Qwen2.5-VL-3B, Qwen3-VL-4B, and Qwen3.5-4B.
62Q0vpzvta.claimed_gains: Raises mean scores over supervised fine-tuning on identical data by 3.8, 1.7, and 2.5 percentage points for Qwen2.5-VL-3B, Qwen3-VL-4B, and Qwen3.5-4B, respectively.
62Q0vpzvta.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the layerwise mechanistic link between depth readability and answer influence is insightful and that the QA-only training objective is practical with no inference overhead.
62Q0vpzvta.main_concern: Reviewers note that the analysis and gains are narrow, focusing almost exclusively on depth in 3B-4B Qwen models with modest improvements over SFT and limited evidence of broader 3D spatial reasoning.

8aErJ21sV6.one_liner: Adaptively budgets and selects refinement policies for a frozen segmentor using accumulated contextual experience and post-execution mask comparison.
8aErJ21sV6.problem: Visual degradation harms semantic segmentation unevenly across images, making fixed multi-policy execution wasteful and static single-pass inference brittle.
8aErJ21sV6.method: DevoSeg keeps the segmentor frozen and learns an external decision state that assigns per-image policy budgets by estimating opportunity relative to Direct inference, compares resulting masks against Direct using post-execution image-mask evidence, and updates contextual knowledge via disjoint-group validation.
8aErJ21sV6.key_idea: Decoupling experience-guided pre-execution policy budgeting from post-execution mask comparison against a Direct fallback enables adaptive deployment of a frozen segmentor.
8aErJ21sV6.evidence: Evaluated on the ACDC validation set (200 images, Cityscapes-19 queries, four weather conditions) using a frozen SAM 3 backbone, with component ablations and collection-time measurements.
8aErJ21sV6.claimed_gains: Improves mean per-image IoU by 1.363 and dataset-level mIoU by 2.138 percentage points over Direct on ACDC, while executing 30.1% fewer candidate policies and cutting collection time by 23.3%.
8aErJ21sV6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clean separation of pre-execution policy acquisition from post-execution mask selection with a Direct fallback on a frozen SAM 3 backbone.
8aErJ21sV6.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the narrow evaluation (200 ACDC images on a single SAM 3 backbone), mixed statistical evidence where pooled mIoU confidence intervals cross zero and 23.5% of images degrade, and missing fine-tuned or closely related baselines.

IT8mxalCPp.one_liner: Models sparse, irregular multivariate time series via continuous-time latent SDEs on Euclidean or hyperspherical spaces for anomaly detection.
IT8mxalCPp.problem: Existing multivariate time series anomaly detection methods assume uniform sampling and rely on imputation or resampling when observations are sparse or irregular.
IT8mxalCPp.method: Latent SDE Anomaly Detection (LSD) is a generative model that represents observed time series via a continuous-time stochastic dynamical system in a low-dimensional Euclidean or hyperspherical latent space, incorporating masks and timestamps directly without imputation.
IT8mxalCPp.key_idea: Modeling irregular multivariate observations through continuous-time latent stochastic differential equations on Euclidean or hyperspherical manifolds enables imputation-free anomaly detection.
IT8mxalCPp.evidence: Evaluated on six established MTSAD benchmarks and an industrial benchmark with repetitive dynamics down to 1% retained observations.
IT8mxalCPp.claimed_gains: Achieves the best overall rank across six benchmarks, reaches roughly twice the AUPRC of the strongest discrete-time baseline on an industrial benchmark, and remains top-ranked at 1% data retention.
IT8mxalCPp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling sparse, irregular multivariate time series directly via continuous-time latent SDEs is well-motivated and empirically tested across multiple benchmarks and sparsity regimes.
IT8mxalCPp.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing primary comparisons against native continuous-time irregular-series baselines (such as Neural ODEs and Neural CDEs), dataset-sensitive latent geometry choices, and limited novelty over prior latent SDE formulations.

QYqvpMZT0s.one_liner: Aligns one-step generators to black-box rewards via feature-space optimal transport toward a mixture of tilted current and reference distributions.
QYqvpMZT0s.problem: One-step generative models lack tractable likelihoods and denoising trajectories, preventing standard likelihood- or gradient-based RLHF post-training with non-differentiable rewards.
QYqvpMZT0s.method: RWTD constructs an adaptive target mixing separately reward-tilted current and reference sample distributions and aligns the one-step generator to it via feature-space optimal transport and fixed-point regression using only samples and scalar rewards.
QYqvpMZT0s.key_idea: Feature-space optimal transport and fixed-point regression align a one-step generator to an adaptive mixture of reward-tilted current and reference distributions without likelihoods or reward gradients.
QYqvpMZT0s.evidence: Theoretical fixed-point analysis and experiments on SANA Sprint 1.6B and SDXL-Turbo backbones with GenEval and HPSv2 preference alignment.
QYqvpMZT0s.claimed_gains: Improves the GenEval score of the one-step SANA Sprint 1.6B backbone from 0.73 to 0.80.
QYqvpMZT0s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical black-box post-training interface requiring neither likelihoods nor reward gradients and find the current/reference mixture target intuitive and effective on two one-step backbones.
QYqvpMZT0s.main_concern: Reviewers note a gap between exact optimal-transport theory and the finite-particle Sinkhorn/regression implementation, potential GenEval reward overfitting without independent evaluation, and unclear preservation of general capabilities.

KQxJ6xI0LN.one_liner: Introduces dynamic manipulation benchmarks and accelerates frozen VLA/WAM policies via training-free cached representation and action reuse.
KQxJ6xI0LN.problem: High inference latency in VLA and world action models leaves executed actions conditioned on stale observations while dynamic environments continue evolving.
KQxJ6xI0LN.method: The authors introduce Dynamic-LIBERO and Dynamic-RoboTwin with inference-time world evolution and propose PACE, a training-free runtime that reuses cached observation representations and action computations across replanning and integration steps while compiling remaining operations.
KQxJ6xI0LN.key_idea: Training-free caching and reuse of visual representations, residuals, and action velocities across replanning and integration steps cuts VLA latency to prevent stale actions in evolving scenes.
KQxJ6xI0LN.evidence: Evaluated on Dynamic-LIBERO and Dynamic-RoboTwin across two policies and eight dynamic settings, plus physical-robot experiments.
KQxJ6xI0LN.claimed_gains: PACE accelerates simulated inference by up to 3.8x, improves dynamic task success by up to 42.8 percentage points, and cuts physical-robot per-chunk stalls from 159 to 69 ms.
KQxJ6xI0LN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that connecting VLA inference latency directly to closed-loop success in continuously evolving dynamic benchmarks addresses a practical, overlooked robotics problem.
KQxJ6xI0LN.main_concern: Reviewers flag limited methodological novelty in PACE's caching techniques, missing comparisons to caching baselines like VLA-Cache and BAC, and small real-robot evaluation scale (10 trials per condition).

r8SaLsl8Kk.one_liner: Benchmarks autonomous LLM researchers jointly modifying model weights and agent harnesses under fixed budgets across five domains.
r8SaLsl8Kk.problem: Existing automated AI research benchmarks evaluate model training or harness editing in isolation rather than joint model-harness co-evolution.
r8SaLsl8Kk.method: CoEvoBench gives LLM researchers a common starting model-harness pair and fixed compute budget across five agentic domains to iteratively choose training, harness revisions, or both using development feedback, then evaluates submitted pairs on held-out test tasks.
r8SaLsl8Kk.key_idea: Evaluating autonomous LLM researchers with joint access to model post-training and harness editing under a shared budget and three-way split measures system-level recursive improvement.
r8SaLsl8Kk.evidence: Evaluated five frontier LLM researcher models across five agentic domains with development, selection, and held-out test splits.
r8SaLsl8Kk.claimed_gains: Among improving runs with at least three selection-set evaluations, the single largest jump in best-so-far performance accounts for a median of 62.5% of total observed gain.
r8SaLsl8Kk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that benchmarking joint model-harness co-evolution with fixed budgets and careful train/selection/test splits addresses a timely and understudied auto-research question.
r8SaLsl8Kk.main_concern: Reviewers question benchmark reliability and necessity of co-evolution due to high run-to-run variance, unexplained selection-to-test drops, underspecified manual cheating audits, and missing harness-only/model-only ablations.

PGsmWBEYnL.one_liner: Systematically ablates 29 spatio-temporal masking geometries across MAE and JEPA EEG foundation models and identifies bias-inflation collapse.
PGsmWBEYnL.problem: EEG foundation models bundle masking strategies with different backbones and objectives, leaving the isolated effect of spatio-temporal masking geometry poorly understood.
PGsmWBEYnL.method: The authors formalize spatio-temporal masking geometries, pre-train 58 models across 29 configurations under a shared pipeline for MAE and JEPA, evaluate them via linear probing on 12 OpenEEGBench datasets, and diagnose a JEPA failure mode called bias-inflation collapse.
PGsmWBEYnL.key_idea: Isolating spatio-temporal masking geometry in a shared MAE and JEPA pre-training pipeline reveals shared optimal masks, broad robustness, and a JEPA-specific bias-inflation collapse mode.
PGsmWBEYnL.evidence: 58 pre-trained models evaluated under linear probing on all 12 datasets of OpenEEGBench, plus feature-mean/residual and band-power collapse analyses.
PGsmWBEYnL.claimed_gains: 11 MAE and 9 JEPA masking configurations are statistically indistinguishable from the best, and a well-chosen mask matches REVE downstream performance at a fraction of its pre-training compute.
PGsmWBEYnL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the systematic shared-pipeline ablation across 58 models and 12 datasets and find the discovery and analysis of JEPA bias-inflation collapse insightful.
PGsmWBEYnL.main_concern: Reviewers note that masking geometry is confounded with realized masking ratios (50.8%-70.0%), evaluation is limited to frozen linear probes with single pre-training seeds, and no mitigation is tested for JEPA collapse.

0ijAhFX5kc.one_liner: Exposes each skill policy's structural prior in language so a runtime agent can select and compose policies for new robot tasks.
0ijAhFX5kc.problem: Skill descriptions used for compositional planning omit the structural priors built into policy training, losing information about where each skill generalizes.
0ijAhFX5kc.method: APPL uses a construction agent to segment demonstrations into skills, propose multiple structural priors per skill, and train and verify one policy per prior. A runtime agent then reads these language-stated structural-prior interfaces to select and compose prior-specific policies for new task goals.
0ijAhFX5kc.key_idea: Trains multiple structural-prior-specific policies per segmented skill and exposes those priors in language as the selection interface for a runtime composition agent.
0ijAhFX5kc.evidence: Evaluated on MetaWorld and long-horizon ManiSkill robot manipulation tasks.

teRONzrtEL.one_liner: Builds large-scale continual pretraining, instruction-tuning, and benchmark datasets to evaluate multilingual LLMs on Standardized Yi.
teRONzrtEL.problem: Whether multilingual LLM cross-lingual transfer extends to languages with severely underrepresented scripts like Standardized Yi (Nuosu) remains unmeasured.
teRONzrtEL.method: The authors curate Nuosu-Datasets (78.6M CPT tokens and 166M SFT tokens across 1.1M instruction instances) via OCR digitization, filtering, and expert validation, alongside Nuosu-Benchmark (110,513 instances across five sub-benchmarks and 12 metrics), and evaluate 14 LLMs and adapted models.
teRONzrtEL.key_idea: Digitizes and validates Standardized Yi corpora and a five-category, 12-metric benchmark to test multilingual LLM transfer to an underrepresented script.
teRONzrtEL.evidence: Evaluates 14 representative LLMs and adapted models (such as BIMO-8B) on 110,513 Nuosu-Benchmark instances.
teRONzrtEL.claimed_gains: All 14 evaluated general-purpose LLMs achieve aggregate scores below 40% on Nuosu-Benchmark.
teRONzrtEL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper targets an important, underserved language and contributes a substantial, well-engineered dataset and benchmark resource.
teRONzrtEL.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about severe catastrophic forgetting in BIMO-8B on general benchmarks (76.26 to 48.64), potential train-test overlap or shared template bias, and unclear aggregation of the 12 evaluation metrics.

qAYeg9I0K3.one_liner: Adapts agent harnesses recursively by retaining typed control modules and recombining compatible discoveries using cooperation memory.
qAYeg9I0K3.problem: Whole-harness updates in recursive self-improvement couple control decisions, making it hard to preserve, combine, and reuse effective modifications across runs.
qAYeg9I0K3.method: CoRSI retains typed harness modules while evaluating complete assembled harnesses. It uses base inheritance to preserve unchanged controls, guarded assembly to combine compatible discoveries from different executions, and cooperation memory to guide task-conditioned composition.
qAYeg9I0K3.key_idea: Stores typed harness-level modifications with base inheritance, guarded cross-run assembly, and cooperation memory while evaluating the complete assembled workflow.
qAYeg9I0K3.evidence: Evaluated across competition mathematics, GPQA, condensed-matter problems (CMT-Bench), and tool-driven scientific tasks (Biomni) with ablations.
qAYeg9I0K3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation for modular, reusable harness adaptation is clear and practical, and the empirical evaluation spans a broad set of domains.
qAYeg9I0K3.main_concern: Reviewers question limited novelty and weak evidence of genuine recursive self-improvement or module synergy, noting short non-monotonic trajectories (e.g., 5–10 rounds) and a constrained fixed-workflow search space.

lRQA08VHtX.one_liner: Maps continuous trajectories on the SPD matrix manifold into interpretable Euclidean vectors via intrinsic layers and functional projection.
lRQA08VHtX.problem: Discrete-time neural networks do not model continuous trajectories on the symmetric positive definite (SPD) manifold while preserving Riemannian geometry and temporal dynamics.
lRQA08VHtX.method: MatFAE applies intrinsic SPD-preserving layers (BiMap, manifold averaging, activation, and logarithmic mapping) to transform manifold-valued functions into Euclidean vector-valued functions, followed by a functional encoder layer projecting them to finite-dimensional vectors whose functional weights provide temporal interpretability.
lRQA08VHtX.key_idea: Chains intrinsic SPD-to-Euclidean manifold layers with a continuous functional projection layer to encode SPD trajectories into low-dimensional vectors.
lRQA08VHtX.evidence: Supported by theoretical equivariance/Lipschitz analysis and experiments on 10 simulated trajectory scenarios and six real fMRI datasets.
lRQA08VHtX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining SPD manifold geometry with functional data representation learning is principled and well-motivated, backed by theoretical layer analysis and extensive simulation and fMRI experiments.
lRQA08VHtX.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited methodological novelty beyond integrating SPDNet and FAEclust, insufficient justification for claimed temporal-derivative modeling, and low real-fMRI clustering AMI scores (0.030–0.137).

QD7QBADiHB.one_liner: Estimates multimodal individual treatment effects using tabular-anchored cross-modal extraction and dual-branch balanced-predictive representations.
QD7QBADiHB.problem: Existing multimodal ITE estimators overlook explicit tabular semantics and the trade-off between confounding distribution balancing and factual outcome prediction.
QD7QBADiHB.method: MultiCFR uses tabular semantic anchoring to guide feature extraction from text tokens and image patches, then splits the fused representation into balanced and predictive branches to reduce confounding bias while retaining outcome-predictive signals. The authors also derive a generalization-error bound and release two semi-synthetic benchmarks, MIMIC-TIT and IHDP-TIT.
QD7QBADiHB.key_idea: Anchors text and image extraction on tabular queries and splits fused representations into balanced and predictive branches for multimodal ITE estimation.
QD7QBADiHB.evidence: Supported by a generalization-error bound and experiments with ablations on two semi-synthetic multimodal benchmarks, MIMIC-TIT and IHDP-TIT.
QD7QBADiHB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree multimodal confounding adjustment is a relevant problem, the benchmarks MIMIC-TIT and IHDP-TIT are well-documented, and the empirical comparisons and ablations are thorough.
QD7QBADiHB.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over standard cross-attention and existing representation-splitting methods (like DIGNet), potential confounding leakage in selective gating, and reliance on semi-synthetic rather than real clinical outcomes.

YIll7t6ssN.one_liner: Learns distributionally robust optimization hyperparameters from held-out data via nested bilevel minimax optimization.
YIll7t6ssN.problem: Distributionally robust optimization methods require extensive manual tuning of robustness hyperparameters such as perturbation radii and group parameters.
YIll7t6ssN.method: The authors formulate robustness-parameter learning as a bilevel optimization problem with minimax objectives at both upper and lower levels, instantiating two variants (Bi-HDRO and Bi-PG-DRO) for settings with and without training group labels. They provide sample complexity guarantees and evaluate under simultaneous intra-group and inter-group distribution shifts.
YIll7t6ssN.key_idea: Optimizes DRO robustness parameters directly on held-out worst-group performance using a nested bilevel minimax formulation with or without group labels.
YIll7t6ssN.evidence: Supported by sample-complexity theory compared to grid search and empirical evaluations under combined intra-group and inter-group test shifts.
YIll7t6ssN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper addresses a practical limitation of DRO—manual tuning of robustness hyperparameters—with clear motivation and well-developed formulations.
YIll7t6ssN.main_concern: Reviewers question limited methodological novelty over existing bilevel minimax and DRO methods, high conceptual and computational complexity, and unclear relevance where function-space GDRO reduces to convex reweighting plus ERM.

5tsPBUO8oQ.one_liner: Compresses expert-parallel MoE communication and compute via asymmetric KFAC-weighted Tucker factorization and factor-space execution.
5tsPBUO8oQ.problem: All-to-all expert-parallel communication accounts for up to 47% of MoE inference time, and existing systems optimize transport without compressing redundant expert activations.
5tsPBUO8oQ.method: FactorEP applies post-training group-wise Tucker factorization with KFAC-weighted calibration to produce group-shared input factors, compact expert cores, and a layer-shared output factor so dispatch and combine stay in factor space. A three-stage overlapped pipeline and route-compiled packed token layout convert these reductions into system speedups.
5tsPBUO8oQ.key_idea: Projects inputs with group-shared factors before dispatch, executes compact Tucker cores, and reconstructs via a layer-shared output factor after combine.
5tsPBUO8oQ.evidence: Evaluated on Qwen3-30B-A3B across compression budgets, NVSwitch and PCIe ablations, and end-to-end latency profiling.
5tsPBUO8oQ.claimed_gains: Communication can account for up to 47% of MoE execution; FactorEP's deployment configuration reduces dispatch and combine feature widths by 20% while outperforming compression baselines on Qwen3-30B-A3B.
5tsPBUO8oQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that co-designing post-training asymmetric factorization with the expert-parallel dispatch/combine path is well-motivated and yields strong compression accuracy.
5tsPBUO8oQ.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing comparisons to FP8 communication (e.g., DeepEP), end-to-end latency evaluation on only one model with speedup dropping to ~1.0x at 1K tokens/rank (decode regime), and unclear novelty over prior low-rank MoE methods.

UEHHIh1LZr.one_liner: Synthesizes symbolic behavioral programs via evolutionary search to model LLM and VLM decision strategies on spatial tasks.
UEHHIh1LZr.problem: Chain-of-thought traces can be unfaithful and internal activations are inaccessible in closed models, hindering interpretability of how models solve spatial tasks.
UEHHIh1LZr.method: Drawing on behavioral psychology, the authors use evolutionary search to synthesize compact symbolic programs that predict a model's action distributions and errors from execution traces, evaluated via situational forward KL divergence without needing weights or activations.
UEHHIh1LZr.key_idea: Uses evolutionary program synthesis fitted to black-box execution traces to uncover interpretable symbolic decision rules reproducing model actions and mistakes.
UEHHIh1LZr.evidence: Evaluated on four interactive spatial cognition tasks (including maze navigation, Cambridge spatial working memory, and egocentric navigation) across stronger and weaker LLMs and VLMs.
UEHHIh1LZr.claimed_gains: Synthesized programs match each model's action distribution to within 0.07 nats while being two orders of magnitude simpler than a memorization baseline.
UEHHIh1LZr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that black-box behavioral interpretability via evolutionary symbolic program synthesis is a meaningful, novel, and carefully designed approach for analyzing closed models.
UEHHIh1LZr.main_concern: Reviewers note missing comparisons against other interpretable behavioral baselines (e.g., decision trees or rule learners), potential overfitting or coarseness in Situational KL evaluation, and a 2D-grid abstraction gap for 3D VLM inputs.

LYcySxX65d.one_liner: Evaluates multimodal factual completeness via GAMUT's 1,813 image-grounded questions and two-level meta-rubrics compiled into binary checklists.
LYcySxX65d.problem: Rubric-based evaluation of open-ended answers faces a tension between expressing structured answer spaces (alternatives, orderings, importance) and keeping automatic LLM grading consistent.
LYcySxX65d.method: GAMUT introduces 1,813 image-grounded everyday deep-research questions across 10 domains paired with human-verified two-level rubrics. Authors specify structured meta-rubrics capturing alternatives, orderings, and importance tiers, which fixed mechanical rules compile into flat binary checklists for LLM-as-a-judge grading.
LYcySxX65d.key_idea: Authors structured meta-rubrics capturing open option sets, orderings, and importance tiers, then mechanically compiles them into flat binary checklists for grading.
LYcySxX65d.evidence: Evaluates 14 frontier and open-weight models across 1,813 questions in 10 domains using three LLM judges.
LYcySxX65d.claimed_gains: Evaluated models score from 5.1% to 58.7% on GAMUT with broadly consistent rankings across three LLM judges.
LYcySxX65d.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the expressiveness-versus-reliability tension is well-posed, the two-level meta-rubric compilation design is clean, and the 1,813-question benchmark construction is substantial.
LYcySxX65d.main_concern: Reviewers highlight the lack of an ablation comparing compiled binary checklists against direct holistic meta-rubric grading, no human-judge agreement validation (with Gemini 3.1 Pro used in both authoring and judging), and unpenalized off-rubric hallucinations.

L6KjqbN9Mj.one_liner: Uses coding agents to compile unlabeled LLM reasoning traces into reusable, zero-LLM-cost symbolic program synthesizers.
L6KjqbN9Mj.problem: LLMs are computationally expensive and unreliable on hard program synthesis tasks requiring large combinatorial search.
L6KjqbN9Mj.method: ReaComp feeds a small set of unlabeled LLM reasoning traces to coding agents, which compile them into reusable symbolic program synthesizers over constrained DSLs. These induced solvers run at zero test-time LLM cost either standalone, ensembled, or as a hybrid complement to LLM search.
L6KjqbN9Mj.key_idea: Compiles a small set of unlabeled LLM reasoning traces via coding agents into reusable symbolic DSL synthesizers that execute without test-time LLM calls.
L6KjqbN9Mj.evidence: Evaluated on PBEBench-Lite, PBEBench-Hard, SLR-Bench hard tier, and zero-shot transfer to a historical linguistics sound-change prediction task.
L6KjqbN9Mj.claimed_gains: Symbolic ensembles reach 91.3% on PBEBench-Lite and 84.7% on PBEBench-Hard (+16.3 points over test-time-scaled LLMs at zero LLM cost); hybrids raise PBEBench-Hard from 68.4% to 85.8% (-78% tokens), SLR-Bench hard from 34.4% to 58.0%, and transfer to 80.1% on historical linguistics.
L6KjqbN9Mj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree amortizing LLM reasoning into reusable symbolic solvers for verifiable DSL synthesis is practical and well-motivated, with extensive experiments.
L6KjqbN9Mj.main_concern: Reviewers question whether induced solvers improve over conventional symbolic synthesis or prior LLM-to-code heuristic methods (EoH, HySynth), and flag potential train-test task overlap and oracle-like ensembling over high-variance runs.

1JWXWk1PEf.one_liner: Jointly optimizes an LLM policy and prompt enhancer via alternating updates tailored to an inference-time selection algorithm.
1JWXWk1PEf.problem: Standard post-training alignment optimizes a standalone LLM policy for static decoding, ignoring prompt enhancers and inference-time algorithms present at deployment.
1JWXWk1PEf.method: DynaAlign frames deployment-aware alignment as KL-regularized end-to-end win-rate maximization solved by alternating optimization. It updates the prompt enhancer using downstream utility rewards and trains the LLM policy with an inference-aware surrogate reward calibrated to the target inference-time algorithm.
1JWXWk1PEf.key_idea: Alternates between optimizing a prompt enhancer on downstream utility and updating the LLM policy with an inference-aware calibrated surrogate reward.
1JWXWk1PEf.evidence: Evaluated across two model families on helpfulness and safety alignment benchmarks.
1JWXWk1PEf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that optimizing the prompt enhancer and LLM policy jointly for dynamic inference-time deployment is practically relevant and supported by comprehensive experiments.
1JWXWk1PEf.main_concern: All three reviewers point out a theoretical-to-practical gap: Proposition 2's derived policy reward is intractable and replaced by an InfAlign-style surrogate without proving it preserves the joint optimization objective.

hM41twniwn.one_liner: Distills text embedding teachers by aligning intermediate relational geometry across mismatched depths with emergence-weighted ranking losses.
hM41twniwn.problem: Output-only distillation fails to transfer the intermediate layerwise expansion-contraction and late-layer positive-negative separation trajectories of large text embedding teachers.
hM41twniwn.method: Layerwise Structure Transport (LST) encodes pairwise input relations in a dimension-independent space, learns a soft correspondence to align teacher and student networks with different layer counts, and transfers ranking preferences weighted more heavily at depths where positive-negative margin separation emerges.
hM41twniwn.key_idea: Aligns mismatched-depth teacher and student layers via soft correspondence to transfer pairwise relational geometry and emergence-weighted ranking preferences.
hM41twniwn.evidence: Evaluated on a 15-task embedding suite using Qwen3-Embedding-4B as teacher with two output-KD objectives, alternative student initializations, and layerwise baselines.
hM41twniwn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that transferring intermediate relational trajectories observed in text embedding teachers is well-motivated and coherently designed across relation encoding, soft layer alignment, and ranking supervision.
hM41twniwn.main_concern: Reviewers note modest gains over Output KD (+0.49 to +0.89 points on the 15-task average), evaluation limited to a single teacher (Qwen3-Embedding-4B), and insufficient ablations isolating emergence-aware weighting and baseline tuning.

bN5s2fadbJ.one_liner: Weights multi-view clustering pseudo-targets by topology-perturbation risk certificates and projects gradients to preserve contrastive descent.
bN5s2fadbJ.problem: Graph-propagated pseudo-targets in incomplete multi-view clustering can be confidently wrong under noisy transferred topologies and conflict with contrastive representation learning.
bN5s2fadbJ.method: RTG-IMVC constructs an admissible topology set per missing sample via donor substitution, degree-preserving edge perturbation, and neighborhood bootstrapping, then derives risk-normalized weights from prediction diameter and topology-cover radius for a logarithmic opinion pool. It projects the joint gradient onto a half-space preserving descent of instance- and cluster-level contrastive losses.
bN5s2fadbJ.key_idea: Certifies transferred-topology reliability via perturbation sets to inverse-risk-weight logarithmic opinion pooling while half-space-projecting gradients to protect contrastive descent.
bN5s2fadbJ.evidence: Supported by theoretical proofs of certified teacher robustness and one-step surrogate base-objective decrease under Lipschitz, smoothness, and coverage assumptions.
bN5s2fadbJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that addressing overconfident noisy transferred topologies by combining risk-normalized logarithmic opinion pooling with base-safe gradient projection is principled and coherent.
bN5s2fadbJ.main_concern: Reviewers highlight missing definitions of core backbone, fusion, and loss components making the paper not self-contained, unanalyzed computational overhead of K-topology passes, and unclear equivalence between prediction variance and topology reliability.

2qPJhax9At.one_liner: Benchmarks latent multimodal hazards under benign requests and trains risk awareness via constitution-conditioned token distillation with outcome rewards.
2qPJhax9At.problem: Existing multimodal safety alignment focuses on malicious intent and situational risks, overlooking latent hazards hidden within benign user requests.
2qPJhax9At.method: The authors construct CMMSafe, a 455-pair query-image benchmark for causal hazard detection, and propose Consequence-Aware Safety Policy Optimization (CASPO). CASPO combines constitution-conditioned token distillation from a fixed SFT teacher with outcome-level safety rewards.
2qPJhax9At.key_idea: Distill token-level safety supervision from a constitution-conditioned teacher while optimizing outcome rewards to surface latent causal hazards under benign queries.
2qPJhax9At.evidence: Evaluated on CMMSafe (455 pairs), SIUO, and MSSBench across three model families including Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL-4B, with ablations and human evaluation.
2qPJhax9At.claimed_gains: Closed-source models reach 61.5% failure rates on CMMSafe, while CASPO lowers risk-identification failure ratios to 7.3% for Qwen2.5-VL-7B and 5.7% for Qwen3-VL-4B.
2qPJhax9At.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benign-request hazard problem is well motivated and that CMMSafe and the multi-model experiments with ablations and human evaluation are clear and structured.
2qPJhax9At.main_concern: Reviewers question the fairness of the static-alignment ceiling claim because DPO baselines are not trained on the same consequence-driven data, and note CMMSafe's small 455-sample edge-case scale and reliance on manual constitutions.

TVBNMkPLsv.one_liner: Diagnoses when to keep or drop multi-agent workflow constraints during single-agent skill distillation using a behavior-outcome freedom metric.
TVBNMkPLsv.problem: Distilling multi-agent workflows into single-agent skills indiscriminately transfers pipeline constraints that can hurt performance depending on the evaluation metric.
TVBNMkPLsv.method: The authors separate capability resources from pipeline guidance and define Behavior-Outcome Freedom (F), a pre-synthesis diagnostic measuring signed behavior-outcome rank mismatch. Their method, AdaSkill, keeps validated capabilities, removes runtime orchestration, and applies a development-calibrated F-threshold to decide whether to retain or discard pipeline guidance.
TVBNMkPLsv.key_idea: Threshold a pre-synthesis behavior-outcome rank-mismatch diagnostic to selectively retain or discard workflow pipeline guidance while preserving tool and knowledge capabilities.
TVBNMkPLsv.evidence: Evaluated across 16 matched interventions, 15 atomic treatments, and 11 datasets spanning four data-science task families including causal discovery and Text-to-SQL.
TVBNMkPLsv.claimed_gains: Capability-matched pipeline retention changes normalized utility by +20.0 points under method-selection accuracy and -10.3 under numerical error, with structural effect correlating with F at r = -0.80 (p < 0.001).
TVBNMkPLsv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical framing that separates capability resources from restrictive pipeline guidance and the scorer-reversal ablations showing guidance can hurt.
TVBNMkPLsv.main_concern: Reviewers flag weak held-out evidence for the frozen F-threshold, potential internal inconsistencies in reported diagnostic statistics, and doubts over whether all source systems are genuinely multi-agent.

FjPfxCemDW.one_liner: Proves last-iterate convergence rates for normalized gradient descent under convex Holder smoothness and removes logarithmic overhead via linear stepsize decay.
FjPfxCemDW.problem: Existing analyses of normalized gradient descent under Holder smoothness cover best or weighted-average iterates rather than the last iterate used in practice.
FjPfxCemDW.method: The authors analyze normalized gradient descent on convex (nu, M_nu)-Holder-smooth objectives for both constant and linearly decreasing stepsizes, and complement the theory with numerical Performance Estimation Problem (PEP) worst-case evaluations.
