FjPfxCemDW.key_idea: Apply a linearly decreasing stepsize schedule to normalized gradient descent to eliminate the logarithmic last-iterate overhead without knowing Holder smoothness parameters.
FjPfxCemDW.evidence: Supported by convergence proofs for constant and linearly decreasing stepsizes under convex Holder smoothness and finite-horizon numerical PEP experiments.
FjPfxCemDW.claimed_gains: Establishes an O((log^2(T)/T)^((1+nu)/2)) constant-stepsize bound and an O(T^(-(1+nu)/2)) linearly decreasing stepsize bound matching best-iterate rates without knowing nu or M_nu.
FjPfxCemDW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the writing clear, the analysis clean, and last-iterate guarantees under Holder smoothness a meaningful theoretical gap to address.
FjPfxCemDW.main_concern: Reviewers view the contribution as incremental over prior proof frameworks (e.g., Zamani & Glineur 2025) and note limitations to convex settings and non-anytime T-dependent stepsizes.

x5IHp7avae.one_liner: Separates reference access across dual verification paths of one VLM checkpoint to mitigate shared-reference anchoring in chart reasoning.
x5IHp7avae.problem: Reusing the same fallible model-generated intermediate reference across multimodal verification paths couples their errors and anchors judgments to false premises.
x5IHp7avae.method: The authors diagnose shared-reference anchoring via controlled reference interventions and propose RefSplit, which runs one reference-conditioned verification path and one complementary chart-grounding path that withholds the shared reference using the same verifier checkpoint.
x5IHp7avae.key_idea: Withhold the shared intermediate reference from a second chart-grounded verification path using the same verifier checkpoint to decouple reference-induced errors.
x5IHp7avae.evidence: Tested on 300 Value Position and 300 Legend Binding controlled pairs, 2,509 audited natural error pools, and five public chart benchmarks across five candidate policies.
x5IHp7avae.claimed_gains: Reduces preference-accuracy drop under aligned false references from 26.67 to 4.17 points on Value Position and 7.50 to 0.33 points on Legend Binding, and cuts aligned-error selection by 8.43 points under ordinary generation.
x5IHp7avae.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that shared-reference anchoring is a meaningful failure mode and that the controlled reference-intervention experiments isolate it effectively.
x5IHp7avae.main_concern: Reviewers note limited methodological novelty and marginal practical gains on public benchmarks (0.09 percentage points over reference-free visual verification), questioning the need for a dual-path setup.

hQkETEXdng.one_liner: Trains a human-agent workflow orchestrator via sandboxed capability profiling, a learned feasibility predictor, and multi-turn reinforcement learning.
hQkETEXdng.problem: Effective human-agent collaboration requires deciding when to delegate, verify, or intervene across long-horizon tasks, which prompting-based orchestrators handle poorly.
hQkETEXdng.method: CollabOrchestra formulates orchestration as adaptive workflow plan generation specifying goals, assignees, and handoff deliverables. It profiles agent workers in sandboxes to train a feasibility predictor from execution traces, then uses multi-turn RL to jointly optimize plan quality and execution feasibility.
hQkETEXdng.key_idea: Use an offline execution-grounded feasibility predictor as an RL reward alongside plan quality to train a multi-turn human-agent workflow orchestrator.
hQkETEXdng.evidence: Evaluated on GDPval, JobBench, their underspecified variants, and a small user study, comparing against prompting-based orchestrators and solo agents.
hQkETEXdng.claimed_gains: Improves Task Performance over the best solo agent from 0.474 to 0.744 on GDPval and from 0.260 to 0.286 on JobBench.
hQkETEXdng.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the workflow-level human-agent delegation formulation and the practical two-stage training recipe combining offline feasibility prediction with multi-turn RL.
hQkETEXdng.main_concern: Reviewers emphasize that main execution experiments simulate the human worker with another Gemini-3-Flash CLI agent, confounding orchestration gains with extra compute and not proving real human-agent benefits.

r79D4HR8Lc.one_liner: Defends LLM agents against indirect prompt injection by auditing proposed actions with provenance attribution and retrieved past audit exemplars.
r79D4HR8Lc.problem: Indirect prompt injection defenses that suppress external instructions or enforce rigid boundaries conflict with instruction following and break open-ended agent workflows.
r79D4HR8Lc.method: ActAuditor is a training-free execution-control defense that audits proposed agent actions rather than filtering all external instructions. It combines provenance-aware action attribution, a semantic experience base of few-shot audit exemplars, and experience-augmented action auditing.
r79D4HR8Lc.key_idea: Attribute proposed agent actions to their instruction provenance and audit them using retrieved few-shot precedent cases without retraining the model.
r79D4HR8Lc.evidence: Evaluated against 15 baselines across two benchmarks (including AgentDyn) and adaptive attacks.
r79D4HR8Lc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers view shifting defense from instruction suppression to provenance-aware action auditing as a well-motivated reframing for balancing security and utility.
r79D4HR8Lc.main_concern: Reviewers question whether LLMs can reliably self-attribute action provenance in complex histories or under false-attribution attacks, and note unfairness against training-free baselines since ActAuditor uses human-validated cold-start precedents.

tAg9zeNc4T.one_liner: Applies sliding-window trajectory-weighted minimum Bayes risk decoding to masked diffusion language models for joint early stopping and response selection.
tAg9zeNc4T.problem: Masked diffusion language models often produce strong intermediate responses before denoising ends, but existing methods cannot jointly stop early and recover earlier better states.
tAg9zeNc4T.method: Trajectory-MBR is a training-free decoding wrapper that reuses denoiser outputs to form complete candidate responses and applies trajectory-score-weighted minimum Bayes risk selection over a sliding window. Decoding halts and returns the selected historical or current candidate once minimum weighted risk drops below a threshold.
tAg9zeNc4T.key_idea: Compute trajectory-score-weighted minimum Bayes risk over a sliding window of denoiser outputs to jointly trigger early stopping and select the best intermediate response.
tAg9zeNc4T.evidence: Evaluated across language and multimodal benchmarks including HumanEval, HotpotQA, MME, and LSHT, supported by approximation and offline-improvement bounds.
tAg9zeNc4T.claimed_gains: Maintains or improves average response quality with average denoiser-evaluation speedups up to 3.76x, and a token-level extension achieves a 12.34x step-based speedup on HumanEval.
tAg9zeNc4T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the training-free design and the clear distinction between deciding when to stop and which historical checkpoint to return.
tAg9zeNc4T.main_concern: Reviewers cite heavy sensitivity to per-task hyperparameters tuned on evaluation data, missing core ablations, unclear wall-clock speedups, and degraded full-decoding baselines.

gZeJYR2o54.one_liner: Predicts future visual embeddings inside a frozen video-language model space so negative cosine similarity with language goals drives robot planning.
gZeJYR2o54.problem: Latent world models like DINO-WM and LeWM require goal images that are hard to supply in advance for new robotic tasks.
gZeJYR2o54.method: Grounded World Model (GWM) trains a latent dynamics predictor on offline, task-agnostic video-action pairs without language labels to forecast futures in a pretrained video-language embedding space. At test time, it ranks candidate action sequences by the negative cosine similarity between the predicted future embedding and the frozen language-goal embedding.
gZeJYR2o54.key_idea: Roll out candidate actions in a frozen video-language embedding space and score plans via negative cosine similarity to the text goal.
gZeJYR2o54.evidence: Evaluated in simulation on WISER (288 tasks) and IsaacSim (14 tasks), on a real Franka arm (60 pick-and-place sub-tasks), and zero-shot on xArm6.
gZeJYR2o54.claimed_gains: Solves 87% of 288 WISER tasks versus 22% average for ten fine-tuned VLAs, completes 70/70 IsaacSim trials versus 37/70 for pi0.5, and completes 55/60 real Franka pick-and-place sub-tasks.
gZeJYR2o54.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple, scalable reuse of pretrained video-language embeddings for zero-shot language-goal planning without extra language-alignment training.
gZeJYR2o54.main_concern: Reviewers point out unfair comparisons because GWM only ranks externally provided candidate trajectories (always including a valid option) rather than generating actions like VLAs, and note evaluation flaws and restriction to simple pick-and-place tasks.

kx17FJ7sj6.one_liner: Scores autonomous-driving trajectory candidates using a trajectory-conditioned JEPA predictor supervised by simulator outcomes and anchored to logged futures.
kx17FJ7sj6.problem: Autonomous driving scorers must evaluate unexecuted candidate trajectories for which driving logs provide no observed future scenes.
kx17FJ7sj6.method: World4Scorer passes every candidate trajectory through a shared trajectory-conditioned JEPA-style predictor to produce latent future states and read out trajectory scores. Simulator outcome labels supervise all candidates (augmented by a scene-matched low-scoring bank), observed logged futures anchor the shared parameters during training only, and inertial re-ranking stabilizes consecutive frame selections.
kx17FJ7sj6.key_idea: Train one shared trajectory-conditioned JEPA predictor with simulator outcome labels on all candidates while anchoring parameters to logged real futures during training only.
kx17FJ7sj6.evidence: Evaluated on NAVSIM-v1, NAVSIM-v2, and Bench2Drive using a ViT-S backbone, along with ablation studies.
kx17FJ7sj6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers note strong NAVSIM and Bench2Drive results with a lightweight inference-efficient design that drops future prediction at test time.
kx17FJ7sj6.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty relative to existing outcome-supervised trajectory scorers (Hydra-MDP, GTRS, SafeDrive), note reliance on non-reactive simulator rules, and criticize unclear presentation.

oga3jQcKxf.one_liner: Personalizes frozen text-to-image diffusion models using trigger-indexed external memory injected as gated multi-layer residuals.
oga3jQcKxf.problem: Text-to-image personalization via token embeddings misses subject details, LoRA adapters interfere during composition, and reference-conditioned encoders require backbone-specific large-scale pretraining.
oga3jQcKxf.method: V-Engram learns compact subject memories from a few reference images, indexes them by text triggers, and injects matched entries as gated residuals into selected layers of frozen text encoders and the denoiser, leaving unmatched prompts untouched.
oga3jQcKxf.key_idea: Retrieves trigger-indexed external subject memories and injects them as gated residuals into frozen text-encoder and denoiser layers only when prompts match.
oga3jQcKxf.evidence: Evaluated on Stable Diffusion 3.5 against DreamBooth-LoRA and TI-style baselines, with additional separately trained memory experiments on Stable Diffusion 1.5 and FLUX.1-dev.
oga3jQcKxf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating concept memories from the frozen backbone for prompt-selective modular activation is clean and shows promising subject identity preservation.
oga3jQcKxf.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited baseline comparisons (missing recent customization and training-free reference-image methods) and narrow evaluation centered mainly on SD3.5.

UNnZrfbY9n.one_liner: Compresses full video history into projected spatiotemporal memory tokens for DiT self-attention with dual-pointer denoising.
UNnZrfbY9n.problem: Long-horizon video generation faces growing token-sequence costs when retaining full history, while restricting or compressing context drops information needed for distant recall and suffers autoregressive temporal drift.
UNnZrfbY9n.method: ReCam groups local spatiotemporal blocks of historical latents into vectors projected directly into a Diffusion Transformer's hidden space for native self-attention, and applies dual-pointer denoising with separate noise schedules for recent context and target frames.
UNnZrfbY9n.key_idea: Projects spatiotemporal blocks of full historical latents into DiT hidden-space memory tokens read via native self-attention, paired with dual-pointer denoising noise schedules.
UNnZrfbY9n.evidence: Evaluated on VBench-Long, R2M-Bench static-scene revisitation, and off-screen subject reappearance (present vs. initially absent splits) using Wan2.2-I2V-A14B.
UNnZrfbY9n.claimed_gains: Achieves 80.1 overall score on VBench-Long and 4.09 clothing consistency on off-screen subject reappearance versus 3.03 for the best baseline.
UNnZrfbY9n.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple end-to-end memory token design and the initially-absent subject reappearance evaluation that directly tests mid-history recall.
UNnZrfbY9n.main_concern: Reviewers note that experiments lack controlled same-backbone/same-data comparisons isolating the memory mechanism, exclude failed reappearances from consistency scores, and show limited novelty over FramePack.

hUk9yy8zSU.one_liner: Bakes view-dependent specular appearance onto meshes using order-free on-manifold 2D Gaussian disks, environment maps, and a FastKAN decoder.
hUk9yy8zSU.problem: Standard baked mesh textures cannot represent sharp view-dependent reflections, while binding splats to mesh faces suffers from coplanar compositing-order instability and per-primitive angular band limits.
hUk9yy8zSU.method: Automatic Neural Baking anchors 2D Gaussian disks directly to mesh faces blended via an order-free partition of unity, and factors view dependence out of individual primitives into a shared regional environment map decoded by a FastKAN network within a rasterization pipeline.
hUk9yy8zSU.key_idea: Blends mesh-anchored 2D Gaussian feature disks via an order-free partition of unity and factors view dependence into a shared environment map with a FastKAN decoder.
hUk9yy8zSU.evidence: Theoretical obstruction proofs plus specular novel-view synthesis benchmarks including Shiny-Blender and RTX 4090 rendering-speed tests against 2DGS.
hUk9yy8zSU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method produces sharp real-time specular reflections directly on known meshes without UV atlases or primitive sorting.
hUk9yy8zSU.main_concern: Reviewers find methodological novelty limited relative to combining known components, note missing controls (such as split-sum shading or same-decoder baselines), and say ablations do not isolate the surface field from the KAN decoder and environment maps.

k95GtmeHk2.one_liner: Enhances monocular 3D detector denoising training using dynamic class visual prototypes for difficulty modulation and feature injection.
k95GtmeHk2.problem: Denoising-based monocular 3D object detectors rely mainly on geometric guidance and distribution modeling, underexploiting instance-level visual cues on occluded, truncated, or distant objects.
k95GtmeHk2.method: ProtoDN maintains a dynamic class-specific visual prototype memory during training and adds Geometry-Visual Joint Difficulty Modeling to modulate denoising perturbations alongside Prototype-Guided Visual Enhancement to inject prototype appearance priors into denoising queries.
k95GtmeHk2.key_idea: Uses a training-only dynamic visual prototype memory to jointly estimate geometric-visual instance difficulty for denoising noise scaling and inject appearance priors into queries.
k95GtmeHk2.evidence: Evaluated on the KITTI monocular 3D object detection benchmark.
k95GtmeHk2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers note that the paper is clearly written, uses prototypes only during training with zero inference overhead, and improves KITTI Hard AP3D.
k95GtmeHk2.main_concern: Reviewers question limited incremental novelty over prior geometry-guided denoising and prototype methods, untested long-range datasets beyond KITTI, and unverified perturbation-scaling mechanisms.

Nslkylt38K.one_liner: Places agent skill edits at hierarchy roots only when paired subtree execution shows zero regressions, otherwise localizing to leaves.
Nslkylt38K.problem: In hierarchical self-evolving agent skill libraries, local leaf edits fail to transfer while root edits can silently break sibling tasks undetected by proposing-task or subtree-mean admission rules.
Nslkylt38K.method: ScopeEvo formulates root evolution as edit placement via a subtree gate: a candidate edit is promoted to the root only if no evaluated descendant regresses under paired execution, otherwise it is rewritten and validated in the leaves of helped descendants or discarded, using pluggable leaf editors and release recursion.
Nslkylt38K.key_idea: Gates root-skill promotion on zero descendant regressions under paired execution, relocating beneficial but conflicting edits into validated leaf skills.
Nslkylt38K.evidence: Evaluated programmatically (exact match, ANLS, verifiers) on SkillsBench (atop CoEvoSkills), SearchQA, and DocVQA, plus theoretical analysis of subtree validation.
Nslkylt38K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clear framing of edit-scope placement, programmatic evaluation without LLM judges, and three-way promote/localize/discard gating with leaf validation.
Nslkylt38K.main_concern: Reviewers criticize weak empirical isolation and small sample sizes—citing missing resource-matched CoEvoSkills baselines, zero accepted root edits in leaf-first QA, and unreported end-to-end token costs.
